51	## 1. System Overview & Mental Model
52	
53	deadreckon is a Rust 2024 CLI harness whose default flow is **unattended long-running coding tasks**: `deadreckon run <goal>` creates durable run state, picks a BYOK provider route, executes turns inside a platform-native sandbox, writes spend/provenance/trace records after every turn, and exits only when the LLM declares done, a budget caps the run, or the operator kills it. The CLI is the user-facing layer; `deadreckon-runtime` owns orchestration across providers, sandboxes, docs, and promotion; `deadreckon-core` owns deterministic primitives and durable schemas.
54	
55	```
56	┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
57	│ USER                                                                      │
58	│ deadreckon run "make a hello-world Rust binary" --max-spend 5             │
59	└────────────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────────────┘
60	                                 │
61	┌────────────────────────────────▼──────────────────────────────────────────┐
62	│ CLI LAYER (crates/deadreckon)                                             │
63	│   cli.rs       clap parser definitions                                    │
64	│   main.rs      command handlers, ratatui rendering, post-run summary       │
65	└────────────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────────────┘
66	                                 │ create_run → acquire_lock → runtime loop
67	                                 ▼
68	┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
69	│ RUNTIME ORCHESTRATION (crates/deadreckon-runtime)                         │
70	│                                                                           │
71	│  turn_loop.rs  provider turns, sandboxed tool dispatch, cancellation,      │
72	│                acceptance gate invocation, promotion orchestration         │
73	│  polish.rs     optional end-of-run doc polish via a doc-provider           │
74	└──┬──────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────┬────────────────┘
75	   │ durable primitives       │ ProviderRouter::complete  │ run_sandbox
76	   ▼                          ▼                          ▼
77	┌──────────────────────────┐  ┌──────────────────────┐  ┌──────────────────────┐
78	│ CORE LIBRARY             │  │ PROVIDERS            │  │ SANDBOX              │
79	│ state, paths, locks      │  │ HTTP: anthropic,     │  │ sandbox-exec, bwrap, │
80	│ artifacts, docs, events  │  │ openai, compatible   │  │ docker, none, auto   │
81	│ gate, promotion, chains  │  │ CLI: claude, codex   │  │ policy, PID/cancel   │
82	│ adapter-free schemas     │  │ TEST: smoke          │  │ doctor checks        │
83	└────────────┬─────────────┘  └──────────┬───────────┘  └──────────┬───────────┘
84	             │                           │                         │
85	             └───────────────────────────┴─────────────┬───────────┘
86	                                                       ▼
87	┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
88	│ RUNTIME STATE (~/.deadreckon/)                                            │
89	│ runstate/<scope>/runs/<run-id>, library/<scope>/<run-id>, locks, config   │
90	└───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
91	```
92	
93	Why this shape works:
94	
95	- **The CLI is thin.** It parses args, sets up state, hands off to `deadreckon-runtime`, and prints summaries. Durable schemas and atomic file operations live in `deadreckon-core`.
96	- **State is on disk before every meaningful change.** `state.json` is atomic-written via temp+rename after every phase transition, snapshot, spend record, and tool call.
97	- **The agent cannot mark its own gate.** `dr-gate` is a separate binary that signs an acceptance marker against a nonce only it can read; the deadreckon binary refuses to mark a run `Completed` without that signed marker.
98	- **Sandboxes are platform-native.** macOS uses Seatbelt; Linux uses Bubblewrap; Docker is opt-in. No daemon, no `bollard`, no Lima.
99	- **BYOK extends to subscriptions.** Subscription-bearing users drive deadreckon by routing turns through their local `claude` or `codex` CLIs; no API key required.

202	
203	## 3. The Two-Layer Architecture
204	
205	deadreckon mirrors the Printing Press split (AS-BUILT §3):
206	
207	| Layer | Owns | Lives in | Language |
208	|---|---|---|---|
209	| **Skill** | Agent-facing prose, judgment, prompt frame | `skills/default-coding/SKILL.md` | Markdown |
210	| **Binary** | State, locks, sandboxes, providers, gates | `crates/deadreckon*` | Rust |
211	
212	The skill is invoked indirectly: it sits at the path recorded in `state.skill_path` and is read into the prompt frame by `build_prompt` in `crates/deadreckon-runtime/src/turn_loop.rs`. The binary never reaches into skill internals. New skills can be added under `skills/<name>/SKILL.md` and selected with `deadreckon run --skill <name>`.
213	
214	This split lets each side do what it's good at:
215	
216	- The Rust binary enforces invariants — locks, atomic file ops, signed acceptance markers, sandboxed subprocesses.
217	- The Markdown skill makes judgment calls — what to ask the LLM for, what tool sequence to prefer, when to declare done.
218

222	
223	### 4.1 `PipelineState`
224	
225	`crates/deadreckon-core/src/state.rs:77-110`:
226	
227	```rust
228	pub struct PipelineState {
229	    pub version: u32,                       // STATE_VERSION = 1 (line 15)
230	    pub goal: String,
231	    pub task_key: String,

234	    pub status: RunStatus,

237	    pub updated_at: DateTime<Utc>,
238	    pub cwd: PathBuf,

241	    pub skill_name: String,

247	    pub total_spend_usd: f64,

249	    pub turn: u32,
250	    pub pause_reason: Option<String>,
251	    pub failure_reason: Option<String>,
252	    pub child_pids: Vec<u32>,
253	    pub killed_at: Option<DateTime<Utc>>,
254	    pub promoted_library_dir: Option<PathBuf>,
255	    pub phases: Vec<PhaseState>,
256	}
257	```
258	
259	### 4.2 Status and phase enums
260	
261	`state.rs:17-26`:
262	
263	```rust
264	pub enum RunStatus {
265	    Pending, Planned, Executing, Completed, Failed, Killed,
266	}
267	```
268	
269	`state.rs:42-75`:
270	
271	```rust
272	pub struct PhaseId(pub u16);
273	
274	pub struct PhaseState {
275	    pub id: PhaseId,
276	    pub name: String,
277	    pub status: PhaseStatus,    // Pending | Planned | Executing | Completed | Failed
278	    pub plan_path: Option<PathBuf>,
279	    pub updated_at: DateTime<Utc>,
280	}
281	```
282	
283	### 4.3 Phase numbering (gap-numbered)
284	
285	`state.rs:233-254` initializes seven phases for every new run:
286	
287	| `PhaseId` | name | role |
288	|---|---|---|
289	| 0 | `init` | skill load, run-id mint, working-dir create |
290	| 10 | `plan` | reserved; currently a no-op |
291	| 20 | `provider` | router built from config, fallback chain resolved |
292	| 30 | `sandbox` | sandbox backend selected, profile prepared |
293	| 40 | `execute` | the turn loop runs here; sets `RunStatus::Executing` |
294	| 50 | `verify` | post-loop verification (currently runs `dr-gate`) |
295	| 60 | `complete` | acceptance marker validated, promotion atomic-swaps, `RunStatus::Completed` |
296	
297	The gap-numbering (0, 10, 20 …) leaves room for future phases (e.g., 15, 25, 55) without re-writing on-disk state.
298	
299	### 4.4 Status transitions
300	
301	`state.rs:150-169` is the only function that mutates `PipelineState.status`:
302	
303	```rust
304	pub fn set_phase_status(&mut self, id: PhaseId, status: PhaseStatus) -> Result<()> {
305	    let now = Utc::now();
306	    let phase = self.phases.iter_mut().find(|phase| phase.id == id)
307	        .ok_or_else(|| DeadreckonError::NotFound(format!("phase {}", id.0)))?;
308	    phase.status = status;
309	    phase.updated_at = now;
310	    self.current_phase_id = id;
311	    self.updated_at = now;
312	    self.status = match status {
313	        PhaseStatus::Executing => RunStatus::Executing,
314	        PhaseStatus::Failed => RunStatus::Failed,
315	        PhaseStatus::Completed if id == PhaseId(60) => RunStatus::Completed,
316	        PhaseStatus::Planned => RunStatus::Planned,
317	        PhaseStatus::Pending | PhaseStatus::Completed => self.status,
318	    };
319	    Ok(())
320	}
321	```
322	
323	Key rule: `RunStatus::Completed` is reachable **only** through `Phase(60).Completed`, which the loop refuses to set without `validate_acceptance_marker()` passing (§13).
324	
325	### 4.5 Atomic persistence
326	
327	`state.rs:353-373`:
328	
329	```rust
330	pub(crate) fn atomic_write_json<T: Serialize>(path: &Path, value: &T) -> Result<()> {
331	    let parent = path.parent().ok_or_else(...)?;
332	    fs::create_dir_all(parent).with_path(parent)?;
333	    let mut temp = NamedTempFile::new_in(parent).with_path(parent)?;
334	    serde_json::to_writer_pretty(&mut temp, value).with_json_path(path)?;
335	    temp.write_all(b"\n").with_path(path)?;
336	    temp.as_file_mut().sync_all().with_path(path)?;   // fsync before rename
337	    persist_temp(temp, path)
338	}
339	```
340	
341	Every state-changing function ends with `save_state(state)?`. Crashes never leave a half-written `state.json`.
342	
343	JSONL files (`spend.jsonl`, `traces.jsonl`, `provenance.jsonl`, `events.jsonl`) use `append_json_line` (`state.rs:375-388`): open in append mode, write line + newline, `sync_all`.
344	
345	### 4.6 Schema versioning
346	
347	`STATE_VERSION = 1` (`state.rs:15`) gates future migrations. `load_state` rejects unknown versions; migrations would land here.
348

394	│               │   └── turn-<N>/  # per-turn full working-tree copy
395	│               ├── turns/
396	│               │   └── turn-<N>/  # provider stdout, prompt.md
397	│               ├── proofs/
398	│               │   ├── turn-acceptance.json       # AcceptanceMarker
399	│               │   └── acceptance-progress.jsonl  # streaming AcceptanceProgressEntry
400	│               ├── gate/
401	│               │   └── nonce      # uuid; only dr-gate can read for signing
402	│               ├── child-pids/
403	│               │   └── *.pid      # per-subprocess PID files
404	│               ├── sandbox/       # per-run Seatbelt profile (if mac) or bwrap args
405	│               ├── traces.jsonl
406	│               ├── provenance.jsonl
407	│               ├── spend.jsonl
408	│               ├── events.jsonl
409	│               ├── history.json   # narrative tool-call summaries
410	│               └── acceptance.yaml   # optional spec for dr-gate
411	├── locks/
412	│   └── <scope>--<task_key>.lock   # one lock per task
413	└── library/
414	    └── <scope>/
415	        └── <run_id>/
416	            ├── manifest.json      # PromotionManifest
417	            └── ...                # promoted working tree
418	```
419	
420	The split between `runstate/` (mutable working state) and `library/` (durable promoted artifacts) is deliberate: `runstate/` is per-scope and ephemeral; `library/` is global and intended to outlive cleanup. The `state.working_dir` field starts pointing at `runstate/.../working/` and is rewritten to `library/<scope>/<run_id>/` after promotion.

422	### 5.3 Path derivation
423	
424	`crates/deadreckon-core/src/paths.rs:9-65` exposes:
425	
426	```rust
427	impl DeadreckonPaths {
428	    pub fn home(&self) -> &Path                              // ~/.deadreckon (or DEADRECKON_HOME)
429	    pub fn config_path(&self) -> PathBuf                     // home/config.toml
430	    pub fn runstate_dir(&self) -> PathBuf                    // home/runstate
431	    pub fn scope_root(&self, scope: &str) -> PathBuf
432	    pub fn current_pointer_path(&self, scope, task_key) -> PathBuf
433	    pub fn run_root(&self, scope, run_id) -> PathBuf
434	    pub fn locks_dir(&self) -> PathBuf                       // home/locks
435	    pub fn library_dir(&self, scope, run_id) -> PathBuf
436	}
437	```
438	
439	Scope (`paths.rs:67-86`) derives from `DEADRECKON_SCOPE_ROOT` env var, or the nearest `.git` root, or `cwd`. The literal scope string is `"<sanitized-basename>-<fnv1a32-hex>"` of the canonical path — unique per worktree, stable per checkout.
440	
441	Task key (`paths.rs:88-99`) is `"<slug-of-goal>-<fnv1a32-hex-of-goal>"` (slug capped at 48 chars). Two runs with the same goal share a task key (and a lock).
442	
443	---
444	
445	## 6. Run Lifecycle & Phase Machine
446	
447	Sequence for a typical `deadreckon run` invocation:
448	
449	```
450	main.rs run_command()
451	  ↓
452	  paths = DeadreckonPaths::discover()
453	  ↓
454	  state = create_run(paths, RunOptions{...})       # state.rs:178-231
455	  │   ├── mint run_id (uuid simple form)
456	  │   ├── derive scope (paths.rs:67) and task_key (paths.rs:88)
457	  │   ├── create run_root/working/snapshots/proofs/gate/turns
458	  │   ├── write gate/nonce (uuid)
459	  │   ├── initialize 7 phases (state.rs:233-254)
460	  │   ├── write CurrentRunPointer
461	  │   └── save_state()
462	  ↓
463	  lock = acquire_lock(paths, task_key, run_id, scope, "run", 30min)
464	  │   └── lock.rs:89-158
465	  ↓
466	  state.child_pids = vec![cli_pid]; save_state()
467	  ↓
468	  set_phase_status(20, Completed); save_state()   # provider built
469	  set_phase_status(30, Completed); save_state()   # sandbox resolved
470	  ↓
471	  outcome = run_turn_loop(state, router, RunLoopConfig{...})
472	  ↓
473	  state.child_pids.clear(); save_state()
474	  lock.release()
475	  ↓
476	  match outcome { Done | PausedAtCap | Killed | Failed }
477	  print_run_locations(state)
478	```
479	
480	`Completed` is only reached if the turn loop emits `RunLoopOutcome::Done`, which itself requires:
481	
482	1. The loop saw `Action::Done` (or a CLI sub-agent finished with file changes), **and**
483	2. `acceptance_gate_passed_or_record_failure(state, ...)` returned `true` after invoking `dr-gate` and validating the signed marker (`turn_loop.rs:1298`). Gate failures are non-terminal: the helper logs them and returns `false`, letting the loop continue until the gate passes or the turn budget is exhausted (§13.6), **and**
484	3. `promote_if_ready(state)` swapped `working/` → `library/<scope>/<run_id>/`, **and**
485	4. `set_phase_status(PhaseId(60), Completed)` ran (which is the only path to `RunStatus::Completed`).
486	
487	If gate failures accumulate during a run, `state.failure_reason` accumulates a chained record (e.g. `"acceptance failed after turn 3: ...; acceptance failed after turn 5: ...; max turn budget exhausted"`).
488	
489	---
490	
491	## 7. Locks, Heartbeats, Crash Recovery
492	
493	### 7.1 `LockState`
494	
495	`crates/deadreckon-core/src/lock.rs:15-24`:
496	
497	```rust
498	pub struct LockState {
499	    pub task_key: String,
500	    pub run_id: String,
501	    pub scope: String,
502	    pub phase: String,
503	    pub pid: u32,
504	    pub acquired_at: DateTime<Utc>,
505	    pub updated_at: DateTime<Utc>,
506	}
507	```
508	
509	Lock file lives at `~/.deadreckon/locks/<scope>--<task_key>.lock` (`lock.rs:86`).
510	
511	### 7.2 Acquisition
512	
513	`lock.rs:89-158`:
514	
515	1. Create the `.lock` file.
516	2. `fs2::FileExt::try_lock_exclusive` for OS-level advisory lock.
517	3. If `EWOULDBLOCK`, read existing `LockState` from disk. If owner matches **or** lock is stale, proceed. Otherwise refuse.
518	4. Stale detection: `acquired_at` age > `DEFAULT_STALE_AFTER` (30 min, `lock.rs:13`) **or** `pid_is_alive(pid)` returns false. PID liveness is `nix::sys::signal::kill(pid, 0)` (`lock.rs:235-245`): `ESRCH` → dead, anything else → alive.
519	5. Write the new `LockState` to disk.
520	6. Return a `LockGuard` that releases on drop.
521	
522	### 7.3 Heartbeat
523	
524	`lock.rs:47-51`:
525	
526	```rust
527	pub fn heartbeat(&mut self, phase: impl Into<String>) -> Result<()> {
528	    self.state.phase = phase.into();
529	    self.state.updated_at = Utc::now();
530	    write_lock_state_to_file(&mut self.file, &self.path, &self.state)
531	}
532	```
533	
534	Updates `updated_at` to keep stale-detection at bay. Callers in the turn loop tag the current sub-phase (e.g., `"executing-turn-3"`).
535	
536	### 7.4 Release
537	
538	`lock.rs:53-76`. Drops the file lock, deletes the lock file, gracefully handles `NotFound`.
539	
540	### 7.5 Crash recovery
541	
542	If the process holding the lock dies, the lock file persists but `pid_is_alive(pid)` will return false. The next caller sees the stale state and reclaims it. The new caller writes its own PID; previous run state survives intact in `runstate/<scope>/runs/<dead_run_id>/`.
543	
544	---
545	
546	## 8. Atomic Promotion & the Library
547	
548	### 8.1 `PromotionManifest`
549	
550	`crates/deadreckon-core/src/promotion.rs:14-23`:
551	
552	```rust
553	pub struct PromotionManifest {
554	    pub schema_version: u32,
555	    pub run_id: String,
556	    pub scope: String,
557	    pub goal: String,
558	    pub promoted_at: DateTime<Utc>,
559	    pub source_working_dir: PathBuf,
560	    pub provenance_hash: String,   // hash of provenance.jsonl bytes
561	}
562	```
563	
564	### 8.2 Promotion flow
565	
566	`promotion.rs:25-63`:
567	
568	1. **Guard.** `validate_acceptance_marker(state)?` — refuses if marker missing / wrong run_id / unsigned.
569	2. **Recovery.** `recover_promotion()` — idempotent if a previous attempt half-completed (§8.4).
570	3. **Idempotency check.** If `library/<scope>/<run_id>/manifest.json` already exists, update state and return — no work to do.
571	4. **Staging.** Create `library/<scope>/.{run_id}.promoting/` (parent dir created if needed).
572	5. **Move.** `fs::rename(working_dir, staging)` — atomic on same filesystem.
573	6. **Manifest.** Write `manifest.json` inside staging.
574	7. **Final rename.** `fs::rename(staging, library/<scope>/<run_id>/)` — atomic.
575	8. **State update.** `state.working_dir = library_dir`; `state.promoted_library_dir = Some(library_dir)`; `save_state()`.
576	
577	### 8.3 Where promotion happens
578	
579	In `crates/deadreckon-runtime/src/turn_loop.rs`, **before** `set_phase_status(PhaseId(60), Completed)`. If promotion fails, the run never reaches `Completed`. The `working/` directory is the source of truth until promotion; after promotion, the library copy is canonical and `working/` is gone.
580	
581	### 8.4 Crash recovery between rename steps
582	
583	`promotion.rs:65-84` handles the half-completed states:
584	
585	- If `staging` exists and final dir doesn't: complete the rename.
586	- If both exist: the final rename happened but didn't atomically remove staging; clean up staging.
587	- If final dir exists but its `manifest.json` is missing: write the manifest.
588	
589	This makes promotion crash-safe across a `kill -9` between the two renames.
590	
591	---
592	
593	## 9. The Turn Loop
594	
595	The load-bearing function lives in `/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon-runtime/src/turn_loop.rs`.
596	
597	### 9.1 `RunLoopConfig`
598	
599	`crates/deadreckon-runtime/src/turn_loop.rs` defines:
600	
601	```rust
602	pub struct RunLoopConfig {
603	    pub provider: Option<String>,
604	    pub max_spend_usd: Option<f64>,
605	    pub max_wall_seconds: Option<f64>,
606	    pub sandbox_backend: SandboxBackend,
607	    pub max_turns: u32,             // hard cap, currently 12
608	    pub from_turn: Option<u32>,     // resume override
609	    pub event_sender: Option<broadcast::Sender<RunEvent>>,
610	    pub cancellation_token: Option<CancellationToken>,
611	}
612	```
613	
614	### 9.2 Top-level signature
615	
616	The top-level signature is:
617	
618	```rust
619	pub async fn run_turn_loop(
620	    state: &mut PipelineState,
621	    router: &ProviderRouter,
622	    config: RunLoopConfig,
623	) -> Result<RunLoopOutcome>
624	```
625	
626	### 9.3 Loop body (paraphrased; see `crates/deadreckon-runtime/src/turn_loop.rs`)
627	
628	```text
629	load_or_reconstruct_history()      # lines 69, 550-631
630	set Phase(40)=Executing            # line 70
631	save_state(); save_history()       # line 71
632	
633	for turn in (state.turn+1)..=max_turns:
634	    if cancelled or status=Killed:
635	        return Killed
636	    emit TurnStarted event
637	    snapshot_working(turn-1)        # capture pre-turn state
638	    prompt = build_prompt(state, history) [or build_cli_subagent_prompt]
639	    request = ProviderRequest{
640	        prompt, max_output_tokens=2048, cwd, output_path, sandbox_backend,
641	        pid_file=run_root/child-pids/provider-turn-N.pid,
642	        cancellation_token=turn_token,
643	    }
644	    response = router.complete(&request).await
645	    append_trace(llm.complete, latency, response.trace)
646	    state.total_spend_usd += response.spend.cost_usd
647	    state.total_wall_seconds += response.spend.wall_time_seconds
648	    append_spend(...)
649	    if max_spend exceeded: return PausedAtCap
650	    if subscription and max_wall_seconds exceeded: return PausedAtCap
651	
652	    if response is cli_subagent:
653	        changed = changed_files_since_snapshot(turn-1)
654	        if changed.is_empty: return Failed
655	        snapshot_working(turn)
656	        append_trace(tool.cli_subagent, files=changed)
657	        append_provenance_for_files(turn, tool_call_id, model, changed)
658	        run_acceptance_gate(state)        # dr-gate
659	        validate_acceptance_marker(state) # signed?
660	        promote_if_ready(state)           # working → library
661	        set Phase(60)=Completed
662	        return Done
663	
664	    parse Action from response.content (serde tag="action"):
665	        Bash { tool_call_id, command } =>
666	            run_sandbox(SandboxSpec{
667	                program=sh, args=[-lc, command], cwd=working_dir,
668	                pid_file, cancellation_token=turn_token.child_token(),
669	                read_allowlist=[working_dir],
670	                allow_network=false,
671	            }).await
672	            append_trace(tool.bash, stdout, stderr, status)
673	            snapshot_working(turn); append_provenance(turn, changed_files)
674	            history.push("tool {id} result: status={...}")
675	        WriteFile { tool_call_id, path, content } =>
676	            safe_working_path(path); write_file
677	            append_trace(tool.write_file); snapshot_working(turn)
678	            append_provenance(turn, [path])
679	            history.push("tool {id} result: wrote file")
680	        Done { summary } =>
681	            run_acceptance_gate; validate_marker; promote_if_ready
682	            set Phase(60)=Completed
683	            return Done
684	
685	    state.turn = turn; save_history(); save_state()
686	
687	# loop exited via max_turns
688	state.failure_reason = Some("max turn budget exhausted")
689	set Phase(40)=Failed; save_state()
690	return Failed
691	```
692	
693	### 9.4 Action enum
694	
695	Inline in `crates/deadreckon-runtime/src/turn_loop.rs` (paraphrased):
696	
697	```rust
698	#[derive(Debug, Deserialize)]
699	#[serde(tag = "action", rename_all = "snake_case")]
700	enum Action {
701	    Bash { tool_call_id: String, command: String },
702	    WriteFile { tool_call_id: String, path: PathBuf, content: String },
703	    Done { summary: Option<String> },
704	}
705	```
706	
707	Providers return JSON; the loop parses one action per turn. The CLI sub-agent path is detected by `response.trace["kind"] == "cli_subagent"` before action parsing — those providers do their own tool calls inside the subprocess and return a narrative, not an action JSON.
708	
709	### 9.5 No smoke fallback in the default path
710	
711	`grep -r "coding_turn_script\|hardcoded_smoke" /Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/` returns empty. 712	
713	### 9.6 Error handling
714	
715	The loop does **not** retry on errors:
716	
717	- Provider error → propagates and the run fails.
718	- Tool-call non-zero exit → result fed back to history, next turn's prompt sees the failure; the model decides whether to retry.
719	- Acceptance failure → run fails; no auto-retry.

4	
5	# deadreckon
6	
7	**A harness around the agent CLI you already use, so you can actually walk away.**
8	
9	Claude Code, Codex, Cursor CLI, and the rest are good at writing code. They are not built to run unattended for hours and tell you, honestly, whether the work got done. deadreckon is.
10	
11	You bring the agent CLI you already trust. You tell deadreckon what "done" looks like in plain English. It runs the work in an isolated sandbox, saves every turn, and uses a separate watchdog process to decide when the run is actually finished: a watchdog the agent cannot fool.
12	
13	```bash
14	deadreckon def-done "users can sign up, log in, and save a drawing"
15	deadreckon run "build the app"
16	# walk away, attach later from any terminal
17	deadreckon attach latest
18	```
19	
20	> [!TIP]
21	> deadreckon is alpha software. The core lifecycle (isolated runs, signed gates, durable state, undo, docs, and apply) is implemented and tested, but expect rough edges and breaking changes.
22	
23	## How it works
24	
25	1. **You write "done" in plain English.** deadreckon compiles it into executable checks: tests that must pass, files that must exist, scripts that must succeed.
26	2. **The agent runs in an isolated worktree**, inside a sandbox. Your real checkout is never touched.
27	3. **Every turn is saved** (state, spend, traces, file provenance, snapshots) so you can attach, kill, resume, undo, or audit any moment.
28	4. **A separate watchdog process (`dr-gate`) decides when the work is done.** It holds a secret the agent process cannot read, and signs the result with that secret. The agent cannot forge the signature, so it cannot mark its own work as accepted.
29	5. **If the checks fail, the loop keeps going.** The agent gets another turn. When the watchdog finally signs off for real, the run is atomically promoted to a reviewable artifact: narrative, decisions, file provenance, full audit trail.
30	
31	The loop is the product. The agent CLI does the coding. deadreckon decides when "done" actually means done.
32	
33	## Why this matters
34	
35	- **You can leave a long run going and trust the result.** The agent can't lie its way out of the gate.
36	- **Use whichever agent CLI you prefer.** Claude Code, Codex, Cursor CLI, or direct Anthropic / OpenAI API: deadreckon supervises any of them.
37	- **You get an auditable artifact, not a chat transcript.** Narrative, decisions, file lineage, spend, traces, all on disk.
38	- **If anything dies (terminal, network, the model) the run survives.** Attach from a new terminal, resume from any turn, undo a bad step.
39	
40	## Why "deadreckon"?
41	
42	Dead reckoning is navigation without perfect visibility: track every move so you know where you are now. Unattended agents are the same problem: long task, partial context, the terminal may be gone when you look back. The name is the contract: don't trust the final answer, navigate by evidence.
43	
44	The questions deadreckon is built to answer:
45	
46	- Where did the agent run, and what did it spend?
47	- Can I attach after closing my laptop?
48	- Can I undo turn 7 without rolling back the whole project?
49	- Can I prove the agent did not mark its own work as accepted?
50	
51	## Features
52	
53	### Your Checkout Is Never Touched (Isolated Worktrees By Default)
54	
55	In a git repo, `deadreckon run` creates a separate `git worktree` on a `dr/...` branch under `~/.deadreckon/worktrees/`. Your checkout is left untouched until you explicitly run:
56	
57	```bash
58	deadreckon apply <run-id>
59	```
60	
61	Run ids accept unique prefixes, and most commands also accept `latest` for the
62	newest run in the current project.
63	
64	You can also run in copy mode, fresh mode, or explicit in-place mode:
65	
66	```bash
67	deadreckon run "goal" --from .
68	deadreckon run "goal" --fresh
69	deadreckon run "goal" --in-place --i-know-its-a-lot
70	```
71	
72	### Use The Agent CLI You Already Trust
73	
74	Route turns through whichever provider you prefer:
75	
76	- **Local CLIs** (subscription): `cli:claude-code`, `cli:codex`
77	- **Direct APIs** (BYOK): `anthropic`, `openai`, OpenAI-compatible endpoints
78	- **Smoke** (keyless): `--smoke` for local verification
79	
80	The CLI does the coding; deadreckon owns the run boundary around it.
81	
82	### Crash-Proof: Every Turn Is Saved To Disk
83	
84	Every turn writes state, traces, spend, file provenance, and a working-directory snapshot under `~/.deadreckon/runstate/`. If the terminal dies, attach from another. If the run itself crashes, resume from the last completed turn.
85	
86	### Walk Away, Attach From Any Terminal
87	
88	```bash
89	deadreckon attach latest
90	```
91	
92	The TUI shows live status, current step, spend, recent file edits, and provider activity. Completed runs render `RUN-NARRATIVE.md` inline. Press `Ctrl-D` to detach without killing the run.
93	
94	For longer or multi-agent work, use `deadreckon attach latest --view narrative` for a cited operator overview with an evidence-backed visual map. Raw activity stays one key away with `n`; `v` cycles architecture, agent, file, and evidence views.
95	
96	Provider-backed narrative refresh defaults to local Claude Code on Sonnet when available; use `--narrative-provider <route>` to override the narrator, or `--no-narrative-provider` for deterministic-only attach.
97	
98	### Set A Budget And A Time Limit, Then Walk Away
99	
100	Every provider response appends a spend record and updates totals. API routes track token cost. Subscription CLI routes can be capped by wall-clock time.
101	
102	```bash
103	deadreckon run "large refactor" --max-spend 15
104	deadreckon run "large refactor" --max-wall-seconds 1800
105	```
106	
107	High spend requires explicit confirmation, so scripts do not accidentally launch expensive runs.
108	
109	### Undo A Single Bad Turn Without Losing The Rest
110	
111	deadreckon snapshots the working directory at turn boundaries:
112	
113	```bash
114	deadreckon undo --run <run-id>
115	deadreckon undo --run <run-id> --turn 3
116	```
117	
118	This is not just `git reset`. It works against the run's own snapshot trail and records the undo in the run trace.
119	
120	### Write "Done" In English, Verified By A Watchdog
121	
122	Tell deadreckon what success looks like in plain language. It compiles your sentence into executable checks that an independent watchdog runs:
123	
124	```bash
125	deadreckon def-done "build, load in a browser, and show no console errors"
126	deadreckon def-done add "users can save drawings"
127	deadreckon def-done check
128	deadreckon run "finish the app"
129	```
130	
131	`deadreckon run` and `deadreckon chain run` prompt interactively when a project has no acceptance file yet. Generated files live under `.deadreckon/`.
132	
133	**Why the watchdog matters.** The watchdog holds a secret the agent process cannot read. It stamps the result with that secret. Without a valid stamp, the run can't terminate, and the agent can't produce the stamp itself.
134	
135	If no acceptance file is configured, the default is "the working directory exists and `cargo test` passes" (when `Cargo.toml` is present).

137	You can still edit the compiled YAML directly:

139	```yaml
140	name: notes check
141	checks:
142	  - kind: file_exists

144	  - kind: content_match
145	    path: "{working_dir}/notes.md"
146	    pattern: "dead reckoning"
147	  - kind: build_success
148	    cwd: "{working_dir}"
149	```
150	
151	Supported executable check kinds are `cargo_test`, `file_exists`, `content_match`, `build_success`, and `shell`. `content_match` treats `pattern` as a regex when valid, with substring fallback for simple text.
152	
153	### Get An Auditable Artifact, Not A Transcript
154	
155	deadreckon records which model/tool call touched which files, then writes self-documenting artifacts for the completed run:
156

158	deadreckon doc <run-id>
159	deadreckon doc <run-id> --kind as-built
160	deadreckon doc <run-id> --kind decisions
161	deadreckon doc <run-id> --kind delta

164	Each accepted run produces a review packet:
165	
166	- `RUN-NARRATIVE.md` explains what happened.
167	- `RUN-AS-BUILT.md` captures the subsystem shape after the run.
168	- `RUN-DECISIONS.md` records the implementation decision ledger: design decisions, deviations, tradeoffs, open questions, and multi-alternative decision details.
169	- `implementation-notes.html` is the live working copy the agent maintains while changing files.
170	- `AS-BUILT-DELTA.md` proposes architecture-doc updates when the run is broad enough.
171	- `manifest.json` records what was built and from what.
172	
173	Agentic CLIs usually leave you with a patch and a transcript. deadreckon turns
174	the session into a local published artifact you can inspect, export, extend, or
175	apply.

177	### Resume, Kill, Extend, Or Export Any Run
178	
179	Runs are lifecycle objects, not one terminal session:
180	
181	```bash
182	deadreckon list
183	deadreckon status
184	deadreckon show latest
185	deadreckon kill latest
186	deadreckon resume latest
187	deadreckon resume latest --from-turn 2
188	deadreckon extend latest "add tests and polish the UI"
189	deadreckon finish latest
190	deadreckon export latest --dest ./finished-project
191	deadreckon cleanup --completed
192	```
193	
194	Resume reconstructs history from durable traces and ignores incomplete trailing trace entries.
195	
196	### Autonomous Chains For Multi-Step Work
197	
198	Some tasks are too big for one goal. Chains let you break work into ordered steps that run end-to-end, with the same gate enforcement and the same lifecycle commands per step:
199	
200	```bash
201	deadreckon chain plan "ship a working SaaS billing flow" --n 4
202	deadreckon chain run latest
203	deadreckon chain attach latest
204	deadreckon chain kill latest
205	```
206	
207	Each chain step is a real run with its own signed acceptance gate. If a step fails its gate, the chain stops there; later steps don't start. Killing a chain cascades to whatever step is live. The attach TUI shows the whole chain timeline, not just the current turn, so you can see where you are in the plan without leaving the dashboard.
208	
209	You can also extend a finished run into a follow-up step instead of planning the whole chain up front:
210	
211	```bash
212	deadreckon chain extend latest "add billing webhooks and retry logic"
213	```
214	
215	## The Mental Model
216	
217	```text
218	your repo
219	  |
220	  | deadreckon def-done "what 'finished' looks like, in English"
221	  | deadreckon run  "what to build"
222	  v
223	isolated worktree or copy   ◄── your real checkout untouched
224	  |
225	  | provider route: cli:codex, cli:claude-code, anthropic, openai, ...
226	  v
227	sandboxed turn loop         ◄── agent works here
228	  |
229	  | every turn: trace, spend, provenance, snapshot, docs
230	  | check fails? agent gets another turn
231	  v
232	dr-gate watchdog            ◄── separate process, holds hidden nonce
233	  |                              agent CANNOT produce a valid marker
234	  | checks pass + signature valid?
235	  v
236	promoted artifact           ◄── narrative, decisions, file lineage
237	  |
238	  | inspect, doc, apply, discard, extend, export, cleanup
239	  v
240	your branch or library
241	```
242	
243	For multi-step work, `deadreckon chain` wraps this whole loop and runs N of them in order, stopping on the first gate failure.
244	
245	The agent owns the coding. deadreckon owns the boundary.
246	
247	## Quickstart
248	
249	Build once:
250	
251	```bash
252	cargo build --release
253	```
254	
255	The binary is `./target/release/deadreckon`. Add it to your `PATH` or alias it; the rest of this README just says `deadreckon`.
256	
257	Install shell tab completion. `deadreckon init` does this automatically when it
258	can detect your shell; this command repairs or installs it later:
259	
260	```bash
261	deadreckon completion install
262	```
263	
264	For raw generated scripts or shell overrides, run `deadreckon completion --help`.
265	
266	Configure and run a task end-to-end:
267	
268	```bash
269	deadreckon init --provider cli:claude-code --sandbox auto --max-spend 10
270	
271	deadreckon def-done   "users can sign up, log in, and save a drawing"
272	deadreckon run    "build the app"
273	deadreckon attach latest    # watch live, Ctrl-D to detach
274	deadreckon doc    latest    # read the narrative once done
275	deadreckon apply  latest --autostash --cleanup
276	```
277	
278	`run` prints the run id and attach command immediately, and shows a preview of mode, branch, base ref, and worktree path before creating anything. Use `--preview` to print the preview and exit.
279	
280	### Try It Without API Keys
281	
282	```bash
283	DEADRECKON_HOME=$PWD/.deadreckon-smoke \
284	  deadreckon run "tiny hello rust" --smoke --sandbox none --max-spend 1
285	```
286	
287	The provider response is faked, but every other moving part (turn loop, sandbox, snapshots, spend, traces, gate) is real.
288	
289	## Configuration
290	
291	Switch providers, models, or defaults:
292	
293	```bash
294	deadreckon init --provider cli:codex --sandbox auto --max-spend 10
295	deadreckon init --provider anthropic --api-key "$ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"
296	deadreckon config provider cli:claude-code
297	deadreckon config model sonnet --provider cli:claude-code
298	deadreckon config set defaults.max_spend 15
299	```
300	
301	Override per run:
302	
303	```bash
304	deadreckon run "goal" --provider cli:codex --model gpt-5.1-codex
305	deadreckon run --preview "goal"     # show route and model, don't start
306	```
307	
308	Runtime config lives at `~/.deadreckon/config.toml`. Set `DEADRECKON_HOME` for isolated local runs or tests.
309	
310	### Sandbox Backends
311	
312	| Backend | What it is |
313	|---|---|
314	| `auto` | Picks the right native sandbox for your OS (default) |
315	| `sandbox-exec` | macOS native |
316	| `bwrap` | Linux native (bubblewrap) |
317	| `docker` | Opt-in container sandbox |
318	| `none` | Off (unsafe for real unattended work) |
319	
320	Check what your machine supports with `deadreckon doctor`.
321	
322	## Compared With Agentic Coding CLIs
323	
324	deadreckon doesn't replace Claude Code, Codex, or Cursor CLI; it supervises them. Use deadreckon when the task is too long, risky, or expensive to "run the agent in my checkout and hope I can reconstruct what happened."
325	
326	| Operational concern | Agentic CLI alone | deadreckon supervising the CLI |
327	|---|---|---|
328	| Workspace safety | Often runs where you start it | Creates an isolated worktree by default and leaves your checkout untouched |
329	| Long-running attach | Usually tied to the current terminal session | Run state is durable; attach from another terminal later |
330	| Process control | Kill/resume behavior varies by tool | Tracks child PIDs, kills live work, resumes from durable state |
331	| Spend control | Token/cost visibility varies by provider | Writes `spend.jsonl`, tracks totals, enforces spend and wall-clock caps |
332	| Undo | Usually git-level or manual | Snapshots every turn and restores a specific turn with `deadreckon undo` |
333	| Provenance | Conversation history may not map cleanly to file changes | Records model/tool/file linkage in `provenance.jsonl` |
334	| Observability | Tool logs are tool-specific | Writes normalized `events.jsonl`, `traces.jsonl`, spend, docs, and run state |
335	| Done criteria | The agent may declare itself done | Requires a signed `dr-gate` marker before promotion |
336	| Applying work | Patch review/apply flow is tool-specific | `apply`, `discard`, `export`, `extend`, and `cleanup` are first-class lifecycle actions |
337	| Multi-run coordination | Usually left to the operator | Scope/task locks prevent conflicting same-task runs |
338	
339	Use the agentic CLI for intelligence. Use deadreckon for isolation, supervision, evidence, recovery, and promotion.
340	
341	## Command Surface
342	
343	Core lifecycle:
344	
345	```text
346	init          create local config
347	config        inspect or edit config keys
348	run           start an unattended coding run
349	attach        open the live dashboard
350	status        latest run and next action for this project
351	list          list runs (current project; --all for every scope)
352	show          inspect state, lineage, spend, files
353	doc           print or export run documentation
354	apply         apply a completed worktree run to your branch
355	abandon       remove a worktree run and temporary branch
356	export        copy a completed artifact to a normal directory
357	extend        continue from a completed run
358	resume        continue an interrupted run
359	kill          stop a live run and child processes
360	undo          restore a previous turn snapshot
361	cleanup       clean abandoned, stale, or completed worktrees
362	finish        choose apply or export from completed run
363	import        normalize histories from other coding tools
364	doctor        check config, providers, sandboxes, disk, runtime
365	```
366	
367	Aliases: `keep` → `apply`, `materialize` → `export`, `discard` → `abandon`, `prune` → `cleanup`, `follow-up` → `extend`, `continue` → `resume`, `stop` → `kill`, `next` → `status`.
368	
369	## Verification
370	
371	Full local verification:
372	
373	```bash
374	make verify
375	```
376	
377	Useful targeted checks:
378	
379	```bash
380	make build
381	make smoke
382	make doctor
383	STRESS_SECONDS=30 make stress
384	```
385	
386	The workspace test suite covers provider routing, mock OpenAI-compatible runs, CLI-provider wrappers, kill/resume behavior, signed gates, snapshots, provenance/trace linkage, worktree/copy/in-place modes, lifecycle actions, docs generation, and multi-run locking.
387	
388	## Status
389	
390	deadreckon is alpha software. The core lifecycle (isolated runs, signed gates, durable state, undo, docs, and apply) is implemented and tested.
391	
392	The V1 candidate list is deliberately short. The next big feature is explicit sub-agent forking:
393	
394	```text
395	deadreckon fork <run-id> --prompt "..."
396	```

830	`crates/deadreckon-providers/src/router.rs`. Concrete providers handle Anthropic/OpenAI/OpenAI-compatible/smoke/Codex/Claude; descriptor-backed generic CLI providers handle any registered CLI descriptor that does not need a concrete adapter. On `complete()`:

834	    if !route.has_credential() { failures.push(...); continue; }
835	    match route.complete(request).await {
836	        Ok(resp) => return Ok(resp),
837	        Err(e) => failures.push(format!("{}: {e}", route.name())),
838	    }
839	}
840	Err(ProviderError::NoRoute(failures.join("; ")))
841	```
842	
843	First credentialed route to succeed wins. All errors aggregate into the failure message.

911	- `--die-with-parent --unshare-pid --unshare-ipc --unshare-uts`
912	- `--tmpfs <cwd>/.deadreckon-home` and `--setenv HOME <cwd>/.deadreckon-home` (ephemeral tmpfs `$HOME`)
913	- `--ro-bind <path> <path>` for each entry in `system_read_allowlist(cwd, spec.read_allowlist)`
914	- `--bind <path> <path>` for each entry in `spec.write_allowlist`
915	- `--bind <cwd> <cwd>`, `--proc /proc`, `--dev /dev`, `--chdir <cwd>`
916	- `--unshare-net` unless `allow_network=true`
917	
918	### 11.6 Docker
919	
920	`lib.rs:359-388`. Constructs `docker run --rm -v <cwd>:<cwd> -w <cwd> [--network none] [-e KEY=VAL]... rust:1 <program> <args...>`. Hardcoded base image is `rust:1`. Only the cwd is mounted.
921	
922	### 11.7 None
923	
924	`lib.rs:191-203`. No isolation. Always returns a warning: `"sandbox backend none is unsafe; use only for explicit local verification"`. The warning lands in the trace.
925	
926	### 11.8 SIGTERM/SIGKILL escalation
927	
928	`lib.rs:131-151`:
929	
930	```rust
931	if let Some(token) = spec.cancellation_token.as_ref() {
932	    tokio::select! {
933	        _ = token.cancelled() => {
934	            if let Some(pid) = pid {
935	                signal_pid(pid, false);                      // SIGTERM
936	                sleep(Duration::from_secs(2)).await;         // 2s grace
937	                if child.try_wait()?.is_none() {
938	                    signal_pid(pid, true);                   // SIGKILL
939	                }
940	            }
941	            let _ = child.wait().await;
942	            if let Some(pid_file) = spec.pid_file.as_ref() {
943	                let _ = tokio::fs::remove_file(pid_file).await;
944	            }
945	            return Err(SandboxError::Cancelled);
946	        }
947	        status = child.wait() => status
948	    }
949	}
950	```
951	
952	`signal_pid` is defined at `lib.rs:473-483` (uses `nix::sys::signal::kill`).
953	
954	---
955	
956	## 12. Cancellation & Supervision
957	
958	### 12.1 Cancellation tokens
959	
960	The turn loop owns `run_token = CancellationToken::new()`; per turn it creates `turn_token = run_token.child_token()`; per tool call it can further create `tool_token = turn_token.child_token()`. The token threads through:
961	
962	- HTTP providers: `tokio::select!` on `token.cancelled()` vs the `reqwest` future.
963	- CLI providers: passed to `cli_common::run_cli` → `SandboxSpec.cancellation_token` → the sandbox layer.
964	- Tool dispatch (`Action::Bash`): passed to `run_sandbox(SandboxSpec { cancellation_token: Some(tool_token), ... })`.
965	
966	### 12.2 Child PID supervision
967	
968	Multiple sources contribute PIDs to track:
969	
970	- `state.child_pids: Vec<u32>` — populated by the CLI itself (`main.rs:333`).
971	- Per-subprocess PID files at `run_root/child-pids/*.pid` — written by the sandbox layer (`lib.rs:129`) and read by `supervised_pids()` (`main.rs:923`).
972	
973	`kill_command` reads both, releases the lock, sets `state.status = Killed`, and signals every PID. Without `--escalate`, it tries the graceful signal, waits 1.5s, then SIGKILLs anything still alive.
974	
975	### 12.3 What `kill` cannot do
976	
977	`kill` does **not** flip a cancellation token in a running deadreckon process. If a deadreckon `run` is still running, `kill` only signals its child PIDs; the deadreckon process itself relies on its own cancellation token tree, which `kill` doesn't reach across processes. In practice this works because killing the children causes the providers/sandbox to error out, which the turn loop sees and propagates as a failure. This remains a hardening target.
978	
979	---
980	
981	## 13. Acceptance Gate & Anti-Self-Attestation
982	
983	### 13.1 The principle
984	
985	The agent (LLM) **cannot** be trusted to declare a run done. `Completed` is reachable only via an acceptance marker signed by an external binary that the agent does not have keys to.
986	
987	### 13.2 `AcceptanceMarker`
988	
989	`crates/deadreckon-core/src/gate.rs:16-28`:
990	
991	```rust
992	pub struct AcceptanceMarker {
993	    pub schema_version: u32,
994	    pub run_id: String,
995	    pub status: String,           // "pass" | "fail"
996	    pub produced_by: String,      // must be "dr-gate"
997	    pub checked_at: DateTime<Utc>,
998	    pub working_dir: PathBuf,
999	    pub signature: String,        // hash over fields + nonce
1000	    pub check_count: usize,
1001	}
1002	```
1003	
1004	Marker location: `<run_root>/proofs/turn-acceptance.json`.
1005	
1006	### 13.3 `dr-gate` binary
1007	
1008	`crates/deadreckon/src/bin/dr-gate.rs` (33 lines). Standalone binary that:
1009	
1010	1. Reads `--run <id>` and `--working-dir <path>`.
1011	2. Loads `acceptance.yaml` (if present) from the run root.
1012	3. Runs each check (cargo test, file-exists, content-match, build-success).
1013	4. If all required checks pass, writes a signed `AcceptanceMarker` to `proofs/turn-acceptance.json`.
1014	
1015	The marker's `signature` is computed from `gate/nonce` (a UUID written at run-init time by the deadreckon binary at `state.rs:188`). Only `dr-gate` reads the nonce; the agent never has access.
1016	
1017	### 13.4 Validation
1018	
1019	`gate.rs:88-118`:
1020	
1021	```rust
1022	pub fn validate_acceptance_marker(state: &PipelineState) -> Result<AcceptanceMarker> {
1023	    let path = marker_path(state);
1024	    let raw = std::fs::read(&path).with_path(&path)?;
1025	    let marker: AcceptanceMarker = serde_json::from_slice(&raw).with_json_path(&path)?;
1026	    if marker.schema_version != 1 { return Err(...); }
1027	    if marker.run_id != state.run_id {
1028	        return Err("acceptance marker run_id ... does not match");
1029	    }
1030	    if marker.status != "pass" || marker.produced_by != "dr-gate" {
1031	        return Err("acceptance marker was not produced by dr-gate with pass status");
1032	    }
1033	    let expected = marker_signature(&state.run_root, &marker)?;
1034	    if marker.signature != expected {
1035	        return Err("acceptance marker signature is invalid; forged self-attestation refused");
1036	    }
1037	    Ok(marker)
1038	}
1039	```
1040	
1041	A forged marker by the agent fails the signature check at line 114.
1042	
1043	### 13.5 Streaming progress
1044	
1045	While checks are running, `evaluate_acceptance_checks_with_progress` (`gate.rs:228-244`) appends one `AcceptanceProgressEntry` per state transition to `proofs/acceptance-progress.jsonl`:
1046	
1047	```rust
1048	pub struct AcceptanceProgressEntry {
1049	    pub checked_at: DateTime<Utc>,
1050	    pub status: String,        // "started" | "running" | "passed" | "failed"
1051	    pub index: usize,
1052	    pub total: usize,
1053	    pub result: Option<AcceptanceCheckResult>,
1054	}
1055	```
1056	
1057	The progress file is truncated at the start of each evaluation so resumed/extended runs do not mix with prior attempts. The attach TUI tails this file (§18) so operators can see acceptance advance from "running 2/5" → "passed 2/5" while `dr-gate` works. The signed `AcceptanceMarker` is still the load-bearing artifact; progress is observational telemetry only.
1058	
1059	### 13.6 Where the gate is invoked
1060	
1061	When the turn loop emits `Action::Done` — either through a CLI sub-agent finishing or a JSON-action provider returning `Done` — it routes through `acceptance_gate_passed_or_record_failure` (`crates/deadreckon-runtime/src/turn_loop.rs:1298`). Both call sites (`turn_loop.rs:359` for JSON Done, `turn_loop.rs:615` for CLI sub-agent Done) use this helper.
1062	
1063	The helper composes `run_acceptance_gate` (invokes `dr-gate` as a subprocess) and `validate_acceptance_marker` (signature + run_id check):
1064	
1065	- **If the gate passes:** the helper returns `true` and the loop continues into `promote_if_ready`.
1066	- **If the gate fails:** the helper logs `acceptance.failed` to `traces.jsonl`, appends an explicit corrective hint to the run history (`"acceptance failed after turn N: <reason>. Continue by fixing the failing done criteria; do not declare done until dr-gate passes."`), emits a `RunEventKind::Error` event, records the reason in `state.failure_reason`, and **returns `false` — the run does not terminate**.
1067	
1068	The agent sees the failure inside the next turn doc and can revise the working tree and re-declare `Done`. Only when the turn budget is exhausted does the run fail; at that point the accumulated reasons in `state.failure_reason` become the final `failure_reason` text (`turn_loop.rs:633`).
1069	
1070	---
1071	
1072	## 14. Telemetry: Spend, Traces, Provenance, Events
1073	
1074	Five append-only JSONL files capture every run's history. Four (`spend.jsonl`, `traces.jsonl`, `provenance.jsonl`, `events.jsonl`) live under `<run_root>/` directly; the fifth (`proofs/acceptance-progress.jsonl`, see §13.5) is gate-scoped and truncated per evaluation. All are written via `append_json_line` (`state.rs:375-388`), which opens in append mode and `sync_all`s after each line.
1075	
1076	### 14.1 `spend.jsonl`
1077	
1078	Schema:
1079	
1080	```json
1081	{
1082	  "timestamp": "<RFC3339>",
1083	  "run_id": "...",
1084	  "turn": 3,
1085	  "provider": "cli:claude-code",
1086	  "model": "claude-sonnet-4-5",
1087	  "input_tokens": 0,
1088	  "output_tokens": 0,
1089	  "cost_usd": 0.0,
1090	  "subscription": true,
1091	  "wall_time_seconds": 42.1
1092	}
1093	```
1094	
1095	One line per LLM call. HTTP providers fill in token counts and USD; CLI providers fill in `subscription: true` + `wall_time_seconds`.
1096	
1097	### 14.2 `traces.jsonl`
1098	
1099	Schema:
1100	
1101	```json
1102	{
1103	  "timestamp": "<RFC3339>",
1104	  "run_id": "...",
1105	  "turn": 3,
1106	  "event": "llm.complete" | "tool.bash" | "tool.write_file" | "tool.cli_subagent" | "import.claude-code" | ...,
1107	  "latency_ms": 1234,
1108	  "detail": { "tool_call_id": "...", "provider": "...", "trace": {...} }
1109	}
1110	```
1111	
1112	Every LLM call, every tool dispatch, every notable event. The detail block carries free-form JSON per event kind.
1113	
1114	### 14.3 `provenance.jsonl`
1115	
1116	Schema (per file changed):
1117	
1118	```json
1119	{
1120	  "timestamp": "<RFC3339>",
1121	  "run_id": "...",
1122	  "turn": 3,
1123	  "tool_call_id": "...",
1124	  "model": "claude-sonnet-4-5",
1125	  "session_id": "...",
1126	  "file": "src/main.rs"
1127	}
1128	```
1129	
1130	One line per file changed by a tool call. Lets `show <run-id>` answer "which prompt produced this file?"
1131	
1132	### 14.4 `events.jsonl`
1133	
1134	Structured `RunEvent` log: `TurnStarted { turn }`, `ToolCallStarted { tool_call_id, kind }`, `ToolCallResult { tool_call_id, status, latency_ms }`, `RunCompleted { outcome }`. Also published on a `tokio::sync::broadcast` channel (`events.rs`) for in-process subscribers (the TUI uses this when implemented; today the TUI polls files instead — see §22).
1135	
1136	---
1137	
1138	## 15. Resume Semantics
1139	
1140	`crates/deadreckon/src/main.rs:940-1000` is the `resume_command` handler.
1141	
1142	### 15.1 The Completed guard
1143	
1144	`main.rs:947`:
1145	
1146	```rust
1147	if state.status == RunStatus::Completed {
1148	    println!("run {} is already completed", state.run_id);
1149	    return Ok(());
1150	}
1151	```
1152	
1153	Completed runs cannot be resumed. They can be re-promoted (idempotent) but not re-entered into the loop. The only forward path for a completed run today is to start a new run.
1154	
1155	### 15.2 The replay process
1156	
1157	For non-Completed runs (`Failed`, `Killed`, `Paused`):
1158	
1159	1. Acquire the task lock.
1160	2. Clear `failure_reason`, `pause_reason`, `killed_at`.
1161	3. Set `status = Planned`.
1162	4. Optionally extend `max_wall_seconds` from the resume flag.
1163	5. Set `child_pids = vec![cli_pid]`.
1164	6. `save_state()`.
1165	7. Call `run_turn_loop` with `RunLoopConfig.from_turn = <CLI flag>`.
1166	8. The loop calls `load_or_reconstruct_history(state, from_turn)` in `crates/deadreckon-runtime/src/turn_loop.rs`, which loads `history.json` if present, else reconstructs from `traces.jsonl`. With `from_turn = N`, history is truncated to N entries and `state.turn = N`.
1167	
1168	History reconstruction tolerates a `traces.jsonl` that ends mid-tool-call by ignoring incomplete entries — the next turn re-runs that turn.
1169	
1170	See `/Users/gdc/deadreckon/docs/RESUME-SEMANTICS.md` for the contract.
1171	
1172	---
1173	
1174	## 16. Cross-Tool Import
1175	
1176	`deadreckon import <source>` reads from external coding-agent histories and synthesizes a completed deadreckon run from one concrete imported session, or from an explicit `--all` root import. It is read-only with respect to provider-owned transcript roots and writes only deadreckon run-state files.
1177	
1178	Today's sources:
1179	
1180	| Source | Discovery | Format |
1181	|---|---|---|
1182	| `codex` / `cli:codex` | `cli:codex` descriptor `[ingest]`, including `CODEX_SESSIONS_DIR`, `session_meta.payload.cwd`, `*.jsonl`, and `codex-cli` schema | JSONL |
1183	| `claude-code` / `cli:claude-code` | `cli:claude-code` descriptor `[ingest]`, including `CLAUDE_PROJECTS_DIR` and Claude project-directory cwd mapping | JSONL |
1184	| `gemini` / `cli:gemini` | `cli:gemini` descriptor `[ingest]`, including `GEMINI_DIR`, JSON/JSONL storage, and `gemini` schema | JSON or JSONL |
1185	| `opencode` / `cli:opencode` | `cli:opencode` descriptor `[ingest]`, file-mode `storage/session`, `storage/message`, and `storage/part` | JSON |
1186	| `copilot` / `cli:copilot` | `cli:copilot` descriptor `[ingest]`, including `COPILOT_DIR`, `session-state`, nested `events.jsonl`, and `data.context.cwd` | JSONL |
1187	| `pi` / `cli:pi` | `cli:pi` descriptor `[ingest]`, including `PI_CODING_AGENT_SESSION_DIR`, top-level `cwd`, and Pi session-header validation | JSONL |
1188	| `cursor` | `~/.cursor/chats/` (`DEADRECKON_IMPORT_CURSOR_ROOT`) | SQLite via `sqlite3 -json` |
1189	
1190	The command surface is `deadreckon import <source> [--preview|--list|--session <id-or-path>|--cwd <path>|--all|--since <duration>|--replace|--json]`. Default import filters candidates to the launch cwd or `--cwd` where the descriptor supports cwd matching. Empty, stale, and ambiguous candidate sets refuse without creating a run and print concrete `try:` lines. `--preview` and `--list` never create run directories. `--all` is the explicit whole-root mode.
1191	
1192	The handler creates an `imported-<hash>` run id from the concrete source-session identity, parses selected transcript files, appends normalized source-neutral entries to `traces.jsonl`, writes file provenance to `provenance.jsonl`, marks the run `Completed` (skipping the gate), and writes `import.json` under the run root. The manifest records `source`, `source_alias`, `schema`, `storage`, `cwd`, `mode`, `session_id`, `session_paths`, `content_hash`, source time bounds, row/event/provenance counts, `raw_rows_stored = false`, and the `deadreckon import ... --replace` command needed to reimport. If an existing imported run has a different content hash, import refuses unless `--replace` is explicit.
1193	
1194	Trace `detail` rows use a stable import schema: `import_version`, canonical `source`, `schema`, optional `session_id`, `source_path`, optional `source_line`, `source_event`, optional `role`, `summary`, optional tool fields, `files`, optional token `usage`, and `raw_hash`. Raw provider payloads are not copied into every trace row by default; source path/line plus hashes preserve auditability. Parser coverage includes Codex agent messages/function calls/token counts, Claude content/tool blocks, Gemini JSON/JSONL messages/tool calls, OpenCode file-mode sessions/messages/parts, Copilot assistant/reasoning/tool/usage rows, Pi session/message/tool/result rows, and Cursor SQLite rows.
1195	
1196	`deadreckon import` is the *user-driven* ingest. The *TUI-driven* ingest path that lets `attach` read live provider transcripts uses the same descriptor `[ingest]` roots, env overrides, storage kinds, file globs, freshness windows, cwd matching, and schema keys for CLI providers; see §18.3 and `docs/design/PROVIDER-CLI-INGEST.md`. OpenCode SQLite, provider transcript mutation/undo, full replay UI, and cross-run import analytics remain V1 candidates in `docs/V1-CANDIDATES.md`.
1197	
1198	---

1201	
1202	The `Commands` enum in `crates/deadreckon/src/main.rs` defines the CLI surface. Handlers and roles:
1203	
1204	| Verb | Handler | Role |
1205	|---|---|---|
1206	| `init` | `cli.rs:440` | Interactive setup of `~/.deadreckon/config.toml` |

1221	| `undo` | `cli.rs:1265` | Restore snapshot to a target turn |
1222	| `show` | `cli.rs:1281` | Pretty-print full state + provenance + traces; `--why-failed` for runs and plans |
1223	| `import` | `cli.rs:1329` | Read-only descriptor-backed transcript import from CLI providers plus Cursor SQLite |
1224	| `chain` | `cli.rs:798` | Create, plan, run, attach, pause/resume/kill, undo, extend, and redo serial autonomous chains |
1225	| `orchestrate` | `cli.rs:630` | One-command wrappers for `review` and `full-plan` multi-agent runs |
1226	| `plan` | `cli.rs:679` | Write an orchestration plan (worker specs + `plan.json`) without starting child runs |
1227	| `fork` | `cli.rs:720` | Spawn ready child runs for a plan and supervise them through completion |
1228	| `merge` | `cli.rs:756` | Compose completed child library artifacts into a new promoted run (with semantic merge repair) |
1229	| `def-done` | `cli.rs:502` | Write, add, show, or check the project's English done criteria |
1230	| `acceptance` | `cli.rs:492` | Hidden compatibility surface for creating, explaining, or checking done criteria |
1231	| `doc` | `cli.rs:1182` | Print run narrative, as-built, implementation decision ledger, or delta; with optional polish pass |
1232	| `history` | `cli.rs:1298` | Search durable run traces and provenance (regex/scope/plan filters) |
1233	| `library` | `cli.rs:983` | Query promoted run artifacts by goal/date/scope |
1234	| `detect` | `cli.rs:919` | Probe registered providers and return availability and credential status |
1235	| `providers` | `cli.rs:932` | List provider routes, models, kind tokens, and the active selection |
1236	| `update` | `cli.rs:941` | Check for or route self-updates via npm, Homebrew, shell, Cargo, or source channel |
1237	| `completion` / `completions` | `cli.rs:482` | Generate or install shell tab-completion scripts (bash, zsh, fish, elvish, powershell) |
1238	
1239	The CLI defaults are honest: `--sandbox` defaults to `auto`, `--max-spend` defaults to `$10` (with a confirmation gate above `$50`), `--provider` defaults to the highest-credentialed entry per the fallback chain, `--skill` defaults to `default-coding`.
1240	
1241	`run` now starts codebase-aware by default. In a git repo it previews and then creates a `git worktree` on a `dr/...` branch; `--fresh` preserves the old empty-working-dir behavior, `--from <path>` uses copy mode, and `--in-place --i-know-its-a-lot` edits the source tree directly. Completed worktree runs hint `apply` / `discard`; copy and fresh runs hint `export` / `extend`. Run-id arguments accept unique prefixes and `latest` / `last` resolves to the latest run in the current project scope.
1242	
1243	`completion install` is driven from the real clap command tree, so subcommand aliases, flags, and value-hint completions stay in sync with `deadreckon --help`. The handler detects the active shell via `$SHELL`, writes the script to a per-shell default path (e.g. `~/.zsh/completions/_deadreckon`, `~/.local/share/bash-completion/completions/deadreckon`), and for zsh adds a managed `# deadreckon completion` block to `~/.zshrc` unless `--no-rc` is passed. `init` invokes `try_install_completion_after_init` so first-time setup ships completions opt-out (`init --no-completion`). The per-shell stdout variants (`completion bash|zsh|fish|elvish|powershell`) print the script for users who manage their own shell config.
1244	
1245	`run` startup details (`print_run_started`) are now also emitted at the top of `extend` and `resume` so extended/resumed runs surface their selected provider route and doc-provider source the same way fresh runs do. Interactive terminals receive a `deadreckoning_course` ASCII progress strip and a polled `cli_wait_status` line while a long turn is in flight; the status is cleared as soon as the loop reports back. `kill` against a loaded run now also persists `RunStatus::Killed` + `killed_at` + `failure_reason = "killed by user"` before returning so downstream tooling sees a consistent terminal state.
1246

1248	
1249	## 18. TUI (`attach`)
1250	
1251	`crates/deadreckon/src/main.rs:874-1289` houses `attach_command` plus the rendering helpers.
1252	
1253	### 18.1 Behavior
1254	
1255	- On a TTY: `attach_tui()` enables raw mode, alternate screen, and renders a `ratatui` UI.
1256	- Off-TTY: prints a plain-text summary + locations.
1257	
1258	`attach` dispatches by id kind: a run id opens the run TUI documented below, a chain id opens the chain attach view (`Chains`, §28), and a plan id opens the plan attach TUI (`Plans`, §30.3 / §32.3). All three TUIs draw from the same palette (`ui::TUI_PALETTE`, §26.7) and the same key conventions (`q`/`Esc`/`Ctrl-D` detach; `d` toggles docs view in the run TUI; `Enter` drills into a child run from plan attach).
1259	
1260	`attach <id> --view narrative` adds a calmer operator projection for runs, plans, and plan child refs. The default remains `activity`, so raw tool/provider lines still open first unless the user requests the narrative view. In narrative mode, `n` toggles back to raw activity, `v` cycles `architecture -> agents -> files -> evidence -> none`, and `r` requests a provider-backed refresh when a configured route is available. While the TTY narrative view is open, meaningful run and plan events also request a provider refresh: errors, completions, tool milestones, docs checkpoints, acceptance running/pass/fail transitions, child-run discovery, task terminal states, and merge-repair milestones. Long-running quiet periods request a refresh after the narrative quiet window when the run or plan is still running. Provider refreshes are bounded: the prompt is built from redacted evidence windows, the provider must return strict cited JSON, graph labels may only target deterministic graph ids, and failures persist a stale deterministic projection instead of breaking attach.
1261	
1262	### 18.2 Layout
1263	
1264	`attach_panel_layout` (`main.rs:~10225`):
1265	
1266	```rust
1267	let vertical = Layout::default()
1268	    .direction(Direction::Vertical)
1269	    .constraints([
1270	        Constraint::Length(5),    // top band: header + spend (if metered) + context + acceptance
1271	        Constraint::Min(10),      // tool calls + provider activity + live files
1272	        Constraint::Length(4),    // processes/status
1273	        Constraint::Length(2),    // keybindings footer (multi-line during long ops)
1274	    ])
1275	    .split(area);
1276	```
1277	
1278	The top band is split horizontally into three panels for subscription providers (header 66 / context 17 / acceptance 17) and four for metered API providers (header 55 / spend 15 / context 15 / acceptance 15):
1279	
1280	- **Header** (short run id, status, phase, provider, sandbox, turn timer, truncated goal, working/artifact path; degrades to an identity strip when live status is unavailable).
1281	- **Spend meter** only for metered API providers; CLI subscription providers omit cost and emphasize context/wall time.
1282	- **Context meter**: compact token/window summary with green/yellow/red thresholds.
1283	- **Acceptance meter**: derived from `AcceptanceLive` (`collect_acceptance_live` in `main.rs:~10172`). When `proofs/acceptance-progress.jsonl` exists, the panel tails it and surfaces `running 2/5`, `passed`, or `failed` with the offending check; once `turn-acceptance.json` is signed, it pivots to a marker view (`acceptance_live_from_marker`). Color thresholds are owned by `acceptance_color`.
1284	- **Center, left**: wide streaming list of tool calls + provider activity + recent events. Acceptance lines from `acceptance_activity_lines` are interleaved so the operator sees the same progress in the activity stream and the meter.
1285	- **Narrative view**: `--view narrative` or `n` swaps the center-left activity pane for prose sections under the `Narrated` operator heading: freshness/coverage, headline, current work, architecture notes, risks, next likely action, and citations. Wide terminals split that pane with a right-side visual map; narrow terminals collapse to prose first. Run narratives cite `proofs/acceptance-progress.jsonl` or `proofs/turn-acceptance.json` when acceptance evidence exists, so failed done criteria point at the durable proof artifact. Plain/off-TTY narrative attach prints the same projection with citations and ASCII map lines when `--visual` is not `none`; `--json --view narrative` emits the structured state, snapshot, and graph objects. Non-TTY narrative attach stays deterministic and does not call a provider unless a future explicit refresh surface opts in. Chain narrative attach currently returns an unsupported response with `try:` lines for run and plan narrative attach.
1286	- **Completed docs view**: pressing `d` toggles the center-left panel from provider activity or narrative view to `RUN-NARRATIVE.md` rendered through `pulldown-cmark` into ratatui `Line`/`Span`s. Headings, bullets, inline code, fenced code blocks, links, task markers, math, and horizontal rules receive terminal styles and remain scrollable. The docs view remains a separate completed-run artifact rather than being merged into the live narrative projection.
1287	- **Center, right**: narrower live files list with count/bytes in the panel title.
1288	- **Bottom**: supervised PIDs + their `ps` lines (alive/dead annotation).
1289	- **Footer**: action-first completed footer (`[d] Docs` / `[d] Activity`, `[a] Apply`, `[b] Abandon`, `[s] Show`) or scroll/detach help while running. The footer's second line carries `deadreckoning_status_line` while long operations are in flight.
1290	
1291	### 18.3 Data source
1292	
1293	The run TUI still polls run files on disk every 500 ms: `spend.jsonl`, `traces.jsonl`, `events.jsonl`, `proofs/acceptance-progress.jsonl`, `proofs/turn-acceptance.json`, plus provider-native logs when the active provider writes them. `collect_provider_activity` now resolves provider ingest through descriptor `[ingest]` metadata: candidate roots, env overrides, cwd matching, storage kind, file glob, freshness window, and schema key. `deadreckon import` reuses the same descriptor metadata for provider transcript discovery and adds import-only session selection, manifest writing, and normalized trace/provenance event creation. `cli:codex` reads `~/.codex/sessions/**.jsonl` and matches `session_meta.payload.cwd`; `cli:claude-code` reads `~/.claude/projects/<cwd-slug>/*.jsonl` using Claude Code's path-to-project mapping and matches top-level `cwd`; `cli:gemini` reads Gemini JSON/JSONL file logs; `cli:opencode` reads OpenCode file-mode `storage/session`, `storage/message`, and `storage/part` JSON; `cli:copilot` reads `~/.copilot/session-state/*.jsonl` plus nested `events.jsonl` and matches `data.context.cwd`; `cli:pi` reads `~/.pi/agent/sessions/<encoded-cwd>/*.jsonl`, validates the first nonblank row is a Pi `session`, and matches the header `cwd`. The shared collector handles candidate discovery, recency filtering, run matching, stream capping, and context telemetry. Schema-specific adapters only decode rows into common activity lines (`agent`, `thinking`, `tool`, `result`, `todo`, `tokens`) and normalize tool labels through `deadreckon_providers::taxonomy`.
1294	
1295	Same-process run attaches can use the `RunEventBus` broadcast channel directly; cross-process run attaches still poll. Plan attach is different after the live-UX slice: it consumes `PlanEventBus` / `PlanEventFeed`, which owns `plan-events.jsonl` replay/tailing, emits plan snapshots, tolerates malformed or partial plan-event rows, and multiplexes discovered child and repair run `events.jsonl` streams into the plan activity pane. The production feed remains durable-file backed for cross-process attach, with a broadcast-capable API available for same-process plan streams.
1296	
1297	### 18.4 Narrative projection files
1298	
1299	Narrative attach writes projection files, not source-of-truth state. Run projections live under `<run-root>/narrative/`; plan projections live under `<plan-dir>/narrative/`.
1300	
1301	- `state.json` records the latest snapshot id/status, coverage, cadence, provider source, provider call count, cost/wall-clock accounting, and last refresh error.
1302	- `snapshots.jsonl` is append-only. Each row contains cited `current_work`, `architecture_notes`, `risks`, `next_likely`, citations, and plan-only agent/coordination sections. Malformed rows are skipped when reading the latest snapshot.
1303	- `architecture-graph.json` is a deterministic graph over run files, provider ids, checkpoints, plan tasks, dependencies, child runs, and citation ids. The TUI renders architecture, agent, file, and evidence views from this graph using ASCII-compatible labels and color-independent badges.
1304	
1305	Plan projections prefer each child run's latest narrative snapshot when one exists. The plan agent table cites that child snapshot and uses its headline as the child summary, then falls back to child run state when no child narrative exists. Plan graphs also roll up file nodes from child narrative graphs so the plan-level files visual can show cross-agent touched file evidence without copying child logs into `plan-events.jsonl`.
1306	
1307	Provider-backed narration is an overlay on these projections. Manual `r` refresh, TTY narrative-view event refreshes, and TTY narrative-view quiet-threshold refreshes build a redacted prompt from the deterministic projection, send only bounded evidence summaries to the selected provider route, validate all returned claims against known evidence ids, reject invented graph ids, and persist a new fresh snapshot only after validation. The default narrator route is `cli:claude-code` with model override `sonnet`, which the Claude Code adapter launches as `claude --model sonnet --dangerously-skip-permissions -p <prompt>`; `--narrative-provider` overrides the route and leaves model selection to that provider/config entry, while `--no-narrative-provider` keeps attach deterministic-only. Event refreshes can bypass the ordinary freshness interval for meaningful deltas, while quiet-threshold refreshes still obey the freshness interval; budget, provider availability, JSON validation, citation validation, graph validation, and redaction guards always apply. If the provider is missing, over budget, behind cadence, returns malformed JSON, cites unknown evidence, emits secret-like text, or fails, attach keeps running and persists a stale deterministic snapshot with the error in `state.json`.
1308	
1309	---
1310	
1311	## 19. Configuration & BYOK
1312	
1313	### 19.1 `config.toml`
1314	
1315	Lives at `/Users/gdc/.deadreckon/config.toml` (overridable via `DEADRECKON_HOME`). Schema (`crates/deadreckon-providers/src/types.rs`):
1316	
1317	```rust
1318	pub struct ProviderConfigFile {
1319	    pub default_provider: Option<String>,
1320	    pub fallback: Option<Vec<String>>,
1321	    pub providers: BTreeMap<String, ProviderEntry>,
1322	}
1323	
1324	pub struct ProviderEntry {
1325	    pub kind: Option<ProviderKind>,
1326	    pub api_key: Option<String>,
1327	    pub api_key_env: Option<String>,
1328	    pub base_url: Option<String>,
1329	    pub model: Option<String>,
1330	    pub input_cost_per_million: Option<f64>,
1331	    pub output_cost_per_million: Option<f64>,
1332	    pub binary: Option<String>,
1333	    pub extra_args: Vec<String>,
1334	}
1335	```
1336	
1337	Example:
1338	
1339	```toml
1340	default_provider = "cli:codex"
1341	fallback = ["cli:codex", "cli:claude-code", "anthropic", "openai"]
1342	
1343	[defaults]
1344	max_spend = 10
1345	provider = "cli:codex"
1346	sandbox = "auto"
1347	
1348	[providers."cli:codex"]
1349	binary = "codex"
1350	extra_args = []
1351	kind = "cli-codex"
1352	model = "gpt-5.1-codex" # optional; omitted means provider default
1353	
1354	[providers.anthropic]
1355	api_key_env = "ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"
1356	base_url = "https://api.anthropic.com"
1357	model = "claude-sonnet-4-5"
1358	input_cost_per_million = 3.0
1359	output_cost_per_million = 15.0
1360	```
1361	
1362	Operator affordances: `deadreckon run --preview "goal"` renders the selected
1363	provider route, source, and model before state is created; `run --model <model>`
1364	and `extend --model <model>` override one run; `deadreckon config provider
1365	<route>` and `deadreckon config model <model> --provider <route>` persist the
1366	defaults. `init`, `config provider`, primary run/extend, orchestration roles,
1367	resume/doc polish, and provider-selection display all route through
1368	`crates/deadreckon/src/setup.rs`, which reports provider role, route, model,
1369	source (`flag`, `config`, `auto_subscription`, `run_provider`,
1370	`built_in_default`, or `none`), credential state, warnings, and `try:` lines
1371	without adding durable state. CLI providers pass explicit model overrides
1372	through to the underlying tool (`codex exec --model ...`, `claude --model ...`)
1373	and otherwise display `provider default`.
1374	
1375	Route resolution (`configured_route_names` in `crates/deadreckon-providers/src/router.rs`) now puts `default_provider` at the head of the chain, then appends `fallback` entries that aren't already present, then falls back to the built-in chain (`cli:claude-code` → `cli:codex` → `anthropic` → `openai` → `openai-compatible`) only if neither is configured. `read_config` (`config.rs`) backfills `default_provider` from a top-level `[defaults] provider` key when it's omitted, so the same TOML stanza drives both `init`-style defaults and the router. `--provider` on the CLI still short-circuits the whole chain.
1376	
1377	### 19.2 BYOK posture
1378	
1379	Three credential paths:
1380	
1381	1. **HTTP key.** Set `api_key` directly or `api_key_env = "FOO"` to read at runtime.
1382	2. **CLI subscription.** Run with `--provider cli:claude-code` or `cli:codex`. The binary's presence in `$PATH` is the credential. No key required.
1383	3. **OpenAI-compatible.** Plug an OpenRouter or `llama.cpp` endpoint into `base_url` + `api_key`.
1384	
1385	`deadreckon init` walks the user through option (1) or (2): it queries the provider registry for any subscription CLI provider whose binary is available (`setup::auto_subscription_cli_provider`) and offers the first match — `cli:claude-code`, `cli:codex`, `cli:gemini`, `cli:opencode`, `cli:copilot`, or `cli:pi`, depending on what's installed — before asking for keys. The chosen route is immediately validated through the shared setup resolver, and the generated config preserves a `cli:*` route in the fallback chain rather than overwriting with the historic claude/codex default.
1386

1426	
1427	## 21. Key Design Decisions
1428	
1429	1. **No new `PipelineState` fields without a strong reason.** Parent lineage, materialization status, and other run-level metadata live in files inside the working tree (e.g., `.deadreckon/parent.json`), not on the state struct. This keeps `state.json` migration-safe.
1430	
1431	2. **Two-layer split is non-negotiable.** Skills (Markdown) own judgment; the binary owns invariants. A skill cannot bypass the gate; a gate cannot read prompts.
1432	
1433	3. **Anti-self-attestation via a nonce only `dr-gate` reads.** The agent can produce any output it wants; it cannot produce a valid `AcceptanceMarker.signature` because it never sees `gate/nonce`.
1434	
1435	4. **Atomic promotion before completion.** `Completed` is set only after the library swap succeeds. If promotion fails, the run fails. This means a `Completed` status always implies a durable artifact in `library/`.
1436	
1437	5. **Platform-native sandboxing.** No Docker daemon dependency. Seatbelt on macOS, bwrap on Linux. Docker is opt-in. The "running on host machine feels like a bad idea" pain point is solved without forcing Docker.
1438	
1439	6. **BYOK extends to subscriptions.** `cli:claude-code` and `cli:codex` are first-class providers, not afterthoughts. Most users will run deadreckon via subscription, not API keys.
