114	            if let Some(existing) = read_lock_state(&path)? {
115	                return Err(DeadreckonError::LockHeld {

119	                });
120	            }

122	        }
123	        Err(source) => return Err(DeadreckonError::Io { path, source }),
124	    }
125	
126	    let existing = read_lock_state_from_file(&mut file, &path)?;
127	    if let Some(existing) = existing {
128	        let stale = lock_is_stale(&existing, stale_after);
129	        let alive = pid_is_alive(existing.pid);
130	        let same_owner = existing.run_id == run_id;
131	        if !same_owner && !stale && alive {
132	            file.unlock().with_path(&path)?;
133	            return Err(DeadreckonError::LockHeld {
134	                task_key: task_key.to_string(),
135	                run_id: existing.run_id,
136	                phase: existing.phase,
137	            });
138	        }
139	    }
140	
141	    // AS-BUILT §6: process-held locks are paired with a durable heartbeat so
142	    // a successor can distinguish live work from crash residue.
143	    let now = Utc::now();
144	    let state = LockState {
145	        task_key: task_key.to_string(),
146	        run_id: run_id.to_string(),
147	        scope: scope.to_string(),
148	        phase: phase.to_string(),
149	        pid: std::process::id(),
150	        acquired_at: now,
151	        updated_at: now,
152	    };
153	    write_lock_state_to_file(&mut file, &path, &state)?;
154	    Ok(LockGuard {
155	        path,
156	        file,
157	        state,
158	        released: false,
159	    })
160	}

255	fn read_lock_state(path: &Path) -> Result<Option<LockState>> {
256	    match fs::read(path) {

258	        Ok(data) => serde_json::from_slice(&data).map(Some).with_json_path(path),
259	        Err(source) if source.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => Ok(None),

267	fn read_lock_state_from_file(file: &mut File, path: &Path) -> Result<Option<LockState>> {
268	    file.seek(SeekFrom::Start(0)).with_path(path)?;
269	    let mut data = Vec::new();
270	    file.read_to_end(&mut data).with_path(path)?;
271	    if data.is_empty() {
272	        return Ok(None);
273	    }

277	fn write_lock_state_to_file(file: &mut File, path: &Path, state: &LockState) -> Result<()> {
278	    file.set_len(0).with_path(path)?;
279	    file.seek(SeekFrom::Start(0)).with_path(path)?;
280	    serde_json::to_writer_pretty(&mut *file, state).with_json_path(path)?;
281	    file.write_all(b"\n").with_path(path)?;
282	    file.sync_all().with_path(path)
283	}

27	pub fn promote_completed_run(

30	) -> Result<PathBuf> {
31	    validate_acceptance_marker(state)?;

33	    let library_dir = paths.library_dir(&state.scope, &state.run_id);

35	        state.working_dir = library_dir.clone();
36	        state.promoted_library_dir = Some(library_dir.clone());
37	        save_state(state)?;
38	        return Ok(library_dir);

40	
41	    let parent = library_dir.parent().ok_or_else(|| {
42	        DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(format!(
43	            "library path has no parent: {}",
44	            library_dir.display()
45	        ))
46	    })?;
47	    fs::create_dir_all(parent).with_path(parent)?;
48	    let staging = parent.join(format!(".{}.promoting", state.run_id));
49	    if staging.exists() {
50	        fs::remove_dir_all(&staging).with_path(&staging)?;
51	    }
52	    if !state.working_dir.exists() {
53	        return Err(DeadreckonError::NotFound(format!(
54	            "working directory {}",
55	            state.working_dir.display()
56	        )));
57	    }
58	    if state.working_dir == state.run_root.join("working") {
59	        fs::rename(&state.working_dir, &staging).with_path(&state.working_dir)?;
60	    } else {
61	        copy_tree(&state.working_dir, &staging)?;
62	    }
63	    write_manifest(state, &staging, state.working_dir.clone())?;
64	    fs::rename(&staging, &library_dir).with_path(&staging)?;
65	    state.working_dir = library_dir.clone();
66	    state.promoted_library_dir = Some(library_dir.clone());
67	    emit_event(
68	        state,
69	        None,
70	        RunEventKind::RunPromoted {
71	            library_dir: library_dir.clone(),
72	        },
73	    )?;
74	    save_state(state)?;
75	    Ok(library_dir)
76	}

104	    if !root.exists() {
105	        return Ok(Vec::new());
106	    }
107	    let mut files = Vec::new();
108	    for entry in WalkDir::new(root)
109	        .into_iter()
110	        .filter_map(std::result::Result::ok)
111	        .filter(|entry| entry.file_type().is_file())
112	    {
113	        files.push(entry.path().to_path_buf());
114	    }
115	    files.sort();
116	    Ok(files)
117	}
118	
119	pub fn copy_tree(from: &Path, to: &Path) -> Result<()> {
120	    fs::create_dir_all(to).with_path(to)?;
121	    if !from.exists() {
122	        return Ok(());
123	    }
124	    for entry in WalkDir::new(from).into_iter() {
125	        let entry = entry.map_err(|source| DeadreckonError::Io {
126	            path: from.to_path_buf(),
127	            source: source.into(),
128	        })?;
129	        let relative = entry.path().strip_prefix(from).map_err(|err| {
130	            DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(format!("copy source prefix error: {err}"))
131	        })?;
132	        let target = to.join(relative);
133	        if entry.file_type().is_dir() {
134	            fs::create_dir_all(&target).with_path(&target)?;
135	        } else if entry.file_type().is_file() {
136	            if let Some(parent) = target.parent() {
137	                fs::create_dir_all(parent).with_path(parent)?;
138	            }
139	            fs::copy(entry.path(), &target).with_path(&target)?;
140	        }
141	    }
142	    Ok(())
143	}

26	pub fn write_cancel_marker(state: &PipelineState, reason: impl Into<String>) -> Result<PathBuf> {
27	    let path = cancel_marker_path(state);
28	    let marker = CancelMarker {
29	        run_id: state.run_id.clone(),
30	        requested_at: Utc::now(),
31	        reason: reason.into(),
32	    };
33	    if let Some(parent) = path.parent() {
34	        std::fs::create_dir_all(parent).with_path(parent)?;
35	    }
36	    std::fs::write(
37	        &path,
38	        serde_json::to_vec_pretty(&marker).with_json_path(&path)?,
39	    )
40	    .with_path(&path)?;
41	    Ok(path)
42	}
43	
44	pub fn clear_cancel_marker(state: &PipelineState) -> Result<()> {
45	    let path = cancel_marker_path(state);
46	    match std::fs::remove_file(&path) {
47	        Ok(()) => Ok(()),
48	        Err(source) if source.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => Ok(()),
49	        Err(source) => Err(DeadreckonError::Io { path, source }),
50	    }
51	}
52

1	use std::ffi::{OsStr, OsString};
2	use std::io::Write as _;

6	use crate::error::{DeadreckonError, Result};
7	
8	const COMMIT_FAMILY_VERBS: &[&str] = &[
9	    "commit",
10	    "merge",
11	    "cherry-pick",
12	    "rebase",
13	    "tag",
14	    "am",
15	    "revert",
16	];
17	
18	pub fn run_git(cwd: &Path, args: &[&str]) -> Result<Output> {
19	    git_command(cwd, args).output().map_err(git_io)
20	}
21	
22	pub fn run_git_with_input(cwd: &Path, args: &[&str], input: &[u8]) -> Result<Output> {
23	    let mut child = git_command(cwd, args)
24	        .stdin(Stdio::piped())
25	        .stderr(Stdio::piped())
26	        .spawn()
27	        .map_err(git_io)?;
28	    if let Some(stdin) = child.stdin.as_mut() {
29	        stdin
30	            .write_all(input)
31	            .map_err(|source| DeadreckonError::Io {
32	                path: cwd.to_path_buf(),
33	                source,
34	            })?;
35	    }
36	    child.wait_with_output().map_err(git_io)
37	}
38	
39	pub fn git_command(cwd: &Path, args: &[&str]) -> Command {
40	    let mut command = Command::new("git");
41	    command.env("GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT", "0");
42	    for arg in hardened_git_prefix(args) {
43	        command.arg(arg);
44	    }
45	    command.arg("-C").arg(cwd).args(args);
46	    command
47	}
48	
49	pub fn hardened_git_prefix(args: &[&str]) -> Vec<&'static str> {
50	    let Some(verb) = first_git_verb(args) else {
51	        return Vec::new();
52	    };
53	    if COMMIT_FAMILY_VERBS.contains(&verb) {
54	        vec![
55	            "-c",
56	            "commit.gpgsign=false",
57	            "-c",
58	            "tag.gpgsign=false",
59	            "-c",
60	            "gpg.format=",
61	        ]
62	    } else {
63	        Vec::new()
64	    }
65	}
66	
67	pub fn hardened_git_argv(cwd: &Path, args: &[&str]) -> Vec<OsString> {
68	    let mut argv = vec![OsString::from("git")];
69	    argv.extend(hardened_git_prefix(args).into_iter().map(OsString::from));
70	    argv.push(OsString::from("-C"));
71	    argv.push(cwd.as_os_str().to_os_string());
72	    argv.extend(args.iter().map(OsString::from));
73	    argv
74	}
75	
76	fn first_git_verb<'a>(args: &'a [&str]) -> Option<&'a str> {
77	    args.iter().copied().find(|arg| !arg.starts_with('-'))
78	}
79	
80	fn git_io(source: std::io::Error) -> DeadreckonError {
81	    DeadreckonError::Io {
82	        path: PathBuf::from("git"),
83	        source,
84	    }
85	}
86

27	        match self {
28	            Self::Npm => "npm",
29	            Self::Brew => "brew",
30	            Self::Shell => "shell",
31	            Self::Cargo => "cargo",
32	            Self::Source => "source",
33	        }
34	    }

37	#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
38	pub struct Receipt {
39	    pub channel: Channel,
40	    pub channel_version: String,
41	    pub binary_path: PathBuf,
42	    pub installed_at: DateTime<Utc>,
43	    pub install_source: Option<String>,
44	    pub platform_package: Option<String>,
45	    pub receipt_version: u32,
46	}
47	
48	#[must_use]
49	pub fn receipt_path(paths: &DeadreckonPaths) -> PathBuf {
50	    paths.home().join(INSTALL_RECEIPT_FILE)
51	}
52	
53	pub fn read_receipt(paths: &DeadreckonPaths) -> Result<Option<Receipt>> {
54	    let path = receipt_path(paths);
55	    let raw = match fs::read(&path) {
56	        Ok(raw) => raw,
57	        Err(source) if source.kind() == io::ErrorKind::NotFound => return Ok(None),
58	        Err(source) => return Err(crate::DeadreckonError::Io { path, source }),
59	    };
60	    serde_json::from_slice(&raw).with_json_path(path).map(Some)
61	}
62	
63	pub fn write_receipt(paths: &DeadreckonPaths, receipt: &Receipt) -> Result<()> {
64	    let path = receipt_path(paths);
65	    if let Some(parent) = path.parent() {
66	        fs::create_dir_all(parent).with_path(parent)?;
67	    }
68	    let raw = serde_json::to_vec_pretty(receipt).with_json_path(&path)?;
69	    fs::write(&path, raw).with_path(path)
70	}
71	
72	#[must_use]
73	pub fn detect_channel(binary_path: &Path) -> Channel {
74	    let normalized = binary_path
75	        .to_string_lossy()
76	        .replace('\\', "/")
77	        .to_ascii_lowercase();
78	
79	    if normalized.contains("/node_modules/deadreckon/")
80	        || normalized.contains("/node_modules/deadreckon-")
81	    {
82	        return Channel::Npm;
83	    }
84	    if normalized.contains("/cellar/deadreckon/") {
85	        return Channel::Brew;
86	    }
87	    if normalized.contains("/.cargo/bin/deadreckon") {
88	        return Channel::Cargo;
89	    }
90	    if normalized.contains("/.local/share/deadreckon/")
91	        || normalized.contains("/appdata/local/deadreckon/")
92	    {
93	        return Channel::Shell;
94	    }
95	
96	    Channel::Source
97	}
98	
99	#[must_use]
100	pub fn detect_receipt(binary_path: &Path) -> Receipt {
101	    let channel = detect_channel(binary_path);
102	    Receipt {
103	        channel,
104	        channel_version: env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION").to_string(),
105	        binary_path: binary_path.to_path_buf(),
106	        installed_at: Utc::now(),
107	        install_source: Some("detected".to_string()),
108	        platform_package: (channel == Channel::Npm).then(platform_package_for_current),
109	        receipt_version: INSTALL_RECEIPT_VERSION,
110	    }
111	}
112	
113	#[must_use]
114	pub fn platform_package_for_current() -> String {
115	    platform_package_for(std::env::consts::OS, std::env::consts::ARCH)
116	        .unwrap_or_else(|| "deadreckon-unknown-unknown".to_string())
117	}
118	
119	#[must_use]
120	pub fn platform_package_for(os: &str, arch: &str) -> Option<String> {
121	    let os = match os {
122	        "macos" => "darwin",
123	        "linux" => "linux",
124	        "windows" => "win32",
125	        _ => return None,
126	    };
127	    let arch = match arch {
128	        "x86_64" | "x64" => "x64",
129	        "aarch64" | "arm64" => "arm64",
130	        _ => return None,
131	    };
132	    Some(format!("deadreckon-{os}-{arch}"))
133	}

23	    CliCodex,
24	    ScriptedSmoke,
25	    Generic(String),
26	}
27	
28	impl ProviderKind {
29	    pub fn as_config_str(&self) -> &str {
30	        match self {
31	            ProviderKind::Anthropic => "anthropic",
32	            ProviderKind::OpenAi => "open-ai",
33	            ProviderKind::OpenAiCompatible => "open-ai-compatible",
34	            ProviderKind::CliClaudeCode => "cli-claude-code",
35	            ProviderKind::CliCodex => "cli-codex",
36	            ProviderKind::ScriptedSmoke => "scripted-smoke",
37	            ProviderKind::Generic(id) => id,
38	        }
39	    }
40	}
41	
42	impl Serialize for ProviderKind {
43	    fn serialize<S>(&self, serializer: S) -> std::result::Result<S::Ok, S::Error>
44	    where
45	        S: Serializer,
46	    {
47	        serializer.serialize_str(self.as_config_str())
48	    }
49	}
50	
51	impl<'de> Deserialize<'de> for ProviderKind {
52	    fn deserialize<D>(deserializer: D) -> std::result::Result<Self, D::Error>
53	    where
54	        D: Deserializer<'de>,
55	    {
56	        let value = String::deserialize(deserializer)?;
57	        Ok(match value.as_str() {
58	            "anthropic" => ProviderKind::Anthropic,
59	            "open-ai" | "openai" => ProviderKind::OpenAi,
60	            "open-ai-compatible" | "openai-compatible" => ProviderKind::OpenAiCompatible,
61	            "cli-claude-code" | "cli:claude-code" => ProviderKind::CliClaudeCode,
62	            "cli-codex" | "cli:codex" => ProviderKind::CliCodex,
63	            "scripted-smoke" | "smoke" => ProviderKind::ScriptedSmoke,
64	            _ => ProviderKind::Generic(value),
65	        })
66	    }
67	}

12	pub struct ProviderAdapter {

14	    kind: ProviderKind,
15	    base_url: String,
16	    model: String,

22	
23	impl ProviderAdapter {
24	    pub fn new(name: impl Into<String>, kind: ProviderKind, entry: ProviderEntry) -> Self {
25	        let name = name.into();
26	        let api_key = entry
27	            .api_key
28	            .or_else(|| entry.api_key_env.as_deref().and_then(env_value));
29	        let base_url = entry.base_url.unwrap_or_else(|| default_base_url(&kind));
30	        let model = entry.model.unwrap_or_else(|| default_model(&kind));
31	        Self {
32	            name,
33	            kind,
34	            base_url,
35	            model,
36	            api_key,
37	            input_cost_per_million: entry.input_cost_per_million.unwrap_or(0.0),
38	            output_cost_per_million: entry.output_cost_per_million.unwrap_or(0.0),
39	            client: reqwest::Client::new(),
40	        }
41	    }
42	
43	    fn headers(&self) -> Result<HeaderMap> {
44	        let Some(api_key) = self.api_key.as_deref() else {
45	            return Err(ProviderError::MissingCredential(self.name.clone()));
46	        };
47	        let mut headers = HeaderMap::new();
48	        headers.insert(CONTENT_TYPE, HeaderValue::from_static("application/json"));
49	        match &self.kind {
50	            ProviderKind::Anthropic => {
51	                let key = HeaderValue::from_str(api_key).map_err(|err| {
52	                    ProviderError::InvalidConfig(format!("invalid Anthropic API key header: {err}"))
53	                })?;
54	                headers.insert("x-api-key", key);
55	                headers.insert("anthropic-version", HeaderValue::from_static("2023-06-01"));
56	            }
57	            ProviderKind::OpenAi | ProviderKind::OpenAiCompatible => {
58	                let bearer =
59	                    HeaderValue::from_str(&format!("Bearer {api_key}")).map_err(|err| {
60	                        ProviderError::InvalidConfig(format!("invalid bearer token header: {err}"))
61	                    })?;
62	                headers.insert(AUTHORIZATION, bearer);
63	            }
64	            ProviderKind::CliClaudeCode
65	            | ProviderKind::CliCodex
66	            | ProviderKind::ScriptedSmoke
67	            | ProviderKind::Generic(_) => {}
68	        }
69	        Ok(headers)
70	    }
71	
72	    fn endpoint(&self) -> String {
73	        match &self.kind {
74	            ProviderKind::Anthropic => {
75	                format!("{}/v1/messages", self.base_url.trim_end_matches('/'))
76	            }
77	            ProviderKind::OpenAi | ProviderKind::OpenAiCompatible => {
78	                format!("{}/chat/completions", self.base_url.trim_end_matches('/'))
79	            }
80	            ProviderKind::CliClaudeCode
81	            | ProviderKind::CliCodex
82	            | ProviderKind::ScriptedSmoke
83	            | ProviderKind::Generic(_) => {
84	                unreachable!("CLI providers do not use HTTP endpoints")
85	            }
86	        }
87	    }
88	
89	    fn payload(&self, request: &ProviderRequest) -> Value {
90	        match &self.kind {
91	            ProviderKind::Anthropic => json!({
92	                "model": self.model,
93	                "max_tokens": request.max_output_tokens,
94	                "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": request.prompt}],
95	            }),
96	            ProviderKind::OpenAi | ProviderKind::OpenAiCompatible => json!({
97	                "model": self.model,
98	                "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": request.prompt}],
99	                "max_tokens": request.max_output_tokens,
100	                "stream": false,
101	            }),
102	            ProviderKind::CliClaudeCode
103	            | ProviderKind::CliCodex
104	            | ProviderKind::ScriptedSmoke
105	            | ProviderKind::Generic(_) => {
106	                unreachable!("CLI providers do not use HTTP payloads")
107	            }
108	        }
109	    }
110	
111	    async fn send(&self, request: &ProviderRequest) -> Result<ProviderResponse> {
112	        let headers = self.headers()?;
113	        let request_future = self
114	            .client
115	            .post(self.endpoint())
116	            .headers(headers)
117	            .json(&self.payload(request))
118	            .send();
119	        let response = if let Some(token) = request.cancellation_token.as_ref() {
120	            tokio::select! {
121	                _ = token.cancelled() => {
122	                    return Err(ProviderError::Http {
123	                        provider: self.name.clone(),
124	                        detail: "request cancelled".to_string(),
125	                    });
126	                }
127	                response = request_future => response
128	            }
129	        } else {
130	            request_future.await
131	        }
132	        .map_err(|err| ProviderError::Http {
133	            provider: self.name.clone(),
134	            detail: err.to_string(),
135	        })?;
136	        let status = response.status();
137	        let body = response.text().await.map_err(|err| ProviderError::Http {
138	            provider: self.name.clone(),
139	            detail: err.to_string(),
140	        })?;
141	        if !status.is_success() {
142	            return Err(ProviderError::Http {
143	                provider: self.name.clone(),
144	                detail: format!("HTTP {status}: {}", trim_for_error(&body)),
145	            });
146	        }
147	        self.parse_response(&body)
148	    }
149	
150	    fn parse_response(&self, body: &str) -> Result<ProviderResponse> {
151	        let value: Value = serde_json::from_str(body).map_err(|err| ProviderError::Http {
152	            provider: self.name.clone(),
153	            detail: err.to_string(),
154	        })?;
155	        let (content, usage) = match &self.kind {
156	            ProviderKind::Anthropic => parse_anthropic_response(&value),
157	            ProviderKind::OpenAi | ProviderKind::OpenAiCompatible => parse_openai_response(&value),
158	            ProviderKind::CliClaudeCode
159	            | ProviderKind::CliCodex
160	            | ProviderKind::ScriptedSmoke
161	            | ProviderKind::Generic(_) => {
162	                unreachable!("CLI providers do not parse HTTP responses")
163	            }
164	        };
165	        let spend = self.estimate_spend(usage.clone());
166	        Ok(ProviderResponse {
167	            provider: self.name.clone(),
168	            model: self.model.clone(),
169	            content,
170	            usage,
171	            spend,
172	            trace: json!({"kind": "http_llm"}),
173	        })
174	    }
175	}
176	
177	impl Provider for ProviderAdapter {
178	    fn name(&self) -> &str {
179	        &self.name
180	    }
181	
182	    fn kind(&self) -> ProviderKind {
183	        self.kind.clone()
184	    }
185	
186	    fn model(&self) -> &str {
187	        &self.model
188	    }
189	
190	    fn has_credential(&self) -> bool {
191	        self.api_key.as_deref().is_some_and(|key| !key.is_empty())
192	    }
193	
194	    fn estimate_spend(&self, usage: ProviderUsage) -> SpendEstimate {
195	        let input = usage.input_tokens as f64 / 1_000_000.0 * self.input_cost_per_million;
196	        let output = usage.output_tokens as f64 / 1_000_000.0 * self.output_cost_per_million;
197	        SpendEstimate {
198	            provider: self.name.clone(),
199	            model: self.model.clone(),
200	            input_tokens: usage.input_tokens,
201	            output_tokens: usage.output_tokens,
202	            cost_usd: round_usd(input + output),
203	            subscription: false,
204	            wall_time_seconds: None,
205	        }
206	    }
207	
208	    fn complete<'a>(&'a self, request: &'a ProviderRequest) -> ProviderFuture<'a> {
209	        Box::pin(async move { self.send(request).await })
210	    }
211	}
212	
213	fn env_value(name: &str) -> Option<String> {
214	    env::var(name).ok().filter(|value| !value.trim().is_empty())
215	}
216	
217	fn default_base_url(kind: &ProviderKind) -> String {
218	    match kind {
219	        ProviderKind::Anthropic => "https://api.anthropic.com".to_string(),
220	        ProviderKind::OpenAi => "https://api.openai.com/v1".to_string(),
221	        ProviderKind::OpenAiCompatible => "http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1".to_string(),
222	        ProviderKind::CliClaudeCode
223	        | ProviderKind::CliCodex
224	        | ProviderKind::ScriptedSmoke
225	        | ProviderKind::Generic(_) => String::new(),
226	    }
227	}
228	
229	fn default_model(kind: &ProviderKind) -> String {
230	    match kind {
231	        ProviderKind::Anthropic => "claude-sonnet-4-5".to_string(),
232	        ProviderKind::OpenAi => "gpt-5.1-codex".to_string(),
233	        ProviderKind::OpenAiCompatible => "local-model".to_string(),
234	        ProviderKind::CliClaudeCode => "cli:claude-code".to_string(),
235	        ProviderKind::CliCodex => "cli:codex".to_string(),
236	        ProviderKind::ScriptedSmoke => "local-scripted-smoke".to_string(),
237	        ProviderKind::Generic(id) => id.clone(),
238	    }
239	}
240	
241	fn parse_openai_response(value: &Value) -> (String, ProviderUsage) {
242	    let content = value
243	        .pointer("/choices/0/message/content")
244	        .and_then(Value::as_str)
245	        .unwrap_or_default()
246	        .to_string();
247	    let usage = ProviderUsage {
248	        input_tokens: value
249	            .pointer("/usage/prompt_tokens")
250	            .and_then(Value::as_u64)
251	            .unwrap_or(0),
252	        output_tokens: value
253	            .pointer("/usage/completion_tokens")
254	            .and_then(Value::as_u64)
255	            .unwrap_or(0),
256	    };
257	    (content, usage)
258	}
259	
260	fn parse_anthropic_response(value: &Value) -> (String, ProviderUsage) {
261	    let content = value
262	        .pointer("/content/0/text")
263	        .and_then(Value::as_str)
264	        .unwrap_or_default()
265	        .to_string();
266	    let usage = ProviderUsage {
267	        input_tokens: value
268	            .pointer("/usage/input_tokens")
269	            .and_then(Value::as_u64)
270	            .unwrap_or(0),
271	        output_tokens: value
272	            .pointer("/usage/output_tokens")
273	            .and_then(Value::as_u64)
274	            .unwrap_or(0),
275	    };
276	    (content, usage)
277	}
278	
279	fn trim_for_error(body: &str) -> String {
280	    const MAX: usize = 240;
281	    if body.len() <= MAX {
282	        body.to_string()
283	    } else {
284	        format!("{}...", &body[..MAX])
285	    }
286	}

288	fn round_usd(value: f64) -> f64 {

290	}

2	
3	use crate::cli_claude_code::CliClaudeCodeProvider;
4	use crate::cli_codex::CliCodexProvider;
5	use crate::cli_generic::GenericCliProvider;
6	use crate::config::{
7	    kind_from_name, merge_provider_entry, provider_entries_from_registry, read_config,
8	};
9	use crate::http::ProviderAdapter;
10	use crate::registry::{DescriptorKind, ProviderRegistry};
11	use crate::smoke::ScriptedSmokeProvider;
12	use crate::{
13	    Provider, ProviderConfigFile, ProviderEntry, ProviderError, ProviderKind, ProviderRequest,
14	    ProviderResponse, ProviderRouteInfo, ProviderUsage, Result, SpendEstimate,
15	};
16	
17	pub struct ProviderRouter {
18	    routes: Vec<Box<dyn Provider>>,
19	}
20	
21	impl ProviderRouter {
22	    pub fn smoke() -> Self {
23	        Self {
24	            routes: vec![Box::new(ScriptedSmokeProvider::new())],
25	        }
26	    }
27	
28	    pub fn from_config_path(path: &Path, override_provider: Option<&str>) -> Result<Self> {
29	        Self::from_config_path_with_model(path, override_provider, None)
30	    }
31	
32	    pub fn from_config_path_with_model(
33	        path: &Path,
34	        override_provider: Option<&str>,
35	        override_model: Option<&str>,
36	    ) -> Result<Self> {
37	        // REPORT.md: Provider Routing / BYOK keeps credentials in the user's
38	        // local config/env and tries the configured fallback chain.
39	        let config = read_config(path)?;
40	        let registry = path
41	            .parent()
42	            .map(ProviderRegistry::with_overrides)
43	            .transpose()?
44	            .unwrap_or(ProviderRegistry::builtin()?);
45	        Self::from_config_with_model_and_registry(
46	            config,
47	            override_provider,
48	            override_model,
49	            &registry,
50	        )
51	    }
52	
53	    pub fn from_config(
54	        config: ProviderConfigFile,
55	        override_provider: Option<&str>,
56	    ) -> Result<Self> {
57	        Self::from_config_with_model(config, override_provider, None)
58	    }
59	
60	    pub fn from_config_with_model(
61	        config: ProviderConfigFile,
62	        override_provider: Option<&str>,
63	        override_model: Option<&str>,
64	    ) -> Result<Self> {
65	        let registry = ProviderRegistry::builtin()?;
66	        Self::from_config_with_model_and_registry(
67	            config,
68	            override_provider,
69	            override_model,
70	            &registry,
71	        )
72	    }
73	
74	    fn from_config_with_model_and_registry(
75	        config: ProviderConfigFile,
76	        override_provider: Option<&str>,
77	        override_model: Option<&str>,
78	        registry: &ProviderRegistry,
79	    ) -> Result<Self> {
80	        let mut providers = provider_entries_from_registry(registry);
81	        for (name, entry) in config.providers {
82	            if let Some(base) = providers.get_mut(&name) {
83	                merge_provider_entry(base, entry);
84	            } else {
85	                providers.insert(name, entry);
86	            }
87	        }
88	
89	        let route_names = if let Some(provider) = override_provider {
90	            vec![provider.to_string()]
91	        } else {
92	            configured_route_names(config.default_provider, config.fallback)
93	        };
94	
95	        let mut routes = Vec::new();
96	        for name in route_names {
97	            let Some(mut entry) = providers.remove(&name) else {
98	                return Err(ProviderError::InvalidConfig(format!(
99	                    "unknown provider route {name}"
100	                )));
101	            };
102	            if let Some(model) = override_model {
103	                entry.model = Some(model.to_string());
104	            }
105	            let kind = entry.kind.unwrap_or_else(|| kind_from_name(&name));
106	            entry.kind = Some(kind.clone());
107	            routes.push(build_provider(name, kind, entry, registry)?);
108	        }
109	
110	        Ok(Self { routes })
111	    }
112	
113	    pub fn routes(&self) -> &[Box<dyn Provider>] {
114	        &self.routes
115	    }
116	
117	    pub fn route_info(&self) -> Vec<ProviderRouteInfo> {
118	        self.routes
119	            .iter()
120	            .map(|route| ProviderRouteInfo {
121	                name: route.name().to_string(),
122	                kind: route.kind(),
123	                model: route.model().to_string(),
124	                has_credential: route.has_credential(),
125	            })
126	            .collect()
127	    }
128	
129	    pub fn selected_route_info(&self) -> Option<ProviderRouteInfo> {
130	        let routes = self.route_info();
131	        routes
132	            .iter()
133	            .find(|route| route.has_credential)
134	            .cloned()
135	            .or_else(|| routes.into_iter().next())
136	    }
137	
138	    pub async fn complete(&self, request: &ProviderRequest) -> Result<ProviderResponse> {
139	        let mut failures = Vec::new();
140	        for route in &self.routes {
141	            if !route.has_credential() {
142	                failures.push(format!("{}: missing credential", route.name()));
143	                continue;
144	            }
145	            match route.complete(request).await {
146	                Ok(response) => return Ok(response),
147	                Err(err) => failures.push(format!("{}: {err}", route.name())),
148	            }
149	        }
150	        Err(ProviderError::NoRoute(failures.join("; ")))
151	    }
152	
153	    pub fn estimate_for_route(
154	        &self,
155	        provider_name: Option<&str>,
156	        usage: ProviderUsage,
157	    ) -> Result<SpendEstimate> {
158	        let route = provider_name
159	            .and_then(|name| self.routes.iter().find(|route| route.name() == name))
160	            .or_else(|| self.routes.first())
161	            .ok_or_else(|| ProviderError::NoRoute("empty provider route".to_string()))?;
162	        Ok(route.estimate_spend(usage))
163	    }
164	}
165	
166	fn configured_route_names(
167	    default_provider: Option<String>,
168	    fallback: Option<Vec<String>>,
169	) -> Vec<String> {
170	    let mut route_names = Vec::new();
171	    if let Some(default_provider) = default_provider {
172	        route_names.push(default_provider);
173	    }
174	    if let Some(fallback) = fallback {
175	        for provider in fallback {
176	            if !route_names.iter().any(|route| route == &provider) {
177	                route_names.push(provider);
178	            }
179	        }
180	    }
181	    if route_names.is_empty() {
182	        route_names.extend([
183	            "cli:claude-code".to_string(),
184	            "cli:codex".to_string(),
185	            "anthropic".to_string(),
186	            "openai".to_string(),
187	            "openai-compatible".to_string(),
188	        ]);
189	    }
190	    route_names
191	}
192	
193	fn build_provider(
194	    name: String,
195	    kind: ProviderKind,
196	    entry: ProviderEntry,
197	    registry: &ProviderRegistry,
198	) -> Result<Box<dyn Provider>> {
199	    match kind {
200	        ProviderKind::CliClaudeCode => Ok(Box::new(CliClaudeCodeProvider::new(name, entry))),
201	        ProviderKind::CliCodex => Ok(Box::new(CliCodexProvider::new(name, entry))),
202	        ProviderKind::ScriptedSmoke => Ok(Box::new(ScriptedSmokeProvider::new())),
203	        ProviderKind::Anthropic | ProviderKind::OpenAi | ProviderKind::OpenAiCompatible => {
204	            Ok(Box::new(ProviderAdapter::new(name, kind, entry)))
205	        }
206	        ProviderKind::Generic(id) => {
207	            let descriptor = registry
208	                .get(&id)
209	                .or_else(|| registry.get(&name))
210	                .ok_or_else(|| {
211	                    ProviderError::InvalidConfig(format!("generic provider {id} has no descriptor"))
212	                })?;
213	            if descriptor.kind != DescriptorKind::Cli {
214	                return Err(ProviderError::InvalidConfig(format!(
215	                    "generic provider {id} is not a cli descriptor"
216	                )));
217	            }
218	            Ok(Box::new(GenericCliProvider::new(
219	                name,
220	                entry,
221	                descriptor.clone(),
222	            )?))
223	        }
224	    }
225	}

545	
546	## 8. Atomic Promotion & the Library
547	
548	### 8.1 `PromotionManifest`
549	
550	`crates/deadreckon-core/src/promotion.rs:14-23`:
551	
552	```rust
553	pub struct PromotionManifest {
554	    pub schema_version: u32,
555	    pub run_id: String,
556	    pub scope: String,
557	    pub goal: String,
558	    pub promoted_at: DateTime<Utc>,
559	    pub source_working_dir: PathBuf,
560	    pub provenance_hash: String,   // hash of provenance.jsonl bytes
561	}
562	```
563	
564	### 8.2 Promotion flow
565	
566	`promotion.rs:25-63`:
567	
568	1. **Guard.** `validate_acceptance_marker(state)?` — refuses if marker missing / wrong run_id / unsigned.
569	2. **Recovery.** `recover_promotion()` — idempotent if a previous attempt half-completed (§8.4).
570	3. **Idempotency check.** If `library/<scope>/<run_id>/manifest.json` already exists, update state and return — no work to do.
571	4. **Staging.** Create `library/<scope>/.{run_id}.promoting/` (parent dir created if needed).
572	5. **Move.** `fs::rename(working_dir, staging)` — atomic on same filesystem.
573	6. **Manifest.** Write `manifest.json` inside staging.
574	7. **Final rename.** `fs::rename(staging, library/<scope>/<run_id>/)` — atomic.
575	8. **State update.** `state.working_dir = library_dir`; `state.promoted_library_dir = Some(library_dir)`; `save_state()`.
576	
577	### 8.3 Where promotion happens
578	
579	In `crates/deadreckon-runtime/src/turn_loop.rs`, **before** `set_phase_status(PhaseId(60), Completed)`. If promotion fails, the run never reaches `Completed`. The `working/` directory is the source of truth until promotion; after promotion, the library copy is canonical and `working/` is gone.
580	
581	### 8.4 Crash recovery between rename steps
582	
583	`promotion.rs:65-84` handles the half-completed states:
584	
585	- If `staging` exists and final dir doesn't: complete the rename.
586	- If both exist: the final rename happened but didn't atomically remove staging; clean up staging.
587	- If final dir exists but its `manifest.json` is missing: write the manifest.
588	
589	This makes promotion crash-safe across a `kill -9` between the two renames.
590	
591	---
592	
593	## 9. The Turn Loop
594	
595	The load-bearing function lives in `/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon-runtime/src/turn_loop.rs`.
596	
597	### 9.1 `RunLoopConfig`
598	
599	`crates/deadreckon-runtime/src/turn_loop.rs` defines:
600

603	    pub provider: Option<String>,
604	    pub max_spend_usd: Option<f64>,
605	    pub max_wall_seconds: Option<f64>,
606	    pub sandbox_backend: SandboxBackend,
607	    pub max_turns: u32,             // hard cap, currently 12
608	    pub from_turn: Option<u32>,     // resume override
609	    pub event_sender: Option<broadcast::Sender<RunEvent>>,
610	    pub cancellation_token: Option<CancellationToken>,
611	}
612	```
613	
614	### 9.2 Top-level signature

616	The top-level signature is:
617	
618	```rust
619	pub async fn run_turn_loop(
620	    state: &mut PipelineState,
621	    router: &ProviderRouter,
622	    config: RunLoopConfig,
623	) -> Result<RunLoopOutcome>
624	```
625	
626	### 9.3 Loop body (paraphrased; see `crates/deadreckon-runtime/src/turn_loop.rs`)
627	
628	```text
629	load_or_reconstruct_history()      # lines 69, 550-631
630	set Phase(40)=Executing            # line 70
631	save_state(); save_history()       # line 71
632

1389	## 20. Testing Strategy
1390	
1391	### 20.1 Test locations
1392	
1393	- `crates/deadreckon-providers/tests/cli_providers.rs` (297 lines) — CLI provider routing, fake `claude`/`codex` binaries, output capture, spend.
1394	- `crates/deadreckon-providers/tests/mock_server.rs` (220 lines) — axum-based OpenAI-compatible mock for HTTP provider tests.
1395	- `crates/deadreckon-providers/src/lib.rs` (inline) and focused module tests — config parsing, spend math, credential check, smoke determinism.
1396	- `crates/deadreckon/tests/agentic_loop.rs` (841 lines) — end-to-end: run, kill, resume, list, attach, import, doctor, stress.
1397	
1398	### 20.2 Notable integration tests
1399	
1400	| Test (in `agentic_loop.rs`) | What it proves |
1401	|---|---|
1402	| `mock_provider_records_three_turns_and_artifacts_match` (line 19) | mock-driven run produces 3 turns, ≥ 5 trace lines, 3 spend lines, signed acceptance marker, working files |
1403	| `kill_mid_turn_sets_killed_and_stops_process` (line 65) | kill interrupts within 2 s, sets `Killed` |
1404	| `resume_preserves_history_file` (line 103) | resume preserves `history.json` tool_call_ids |
1405	| `cli_subagent_without_file_changes_fails_run` (line 134) | CLI provider with no file effects → `Failed` |
1406	| `init_config_and_default_spend_work` (line 180) | `init` writes config; `config get/set` works; `--smoke` respects defaults |
1407	| `high_spend_requires_confirmation_flag_in_scripts` (line 246) | `--max-spend 51` without `--i-know-its-a-lot` fails with a hint |
1408	| `cli_wall_clock_budget_enforced` (line 266) | subscription run pauses at `--max-wall-seconds` cap |
1409	| `kill_storm_no_leaks` (line 334) | 10 concurrent kills release all PIDs + locks |
1410	| `doctor_fails_actionably` (line 408) | `doctor` output contains specific fix commands |
1411	| `import_*` focused cases (lines 425+) | descriptor-backed import normalizes CLI/Cursor histories, writes manifests, refuses ambiguous/changed imports, and preserves preview/list no-write behavior |
1412	| `stress_5_concurrent_10min` (line 470, gated `DEADRECKON_STRESS=1`) | 5 concurrent scoped runs complete cleanly |
1413	
1414	### 20.3 Verification gates
1415	
1416	Every commit is expected to leave the workspace green on:
1417	
1418	```zsh
1419	cargo build --release
1420	cargo test --workspace
1421	cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings
1422	cargo fmt --check
1423	```
1424	
1425	---
1426	
1427	## 21. Key Design Decisions
1428	
1429	1. **No new `PipelineState` fields without a strong reason.** Parent lineage, materialization status, and other run-level metadata live in files inside the working tree (e.g., `.deadreckon/parent.json`), not on the state struct. This keeps `state.json` migration-safe.
1430	
1431	2. **Two-layer split is non-negotiable.** Skills (Markdown) own judgment; the binary owns invariants. A skill cannot bypass the gate; a gate cannot read prompts.
1432	
1433	3. **Anti-self-attestation via a nonce only `dr-gate` reads.** The agent can produce any output it wants; it cannot produce a valid `AcceptanceMarker.signature` because it never sees `gate/nonce`.
1434	
1435	4. **Atomic promotion before completion.** `Completed` is set only after the library swap succeeds. If promotion fails, the run fails. This means a `Completed` status always implies a durable artifact in `library/`.
1436	
1437	5. **Platform-native sandboxing.** No Docker daemon dependency. Seatbelt on macOS, bwrap on Linux. Docker is opt-in. The "running on host machine feels like a bad idea" pain point is solved without forcing Docker.
1438	
1439	6. **BYOK extends to subscriptions.** `cli:claude-code` and `cli:codex` are first-class providers, not afterthoughts. Most users will run deadreckon via subscription, not API keys.
1440	
1441	7. **Phase numbering with gaps (0, 10, 20, …).** Future phases can be inserted (e.g., a phase 15 for plan refinement) without rewriting durable state.
1442	
1443	8. **Append-only telemetry.** `spend.jsonl`, `traces.jsonl`, `provenance.jsonl`, `events.jsonl` are immutable audit trails. The TUI and `show` command read them; nothing rewrites them.
1444	
1445	9. **The smoke provider is a real provider.** `--smoke` selects `ScriptedSmokeProvider`, which goes through the same `ProviderRouter::complete` path. There is no separate "smoke turn loop" — the loop is always the loop.
1446	
1447	10. **PID-aware locks with stale reclaim.** A crashed deadreckon process can be detected (its lock holder PID is dead via `kill(pid, 0)`); the next run reclaims the lock. No external lock daemon.
1448	
1449	---
1450	
1451	## 22. What's Built vs Scaffolding-Thin
1452	
1453	The codebase is more complete than a typical first pass, and the 2026-05-11 hardening pass replaced the earlier thin seams with depth-tested implementations where those seams were in alpha scope. Honest accounting per `docs/CHANGELOG.md`, `docs/GAP-ANALYSIS.md`, and `docs/AUDIT-2026-05-11.md`:
1454	
1455	### Built and reliable
1456	
1457	- Workspace, crates, build, lint, fmt, test discipline.
1458	- Workspace lint discipline (deny-tier clippy + rustc), tuned release profile, registry-shaped library `lib.rs`, library print refusal, and error retryable/fatal taxonomy as vocabulary for future watchdog work.
```

373	
374	fn probe_cli_descriptor(descriptor: &ProviderDescriptor) -> ProviderProbeResult {
375	    let Some(binary) = descriptor.default_binary.as_deref() else {
376	        return base_probe_result(
377	            descriptor,
378	            ProbeStatus::Failed,
379	            None,
380	            None,
381	            "missing",
382	            Some(ProbeErrorKind::NotFound),
383	            Some("no default binary configured".to_string()),
384	        );
385	    };
386	    let Some(location) = resolve_binary(binary) else {
387	        return base_probe_result(
388	            descriptor,
389	            ProbeStatus::Failed,
390	            Some(binary.to_string()),
391	            None,
392	            "missing",
393	            Some(ProbeErrorKind::NotFound),
394	            Some(format!("{binary} not on PATH")),
395	        );
396	    };
397	    if let Some(probe) = descriptor.version_probe.as_ref()
398	        && !probe.args.is_empty()
399	    {
400	        match Command::new(&location).args(&probe.args).output() {
401	            Ok(output) => {
402	                if !output.status.success() {
403	                    let stderr = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr);
404	                    return base_probe_result(
405	                        descriptor,
406	                        ProbeStatus::Failed,
407	                        Some(location.display().to_string()),
408	                        None,
409	                        "missing",
410	                        Some(ProbeErrorKind::ProbeFailed),
411	                        Some(trim_probe_message(&stderr)),
412	                    );
413	                }
414	                let version = trim_probe_message(&format!(
415	                    "{}{}",
416	                    String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout),
417	                    String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr)
418	                ));
419	                if let Some(expected) = probe.expect_substring.as_deref()
420	                    && !version.contains(expected)
421	                {
422	                    return base_probe_result(
423	                        descriptor,
424	                        ProbeStatus::Failed,
425	                        Some(location.display().to_string()),
426	                        Some(version),
427	                        "missing",
428	                        Some(ProbeErrorKind::VersionMismatch),
429	                        Some(format!("version output did not contain {expected}")),
430	                    );
431	                }
432	                if let Some(min) = probe.min_known_good.as_deref()
433	                    && !version_at_least(&version, min)
434	                {
435	                    return base_probe_result(
436	                        descriptor,
437	                        ProbeStatus::Failed,
438	                        Some(location.display().to_string()),
439	                        Some(version),
440	                        "missing",
441	                        Some(ProbeErrorKind::VersionMismatch),
442	                        Some(format!("version below known-good {min}")),
443	                    );
444	                }
445	                return base_probe_result(
446	                    descriptor,
447	                    ProbeStatus::Ok,
448	                    Some(location.display().to_string()),
449	                    Some(version),
450	                    "ready",
451	                    None,
452	                    None,
453	                );
454	            }
455	            Err(source) if source.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::PermissionDenied => {
456	                return base_probe_result(
457	                    descriptor,
458	                    ProbeStatus::Failed,
459	                    Some(location.display().to_string()),
460	                    None,
461	                    "missing",
462	                    Some(ProbeErrorKind::PermissionDenied),
463	                    Some(format!("permission denied running {binary}")),
464	                );
465	            }
466	            Err(source) => {
467	                return base_probe_result(
468	                    descriptor,
469	                    ProbeStatus::Failed,
470	                    Some(location.display().to_string()),
471	                    None,
472	                    "missing",
473	                    Some(ProbeErrorKind::ProbeFailed),
474	                    Some(source.to_string()),
475	                );
476	            }
477	        }
478	    }
479	    base_probe_result(
480	        descriptor,
481	        ProbeStatus::Ok,
482	        Some(location.display().to_string()),
483	        None,
484	        "ready",
485	        None,
486	        None,
487	    )
488	}

554	async fn ping_endpoint(descriptor: &ProviderDescriptor) -> ProviderProbeResult {
555	    let endpoint = descriptor.default_endpoint.clone().unwrap_or_default();
556	    let client = match reqwest::Client::builder()
557	        .timeout(Duration::from_secs(2))
558	        .build()
559	    {
560	        Ok(client) => client,
561	        Err(source) => {
562	            return base_probe_result(
563	                descriptor,
564	                ProbeStatus::Failed,
565	                Some(endpoint),
566	                None,
567	                "missing",
568	                Some(ProbeErrorKind::ProbeFailed),
569	                Some(source.to_string()),
570	            );
571	        }
572	    };
573	    match client.get(&endpoint).send().await {
574	        Ok(response) => base_probe_result(
575	            descriptor,
576	            ProbeStatus::Ok,
577	            Some(endpoint),
578	            Some(format!("HTTP {}", response.status())),
579	            "ready",
580	            None,
581	            None,
582	        ),
583	        Err(source) => base_probe_result(
584	            descriptor,
585	            ProbeStatus::Failed,
586	            Some(endpoint),
587	            None,
588	            "missing",
589	            Some(ProbeErrorKind::EndpointUnreachable),
590	            Some(source.to_string()),
591	        ),
592	    }
593	}

629	fn resolve_binary(binary: &str) -> Option<PathBuf> {
630	    let configured = PathBuf::from(binary);
631	    if configured.components().count() > 1 || configured.is_absolute() {
632	        return configured.exists().then_some(configured);
633	    }
634	    which::which(binary).ok()

637	fn expand_home_path(path: &Path) -> PathBuf {
638	    let Some(home) = std::env::var_os("HOME").map(PathBuf::from) else {
639	        return path.to_path_buf();
640	    };
641	    if path == Path::new("~") {
642	        return home;
643	    }
644	    if let Ok(rest) = path.strip_prefix("~") {
645	        return home.join(rest);
646	    }
647	    path.to_path_buf()
648	}

650	fn trim_probe_message(message: &str) -> String {
651	    let first_line = message
652	        .lines()
653	        .find(|line| !line.trim().is_empty())
654	        .unwrap_or("");
655	    let trimmed = first_line.trim();
656	    if trimmed.len() > 120 {
657	        format!("{}...", &trimmed[..120])
658	    } else {
659	        trimmed.to_string()
660	    }
661	}

663	fn version_at_least(output: &str, minimum: &str) -> bool {
664	    let observed = first_version_tuple(output);
665	    let required = first_version_tuple(minimum);
666	    if observed.is_empty() || required.is_empty() {
667	        return output >= minimum;
668	    }
669	    compare_version_tuples(&observed, &required) != std::cmp::Ordering::Less
670	}
671	
672	fn first_version_tuple(text: &str) -> Vec<u64> {
673	    text.split(|ch: char| !ch.is_ascii_digit() && ch != '.')
674	        .find(|part| part.chars().any(|ch| ch.is_ascii_digit()))
675	        .unwrap_or("")
676	        .split('.')
677	        .filter_map(|part| part.parse::<u64>().ok())
678	        .collect()
679	}
680	
681	fn compare_version_tuples(left: &[u64], right: &[u64]) -> std::cmp::Ordering {
682	    let len = left.len().max(right.len());
683	    for index in 0..len {
684	        let l = left.get(index).copied().unwrap_or(0);
685	        let r = right.get(index).copied().unwrap_or(0);
686	        match l.cmp(&r) {
687	            std::cmp::Ordering::Equal => {}
688	            ordering => return ordering,
689	        }
690	    }
691	    std::cmp::Ordering::Equal
692	}
693	
694	fn split_command_line(command: &str) -> Vec<String> {
695	    let mut args = Vec::new();
696	    let mut current = String::new();
697	    let mut quote = None::<char>;
698	    let mut escaped = false;
699	    for ch in command.chars() {
700	        if escaped {
701	            current.push(ch);
702	            escaped = false;
703	            continue;
704	        }
705	        if ch == '\\' {
706	            escaped = true;
707	            continue;
708	        }
709	        if let Some(active_quote) = quote {
710	            if ch == active_quote {
711	                quote = None;
712	            } else {
713	                current.push(ch);
714	            }
715	            continue;
716	        }
717	        match ch {
718	            '"' | '\'' => quote = Some(ch),
719	            ' ' | '\t' | '\n' => {
720	                if !current.is_empty() {
721	                    args.push(current.clone());
722	                    current.clear();
723	                }
724	            }
725	            _ => current.push(ch),
726	        }
727	    }
728	    if !current.is_empty() {
729	        args.push(current);
730	    }
731	    args
732	}

778	fn merge_values(base: &mut Value, override_value: Value) {
779	    match (base, override_value) {
780	        (Value::Table(base_table), Value::Table(override_table)) => {
781	            for (key, value) in override_table {
782	                match base_table.get_mut(&key) {
783	                    Some(base_value) => merge_values(base_value, value),
784	                    None => {
785	                        base_table.insert(key, value);
786	                    }
787	                }
788	            }
789	        }
790	        (base_value, override_value) => *base_value = override_value,
791	    }
792	}

100	    fn render_args(&self, request: &ProviderRequest) -> Vec<String> {
101	        let mut args: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
102	        let mut inserted_model = false;
103	        let mut inserted_extra = false;
104	        for part in &self.descriptor.exec_template.args_template {
105	            if part == "{prompt}" {
106	                if args
107	                    .last()
108	                    .is_some_and(|arg| prompt_value_flag_requires_next_arg(arg))
109	                {
110	                    if let Some(prompt_flag) = args.pop() {
111	                        self.push_model_arg(&mut args, &mut inserted_model);
112	                        self.push_extra_args(&mut args, &mut inserted_extra);
113	                        args.push(prompt_flag);
114	                    }
115	                } else {
116	                    self.push_model_arg(&mut args, &mut inserted_model);
117	                    self.push_extra_args(&mut args, &mut inserted_extra);
118	                }
119	                args.push(request.prompt.clone());
120	                continue;
121	            }
122	            args.push(render_template_part(part, request));
123	        }
124	        self.push_model_arg(&mut args, &mut inserted_model);
125	        self.push_extra_args(&mut args, &mut inserted_extra);
126	        args
127	    }

```text
1867	## 29. Workspace Hygiene
1868	
1869	### 29.1 Centralized Lints
1870	
1871	The root `Cargo.toml` owns `[workspace.lints]` for Rust and clippy policy. Every crate inherits it with `[lints] workspace = true`, so deny-tier rules such as `unsafe_code`, `unused_must_use`, `unwrap_used`, `expect_used`, `await_holding_lock`, `redundant_clone`, `needless_borrow`, and the `manual_*` family are enforced from one place. `clippy.toml` keeps test ergonomics explicit with test-only unwrap/expect/dbg exemptions and a `large-error-threshold = 256`.
1872	
1873	### 29.2 Formatted Imports
1874	
1875	`rustfmt.toml` pins edition `2024`, import reordering, `imports_granularity = "Item"`, and `group_imports = "StdExternalCrate"`. Stable rustfmt currently warns that the last two knobs are nightly-only, but `cargo fmt --check` still exits cleanly and the guard tests ensure the config remains intentional.
1876	
1877	### 29.3 Tuned Profiles
1878	
1879	`[profile.release]` uses fat LTO, one codegen unit, symbol stripping, and `split-debuginfo = "off"` while keeping the pre-existing panic behavior explicit with `panic = "unwind"`. `[profile.dev] debug = "limited"` keeps local compiles lighter without changing runtime behavior.
1880	
1881	### 29.4 Internal Crate Routing
1882	
1883	The four internal libraries (`deadreckon-core`, `deadreckon-runtime`, `deadreckon-providers`, `deadreckon-sandbox`) are declared in root `[workspace.dependencies]`. Member crates depend on them through `{ workspace = true }`, which keeps the internal dependency graph centralized and lets metadata tests detect accidental raw `../` path dependencies.
1884	
1885	### 29.5 Registry-Shaped Library Roots
1886	
1887	Every library `lib.rs` is a registry: crate docs, sorted `mod` declarations, sorted `pub mod` declarations, and sorted `pub use` re-exports. Business logic, `impl` blocks, and helper functions live in real modules. Public re-export set tests guard the pre-rider surface.
1888	
1889	### 29.6 Library Print Refusal
1890	
1891	Library crate roots deny `clippy::print_stdout` and `clippy::print_stderr`. User-facing output remains the responsibility of the `deadreckon` binary crate, where formatted CLI/TUI output belongs.
1892	
1893	### 29.7 Error Taxonomy
1894	
1895	`DeadreckonError`, `ProviderError`, and `SandboxError` expose exhaustive `is_retryable()` and `is_fatal()` methods. I/O interruptions, timeouts, reset/aborted connections, broken pipes, and held locks are retryable; schema, config, credential, routing, invalid-input, not-found, CLI, sandbox, cancellation, and status-less HTTP errors are fatal. These methods are vocabulary only in this pass; watchdog wiring remains a future behavior change.
1896	
1897	### 29.8 Behavior Invariants
1898	
1899	`tests/smoke_invariant.rs` protects the smoke-run narrative hash, and `tests/public_surface.rs` protects the public library re-export set. `tests/hygiene_config.rs` adds targeted guards for lints, formatting config, profile settings, internal dependency routing, registry shape, print refusal, binary size, cargo metadata stability, and error taxonomy.
1900	
1901	---
1902	
1903	## 30. Plans & Multi-Agent Orchestration
1904	
1905	### 30.1 Mental Model
1906	
1907	An orchestration plan is a file-backed task graph under `~/.deadreckon/plans/<plan-id>/`. It does not add fields to `PipelineState`; child work is still executed by normal `deadreckon run` subprocesses. The coordinator process owns only plan files: `plan.json`, `coordinator.json` while live, `messages.jsonl`, worker specs, child summaries, merge working state, and merge proofs.
1908	
1909	Two modes are built:
1910	
1911	- `full-plan`: `deadreckon orchestrate full-plan <goal>` or `deadreckon plan <goal> --mode full-plan --n <2..=6>` asks a read-only planner provider for task JSON, records planner/default-child/per-child providers, writes worker specs, and later `fork` starts independent ready tasks as a concurrent batch. Planner output must contain exactly the requested task count; single-task decompositions and values outside `2..=6` are refused before `plan.json` is saved.
1912	- `review`: `deadreckon orchestrate review <goal> --coder-provider <id> --reviewer-provider <id>` writes a coder task and a reviewer task. The reviewer is launched with `deadreckon extend <coder-run-id> ...` after the coder completes, so parent history and `extended_from_parent` trace lineage are preserved.
1913	
1914	### 30.2 Plan Files
1915	
1916	`crates/deadreckon-core/src/plan.rs` defines `Plan`, `PlanTask`, `PlanProviders`, `PlanMessage`, `PlanEvent`, `PlanChildMarker`, and `CoordinatorState`. The durable layout is:
1917	
1918	```text
1919	~/.deadreckon/plans/<plan-id>/
1920	  plan.json
1921	  coordinator.json          # present only while fork is supervising
1922	  messages.jsonl
1923	  plan-events.jsonl
1924	  docs/PLAN-NARRATIVE.md
1925	  worker-specs/task-0.md
1926	  summaries/task-0.md
```
</details></tool-use>

18	
19	impl SandboxError {
20	    /// Transient — the operation may succeed on a retry.
21	    pub fn is_retryable(&self) -> bool {
22	        match self {
23	            SandboxError::InvalidBackend(_) => false,
24	            SandboxError::Unavailable(_) => false,
25	            SandboxError::Io(source) => is_retryable_io_kind(source.kind()),
26	            SandboxError::Cancelled => false,
27	        }
28	    }
29	
30	    /// Unrecoverable — the watchdog should escalate, not retry.
31	    pub fn is_fatal(&self) -> bool {
32	        match self {
33	            SandboxError::InvalidBackend(_) => true,
34	            SandboxError::Unavailable(_) => true,
35	            SandboxError::Io(source) => !is_retryable_io_kind(source.kind()),
36	            SandboxError::Cancelled => true,
37	        }
38	    }
39	}
40	
41	fn is_retryable_io_kind(kind: std::io::ErrorKind) -> bool {
42	    matches!(
43	        kind,
44	        std::io::ErrorKind::Interrupted
45	            | std::io::ErrorKind::WouldBlock
46	            | std::io::ErrorKind::TimedOut
47	            | std::io::ErrorKind::ConnectionReset
48	            | std::io::ErrorKind::ConnectionAborted
49	            | std::io::ErrorKind::BrokenPipe
50	    )
51	}

60	    Bwrap,

62	    None,

65	impl fmt::Display for SandboxBackend {
66	    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
67	        let value = match self {
68	            SandboxBackend::Auto => "auto",
69	            SandboxBackend::SandboxExec => "sandbox-exec",
70	            SandboxBackend::Bwrap => "bwrap",
71	            SandboxBackend::Docker => "docker",
72	            SandboxBackend::None => "none",
73	        };
74	        f.write_str(value)
75	    }
76	}
77	
78	impl FromStr for SandboxBackend {
79	    type Err = SandboxError;
80	
81	    fn from_str(value: &str) -> Result<Self> {
82	        match value {
83	            "auto" => Ok(Self::Auto),
84	            "sandbox-exec" => Ok(Self::SandboxExec),
85	            "bwrap" | "bubblewrap" => Ok(Self::Bwrap),
86	            "docker" => Ok(Self::Docker),
87	            "none" => Ok(Self::None),
88	            other => Err(SandboxError::InvalidBackend(other.to_string())),
89	        }
90	    }

93	pub fn resolve_backend(backend: SandboxBackend) -> Result<(SandboxBackend, Option<String>)> {
94	    match backend {
95	        SandboxBackend::Auto => {
96	            #[cfg(target_os = "macos")]
97	            {
98	                if which("sandbox-exec").is_ok() {
99	                    return Ok((SandboxBackend::SandboxExec, None));
100	                }
101	                Ok((
102	                    SandboxBackend::None,
103	                    Some("sandbox-exec not found; auto fell back to none".to_string()),
104	                ))
105	            }
106	            #[cfg(target_os = "linux")]
107	            {
108	                if which("bwrap").is_ok() {
109	                    return Ok((SandboxBackend::Bwrap, None));
110	                }
111	                Ok((
112	                    SandboxBackend::None,
113	                    Some("bwrap not found; auto fell back to none".to_string()),
114	                ))
115	            }
116	            #[cfg(not(any(target_os = "macos", target_os = "linux")))]
117	            {
118	                Ok((
119	                    SandboxBackend::None,
120	                    Some("no native sandbox backend for this platform; using none".to_string()),
121	                ))
122	            }
123	        }
124	        SandboxBackend::SandboxExec => require_binary("sandbox-exec", SandboxBackend::SandboxExec),
125	        SandboxBackend::Bwrap => require_binary("bwrap", SandboxBackend::Bwrap),
126	        SandboxBackend::Docker => require_binary("docker", SandboxBackend::Docker),
127	        SandboxBackend::None => Ok((SandboxBackend::None, None)),
128	    }
129	}
130	
131	fn require_binary(name: &str, backend: SandboxBackend) -> Result<(SandboxBackend, Option<String>)> {
132	    if which(name).is_ok() {
133	        Ok((backend, None))
134	    } else {
135	        Err(SandboxError::Unavailable(backend.to_string()))

### §14 Telemetry: §14.4 events.jsonl — internal contradiction

**Finding 2 — events bus parenthetical contradicts §18.3 and §22; and the actual code tells a third story**

The doc says: "Also published on a `tokio::sync::broadcast` channel (`events.rs`) for in-process subscribers (the TUI uses this when implemented; today the TUI polls files instead — see §22)."

§18.3 (line 1295) says: "Same-process run attaches can use the `RunEventBus` broadcast channel directly."
§22 (line 1488) says: "Event-backed TUI attach: same-process attaches use `RunEventBus`; cross-process attaches replay `events.jsonl` incrementally."

The code reality (`tui_events.rs:26-37`, `main.rs:23540`): `TuiEventFeed::from_broadcast` is gated `#[cfg(test)]`. Production `attach_tui_with_parent` uses `TuiEventFeed::file_tail` unconditionally — even for same-process runs. The broadcast is emitted to the channel and also written to file simultaneously (`events.rs:99-101`), but the TUI only reads the file. So §18.3 and §22's claim that "same-process attaches use RunEventBus" is currently false at the production path. §14.4's old parenthetical "today the TUI polls files instead" was actually correct at the attach level, but incorrect to say the bus is unused — it's just unused by the TUI itself (used by tests only).

The right fix is to update §14.4 to accurately describe what `emit_event` does (both writes file and sends on channel), note that the TUI always reads via file tail even in-process, and update §18.3/§22 to match.

The \`emit_event\` function writes to \`events.jsonl\` and sends on the channel simultaneously (\`events.rs:89-104\`). Production \`attach\` always reads via \`TuiEventFeed::file_tail\` — even for same-process runs (\`main.rs:23540\`); the broadcast-receiver path in \`TuiEventFeed::from_broadcast\` is \`#[cfg(test)]\` only (\`tui_events.rs:25-37\`). The file tail is the authoritative live-events path; the broadcast channel is available for future same-process subscribers.`

149	pub(crate) fn sandbox_exec_profile(spec: &SandboxSpec) -> Result<String> {
150	    let network = if spec.allow_network {
151	        if spec.network_allowlist.iter().any(|host| host == "*") {
152	            "(allow network*)".to_string()
153	        } else {
154	            "(deny network*)".to_string()
155	        }
156	    } else {
157	        "(deny network*)".to_string()
158	    };
159	    let mut read_rules = String::new();
160	    for path in system_read_allowlist(&spec.cwd, &spec.read_allowlist) {
161	        read_rules.push_str(&format!(
162	            "    (subpath \"{}\")\n",
163	            escape_seatbelt_path(&path)
164	        ));
165	    }
166	    let mut write_rules = String::new();
167	    for path in &spec.write_allowlist {
168	        write_rules.push_str(&format!(
169	            "    (subpath \"{}\")\n",
170	            escape_seatbelt_path(path)
171	        ));
172	    }
173	    let ssh_deny = std::env::var_os("HOME")
174	        .map(PathBuf::from)
175	        .map(|home| {
176	            let ssh = escape_seatbelt_path(&home.join(".ssh"));
177	            format!("(deny file-read* (subpath \"{ssh}\"))\n(deny file-write* (subpath \"{ssh}\"))")
178	        })
179	        .unwrap_or_default();
180	    let profile = format!(
181	        "(version 1)
182	(allow default)
183	{ssh_deny}
184	{network}
185	(allow file-read*
186	{read_rules})
187	(allow file-write*
188	    (subpath \"{}\")
189	    (subpath \"/private/tmp\")
190	    (subpath \"/tmp\")
191	{write_rules})
192	",
193	        escape_seatbelt_path(&spec.cwd)
194	    );
195	    if let Some(profile_dir) = spec.profile_dir.as_ref() {
196	        std::fs::create_dir_all(profile_dir)?;
197	        std::fs::write(profile_dir.join("profile.sb"), &profile)?;
198	    }
199	    Ok(profile)
200	}
201	
202	fn system_read_allowlist(cwd: &Path, extra: &[PathBuf]) -> Vec<PathBuf> {
203	    let mut paths = vec![
204	        PathBuf::from("/bin"),
205	        PathBuf::from("/sbin"),
206	        PathBuf::from("/usr"),
207	        PathBuf::from("/System"),
208	        PathBuf::from("/Library"),
209	        PathBuf::from("/Applications"),
210	        PathBuf::from("/opt/homebrew"),
211	        PathBuf::from("/opt/local"),
212	        PathBuf::from("/dev"),
213	        PathBuf::from("/private/tmp"),
214	        PathBuf::from("/tmp"),
215	        cwd.to_path_buf(),
216	    ];
217	    if let Ok(canonical) = cwd.canonicalize() {
218	        paths.push(canonical);
219	    }
220	    paths.extend(extra.iter().cloned());
221	    paths.extend(extra.iter().filter_map(|path| path.canonicalize().ok()));
222	    paths
223	}
224	
225	fn escape_seatbelt_path(path: &Path) -> String {
226	    path.to_string_lossy()
227	        .replace('\\', "\\\\")
228	        .replace('"', "\\\"")
229	}

15	    pub pid: Option<u32>,

22	pub async fn run(spec: SandboxSpec) -> Result<SandboxRunOutput> {
23	    let command = build_command(&spec)?;
24	    let mut child = Command::new(&command.program)
25	        .args(&command.args)
26	        .current_dir(&command.cwd)
27	        .envs(&command.env)
28	        .stdout(Stdio::piped())
29	        .stderr(Stdio::piped())
30	        .spawn()?;
31	    let pid = child.id();
32	    let stdout = child.stdout.take();
33	    let stderr = child.stderr.take();
34	    let stdout_task = tokio::spawn(read_pipe(stdout));
35	    let stderr_task = tokio::spawn(read_pipe(stderr));
36	    if let (Some(pid), Some(pid_file)) = (pid, spec.pid_file.as_ref()) {
37	        if let Some(parent) = pid_file.parent() {
38	            tokio::fs::create_dir_all(parent).await?;
39	        }
40	        tokio::fs::write(pid_file, format!("{pid}\n")).await?;
41	    }
42	    let status = if let Some(token) = spec.cancellation_token.as_ref() {
43	        tokio::select! {
44	            _ = token.cancelled() => {
45	                if let Some(pid) = pid {
46	                    signal_pid(pid, false);
47	                    sleep(Duration::from_secs(2)).await;
48	                    if child.try_wait()?.is_none() {
49	                        signal_pid(pid, true);
50	                    }
51	                }
52	                let _ = child.wait().await;
53	                if let Some(pid_file) = spec.pid_file.as_ref() {
54	                    let _ = tokio::fs::remove_file(pid_file).await;
55	                }
56	                return Err(SandboxError::Cancelled);
57	            }
58	            status = child.wait() => status
59	        }
60	    } else {
61	        child.wait().await
62	    }?;
63	    let stdout = stdout_task
64	        .await
65	        .unwrap_or_else(|err| Ok(format!("stdout join error: {err}")))?;
66	    let stderr = stderr_task
67	        .await
68	        .unwrap_or_else(|err| Ok(format!("stderr join error: {err}")))?;
69	    if let Some(pid_file) = spec.pid_file.as_ref() {
70	        let _ = tokio::fs::remove_file(pid_file).await;
71	    }
72	    Ok(SandboxRunOutput {
73	        backend: command.backend,
74	        pid,
75	        status_code: status.code(),
76	        stdout,
77	        stderr,
78	        warning: command.warning,
79	    })
80	}

82	async fn read_pipe<R>(pipe: Option<R>) -> std::io::Result<String>
83	where
84	    R: AsyncRead + Unpin + Send + 'static,
85	{
86	    let Some(mut pipe) = pipe else {
87	        return Ok(String::new());
88	    };
89	    let mut bytes = Vec::new();
90	    pipe.read_to_end(&mut bytes).await?;
91	    Ok(String::from_utf8_lossy(&bytes).to_string())
92	}

436	    let parent = path.parent().ok_or_else(|| {
437	        DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(format!("path has no parent: {}", path.display()))

439	    fs::create_dir_all(parent).with_path(parent)?;

1072	## 14. Telemetry: Spend, Traces, Provenance, Events
1073	
1074	Five append-only JSONL files capture every run's history. Four (`spend.jsonl`, `traces.jsonl`, `provenance.jsonl`, `events.jsonl`) live under `<run_root>/` directly; the fifth (`proofs/acceptance-progress.jsonl`, see §13.5) is gate-scoped and truncated per evaluation. All are written via `append_json_line` (`state.rs:375-388`), which opens in append mode and `sync_all`s after each line.
1075	
1076	### 14.1 `spend.jsonl`
1077	
1078	Schema:
1079	
1080	```json
1081	{
1082	  "timestamp": "<RFC3339>",
1083	  "run_id": "...",
1084	  "turn": 3,
1085	  "provider": "cli:claude-code",
1086	  "model": "claude-sonnet-4-5",
1087	  "input_tokens": 0,
1088	  "output_tokens": 0,
1089	  "cost_usd": 0.0,
1090	  "subscription": true,
1091	  "wall_time_seconds": 42.1
1092	}
1093	```
1094	
1095	One line per LLM call. HTTP providers fill in token counts and USD; CLI providers fill in `subscription: true` + `wall_time_seconds`.
1096	
1097	### 14.2 `traces.jsonl`
1098	
1099	Schema:
1100	
1101	```json
1102	{
1103	  "timestamp": "<RFC3339>",
1104	  "run_id": "...",
1105	  "turn": 3,
1106	  "event": "llm.complete" | "tool.bash" | "tool.write_file" | "tool.cli_subagent" | "import.claude-code" | ...,
1107	  "latency_ms": 1234,
1108	  "detail": { "tool_call_id": "...", "provider": "...", "trace": {...} }
1109	}
1110	```
1111	
1112	Every LLM call, every tool dispatch, every notable event. The detail block carries free-form JSON per event kind.
1113	
1114	### 14.3 `provenance.jsonl`
1115	
1116	Schema (per file changed):
1117	
1118	```json
1119	{
1120	  "timestamp": "<RFC3339>",
1121	  "run_id": "...",
1122	  "turn": 3,
1123	  "tool_call_id": "...",
1124	  "model": "claude-sonnet-4-5",
1125	  "session_id": "...",
1126	  "file": "src/main.rs"
1127	}
1128	```
1129	
1130	One line per file changed by a tool call. Lets `show <run-id>` answer "which prompt produced this file?"
1131	
1132	### 14.4 `events.jsonl`
1133	
1134	Structured `RunEvent` log: `TurnStarted { turn }`, `ToolCallStarted { tool_call_id, kind }`, `ToolCallResult { tool_call_id, status, latency_ms }`, `RunCompleted { outcome }`. Also published on a `tokio::sync::broadcast` channel (`events.rs`) for in-process subscribers (the TUI uses this when implemented; today the TUI polls files instead — see §22).
1135

419	        if scope_filter.is_some_and(|scope| scope != state.scope) {
420	            continue;
421	        }

427	            updated_at: state.updated_at,
428	            state_path: entry.path().to_path_buf(),
