1136	---
1137	
1138	## 15. Resume Semantics
1139	
1140	`crates/deadreckon/src/main.rs:940-1000` is the `resume_command` handler.
1141	
1142	### 15.1 The Completed guard
1143	
1144	`main.rs:947`:
1145	
1146	```rust
1147	if state.status == RunStatus::Completed {
1148	    println!("run {} is already completed", state.run_id);
1149	    return Ok(());
1150	}
1151	```
1152	
1153	Completed runs cannot be resumed. They can be re-promoted (idempotent) but not re-entered into the loop. The only forward path for a completed run today is to start a new run.
1154	
1155	### 15.2 The replay process
1156	
1157	For non-Completed runs (`Failed`, `Killed`, `Paused`):
1158	
1159	1. Acquire the task lock.
1160	2. Clear `failure_reason`, `pause_reason`, `killed_at`.
1161	3. Set `status = Planned`.
1162	4. Optionally extend `max_wall_seconds` from the resume flag.
1163	5. Set `child_pids = vec![cli_pid]`.
1164	6. `save_state()`.
1165	7. Call `run_turn_loop` with `RunLoopConfig.from_turn = <CLI flag>`.
1166	8. The loop calls `load_or_reconstruct_history(state, from_turn)` in `crates/deadreckon-runtime/src/turn_loop.rs`, which loads `history.json` if present, else reconstructs from `traces.jsonl`. With `from_turn = N`, history is truncated to N entries and `state.turn = N`.
1167	
1168	History reconstruction tolerates a `traces.jsonl` that ends mid-tool-call by ignoring incomplete entries — the next turn re-runs that turn.
1169	
1170	See `/Users/gdc/deadreckon/docs/RESUME-SEMANTICS.md` for the contract.
1171	
1172	---
1173	
1174	## 16. Cross-Tool Import
1175	
1176	`deadreckon import <source>` reads from external coding-agent histories and synthesizes a completed deadreckon run from one concrete imported session, or from an explicit `--all` root import. It is read-only with respect to provider-owned transcript roots and writes only deadreckon run-state files.
1177	
1178	Today's sources:
1179	
1180	| Source | Discovery | Format |
1181	|---|---|---|
1182	| `codex` / `cli:codex` | `cli:codex` descriptor `[ingest]`, including `CODEX_SESSIONS_DIR`, `session_meta.payload.cwd`, `*.jsonl`, and `codex-cli` schema | JSONL |
1183	| `claude-code` / `cli:claude-code` | `cli:claude-code` descriptor `[ingest]`, including `CLAUDE_PROJECTS_DIR` and Claude project-directory cwd mapping | JSONL |
1184	| `gemini` / `cli:gemini` | `cli:gemini` descriptor `[ingest]`, including `GEMINI_DIR`, JSON/JSONL storage, and `gemini` schema | JSON or JSONL |
1185	| `opencode` / `cli:opencode` | `cli:opencode` descriptor `[ingest]`, file-mode `storage/session`, `storage/message`, and `storage/part` | JSON |
1186	| `copilot` / `cli:copilot` | `cli:copilot` descriptor `[ingest]`, including `COPILOT_DIR`, `session-state`, nested `events.jsonl`, and `data.context.cwd` | JSONL |
1187	| `pi` / `cli:pi` | `cli:pi` descriptor `[ingest]`, including `PI_CODING_AGENT_SESSION_DIR`, top-level `cwd`, and Pi session-header validation | JSONL |
1188	| `cursor` | `~/.cursor/chats/` (`DEADRECKON_IMPORT_CURSOR_ROOT`) | SQLite via `sqlite3 -json` |
1189	
1190	The command surface is `deadreckon import <source> [--preview|--list|--session <id-or-path>|--cwd <path>|--all|--since <duration>|--replace|--json]`. Default import filters candidates to the launch cwd or `--cwd` where the descriptor supports cwd matching. Empty, stale, and ambiguous candidate sets refuse without creating a run and print concrete `try:` lines. `--preview` and `--list` never create run directories. `--all` is the explicit whole-root mode.
1191	
1192	The handler creates an `imported-<hash>` run id from the concrete source-session identity, parses selected transcript files, appends normalized source-neutral entries to `traces.jsonl`, writes file provenance to `provenance.jsonl`, marks the run `Completed` (skipping the gate), and writes `import.json` under the run root. The manifest records `source`, `source_alias`, `schema`, `storage`, `cwd`, `mode`, `session_id`, `session_paths`, `content_hash`, source time bounds, row/event/provenance counts, `raw_rows_stored = false`, and the `deadreckon import ... --replace` command needed to reimport. If an existing imported run has a different content hash, import refuses unless `--replace` is explicit.
1193	
1194	Trace `detail` rows use a stable import schema: `import_version`, canonical `source`, `schema`, optional `session_id`, `source_path`, optional `source_line`, `source_event`, optional `role`, `summary`, optional tool fields, `files`, optional token `usage`, and `raw_hash`. Raw provider payloads are not copied into every trace row by default; source path/line plus hashes preserve auditability. Parser coverage includes Codex agent messages/function calls/token counts, Claude content/tool blocks, Gemini JSON/JSONL messages/tool calls, OpenCode file-mode sessions/messages/parts, Copilot assistant/reasoning/tool/usage rows, Pi session/message/tool/result rows, and Cursor SQLite rows.
1195	
1196	`deadreckon import` is the *user-driven* ingest. The *TUI-driven* ingest path that lets `attach` read live provider transcripts uses the same descriptor `[ingest]` roots, env overrides, storage kinds, file globs, freshness windows, cwd matching, and schema keys for CLI providers; see §18.3 and `docs/design/PROVIDER-CLI-INGEST.md`. OpenCode SQLite, provider transcript mutation/undo, full replay UI, and cross-run import analytics remain V1 candidates in `docs/V1-CANDIDATES.md`.
1197	
1198	---
1199	
1200	## 17. CLI Surface
1201	
1202	The `Commands` enum in `crates/deadreckon/src/main.rs` defines the CLI surface. Handlers and roles:
1203	
1204	| Verb | Handler | Role |
1205	|---|---|---|
1206	| `init` | `cli.rs:440` | Interactive setup of `~/.deadreckon/config.toml` |
1207	| `config get/set` | `cli.rs:465` | Non-interactive TOML edits |
1208	| `run` | `cli.rs:537` | Create + enter turn loop |
1209	| `doctor` | `cli.rs:910` | 8-point actionable preflight |
1210	| `status` / `next` | `cli.rs:1308` | Current project's latest run, locations, and next action |
1211	| `list` | `cli.rs:964` | Project-scoped run inventory by default; `--all` for global history, `--full` for exact values |
1212	| `apply` | `cli.rs:1062` | Apply a completed worktree run (or merged plan result) to the user's current branch |
1213	| `finish` | `cli.rs:992` | Choose the right completion action (apply for git worktrees, export for non-git) for a run or merged plan |
1214	| `abandon` / `discard` | `cli.rs:1103` | Remove a run's worktree branch/path or mark no-op modes abandoned |
1215	| `materialize` / `export` | `cli.rs:1041` | Copy a completed fresh/copy artifact (or merged plan result) to a normal directory |
1216	| `cleanup` / `prune` | `cli.rs:1121` | Clean abandoned, stale, or selected completed worktree runs |
1217	| `attach` | `cli.rs:1216` | TUI on a live or completed run, chain, or plan |
1218	| `kill` | `cli.rs:1230` | Lock release + child PID termination (run, chain, or plan) |
1219	| `resume` | `cli.rs:1248` | Re-enter the loop on a non-Completed run |
1220	| `extend` | `cli.rs:1149` | Re-open a completed run with a follow-up goal that inherits history |
1221	| `undo` | `cli.rs:1265` | Restore snapshot to a target turn |
1222	| `show` | `cli.rs:1281` | Pretty-print full state + provenance + traces; `--why-failed` for runs and plans |
1223	| `import` | `cli.rs:1329` | Read-only descriptor-backed transcript import from CLI providers plus Cursor SQLite |
1224	| `chain` | `cli.rs:798` | Create, plan, run, attach, pause/resume/kill, undo, extend, and redo serial autonomous chains |
1225	| `orchestrate` | `cli.rs:630` | One-command wrappers for `review` and `full-plan` multi-agent runs |
1226	| `plan` | `cli.rs:679` | Write an orchestration plan (worker specs + `plan.json`) without starting child runs |
1227	| `fork` | `cli.rs:720` | Spawn ready child runs for a plan and supervise them through completion |
1228	| `merge` | `cli.rs:756` | Compose completed child library artifacts into a new promoted run (with semantic merge repair) |
1229	| `def-done` | `cli.rs:502` | Write, add, show, or check the project's English done criteria |
1230	| `acceptance` | `cli.rs:492` | Hidden compatibility surface for creating, explaining, or checking done criteria |
1231	| `doc` | `cli.rs:1182` | Print run narrative, as-built, implementation decision ledger, or delta; with optional polish pass |
1232	| `history` | `cli.rs:1298` | Search durable run traces and provenance (regex/scope/plan filters) |
1233	| `library` | `cli.rs:983` | Query promoted run artifacts by goal/date/scope |
1234	| `detect` | `cli.rs:919` | Probe registered providers and return availability and credential status |
1235	| `providers` | `cli.rs:932` | List provider routes, models, kind tokens, and the active selection |
1236	| `update` | `cli.rs:941` | Check for or route self-updates via npm, Homebrew, shell, Cargo, or source channel |
1237	| `completion` / `completions` | `cli.rs:482` | Generate or install shell tab-completion scripts (bash, zsh, fish, elvish, powershell) |
1238	
1239	The CLI defaults are honest: `--sandbox` defaults to `auto`, `--max-spend` defaults to `$10` (with a confirmation gate above `$50`), `--provider` defaults to the highest-credentialed entry per the fallback chain, `--skill` defaults to `default-coding`.
1240	
1241	`run` now starts codebase-aware by default. In a git repo it previews and then creates a `git worktree` on a `dr/...` branch; `--fresh` preserves the old empty-working-dir behavior, `--from <path>` uses copy mode, and `--in-place --i-know-its-a-lot` edits the source tree directly. Completed worktree runs hint `apply` / `discard`; copy and fresh runs hint `export` / `extend`. Run-id arguments accept unique prefixes and `latest` / `last` resolves to the latest run in the current project scope.
1242	
1243	`completion install` is driven from the real clap command tree, so subcommand aliases, flags, and value-hint completions stay in sync with `deadreckon --help`. The handler detects the active shell via `$SHELL`, writes the script to a per-shell default path (e.g. `~/.zsh/completions/_deadreckon`, `~/.local/share/bash-completion/completions/deadreckon`), and for zsh adds a managed `# deadreckon completion` block to `~/.zshrc` unless `--no-rc` is passed. `init` invokes `try_install_completion_after_init` so first-time setup ships completions opt-out (`init --no-completion`). The per-shell stdout variants (`completion bash|zsh|fish|elvish|powershell`) print the script for users who manage their own shell config.
1244	
1245	`run` startup details (`print_run_started`) are now also emitted at the top of `extend` and `resume` so extended/resumed runs surface their selected provider route and doc-provider source the same way fresh runs do. Interactive terminals receive a `deadreckoning_course` ASCII progress strip and a polled `cli_wait_status` line while a long turn is in flight; the status is cleared as soon as the loop reports back. `kill` against a loaded run now also persists `RunStatus::Killed` + `killed_at` + `failure_reason = "killed by user"` before returning so downstream tooling sees a consistent terminal state.

138	            "acceptance marker run_id {} does not match {}",

143	        return Err(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(

145	        ));

212	) -> Result<Vec<AcceptanceCheckResult>> {
213	    let results = evaluate_acceptance_checks(run_root, working_dir)?;
214	    if let Some(failed) = results
215	        .iter()
216	        .find(|result| result.must_pass && !result.passed)
217	    {
218	        return Err(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(format!(
219	            "acceptance check failed: {}",
220	            failed.detail
221	        )));
222	    }
223	    Ok(results)
224	}
225	
226	pub fn evaluate_acceptance_checks(
227	    run_root: &Path,
228	    working_dir: &Path,
229	) -> Result<Vec<AcceptanceCheckResult>> {
230	    evaluate_acceptance_checks_inner(run_root, working_dir, None)
231	}
232	
233	pub fn evaluate_acceptance_checks_with_progress(
234	    run_root: &Path,
235	    working_dir: &Path,
236	) -> Result<Vec<AcceptanceCheckResult>> {
237	    let progress_path = acceptance_progress_path_for_run_root(run_root);
238	    match std::fs::remove_file(&progress_path) {
239	        Ok(()) => {}
240	        Err(source) if source.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => {}
241	        Err(source) => {
242	            return Err(DeadreckonError::Io {
243	                path: progress_path,
244	                source,
245	            });
246	        }
247	    }
248	    evaluate_acceptance_checks_inner(run_root, working_dir, Some(&progress_path))
249	}
250	
251	fn evaluate_acceptance_checks_inner(
252	    run_root: &Path,
253	    working_dir: &Path,
254	    progress_path: Option<&Path>,
255	) -> Result<Vec<AcceptanceCheckResult>> {
256	    let spec_path = acceptance_spec_path_for_run_root(run_root);
257	    if !spec_path.exists() {
258	        return evaluate_default_acceptance_with_progress(working_dir, progress_path);
259	    }
260	    let raw = std::fs::read_to_string(&spec_path).with_path(&spec_path)?;
261	    let checks = parse_acceptance_checks(&raw)?;
262	    let total = checks.len();
263	    emit_acceptance_progress(progress_path, "started", 0, total, None)?;
264	    let mut results = Vec::new();
265	    for (idx, check) in checks.into_iter().enumerate() {
266	        let index = idx + 1;
267	        emit_acceptance_progress(progress_path, "running", index, total, None)?;
268	        let result = evaluate_check(working_dir, check)?;
269	        let status = if result.passed { "passed" } else { "failed" };
270	        emit_acceptance_progress(progress_path, status, index, total, Some(result.clone()))?;
271	        results.push(result);
272	    }
273	    let status = if results
274	        .iter()
275	        .any(|result| result.must_pass && !result.passed)
276	    {
277	        "failed"
278	    } else {
279	        "passed"
280	    };
281	    emit_acceptance_progress(progress_path, status, total, total, None)?;
282	    Ok(results)
283	}
284	
285	fn evaluate_default_acceptance_with_progress(
286	    working_dir: &Path,
287	    progress_path: Option<&Path>,
288	) -> Result<Vec<AcceptanceCheckResult>> {
289	    emit_acceptance_progress(progress_path, "started", 0, 1, None)?;
290	    emit_acceptance_progress(progress_path, "running", 1, 1, None)?;
291	    let results = evaluate_default_acceptance(working_dir)?;
292	    if let Some(result) = results.first().cloned() {
293	        let status = if result.passed { "passed" } else { "failed" };
294	        emit_acceptance_progress(progress_path, status, 1, 1, Some(result))?;
295	    }
296	    let status = if results
297	        .iter()
298	        .any(|result| result.must_pass && !result.passed)
299	    {
300	        "failed"
301	    } else {
302	        "passed"
303	    };
304	    emit_acceptance_progress(progress_path, status, 1, 1, None)?;
305	    Ok(results)
306	}
307	
308	fn emit_acceptance_progress(
309	    progress_path: Option<&Path>,
310	    status: &str,
311	    index: usize,
312	    total: usize,
313	    result: Option<AcceptanceCheckResult>,
314	) -> Result<()> {
315	    let Some(progress_path) = progress_path else {
316	        return Ok(());
317	    };
318	    append_json_line(
319	        progress_path,
320	        &AcceptanceProgressEntry {
321	            checked_at: Utc::now(),
322	            status: status.to_string(),
323	            index,
324	            total,
325	            result,
326	        },
327	    )
328	}
329	
330	fn evaluate_default_acceptance(working_dir: &Path) -> Result<Vec<AcceptanceCheckResult>> {
331	    if working_dir.join("Cargo.toml").exists() {
332	        let started = Instant::now();
333	        let output = Command::new("cargo")
334	            .arg("test")
335	            .current_dir(working_dir)
336	            .output()
337	            .map_err(|source| DeadreckonError::Io {
338	                path: working_dir.join("Cargo.toml"),
339	                source,
340	            })?;
341	        return Ok(vec![AcceptanceCheckResult {
342	            kind: "cargo_test".to_string(),
343	            passed: output.status.success(),
344	            must_pass: true,
345	            detail: format!("cargo test exited with {}", output.status),
346	            command: Some("cargo test".to_string()),
347	            cwd: Some(working_dir.to_path_buf()),
348	            duration_ms: Some(duration_ms(started)),
349	            stdout: clipped_stdout(&output),
350	            stderr: clipped_stderr(&output),
351	        }]);
352	    }
353	    if !working_dir.is_dir() {
354	        return Ok(vec![AcceptanceCheckResult {
355	            kind: "working_dir".to_string(),
356	            passed: false,
357	            must_pass: true,
358	            detail: format!("working directory missing: {}", working_dir.display()),
359	            command: None,
360	            cwd: Some(working_dir.to_path_buf()),
361	            duration_ms: None,
362	            stdout: None,
363	            stderr: None,
364	        }]);
365	    }
366	    Ok(vec![AcceptanceCheckResult {
367	        kind: "working_dir".to_string(),
368	        passed: true,
369	        must_pass: true,
370	        detail: "working directory exists".to_string(),
371	        command: None,
372	        cwd: Some(working_dir.to_path_buf()),
373	        duration_ms: None,
374	        stdout: None,
375	        stderr: None,
376	    }])
377	}
378	
379	fn evaluate_check(working_dir: &Path, check: AcceptanceCheck) -> Result<AcceptanceCheckResult> {
380	    match check {
381	        AcceptanceCheck::CargoTest { args, must_pass } => {
382	            let started = Instant::now();
383	            let output = Command::new("cargo")
384	                .arg("test")
385	                .args(&args)
386	                .current_dir(working_dir)
387	                .output()
388	                .map_err(|source| DeadreckonError::Io {
389	                    path: working_dir.join("Cargo.toml"),
390	                    source,
391	                })?;
392	            Ok(AcceptanceCheckResult {
393	                kind: "cargo_test".to_string(),
394	                passed: output.status.success(),
395	                must_pass,
396	                detail: format!("cargo test exited with {}", output.status),
397	                command: Some(format_command("cargo test", &args)),
398	                cwd: Some(working_dir.to_path_buf()),
399	                duration_ms: Some(duration_ms(started)),
400	                stdout: clipped_stdout(&output),
401	                stderr: clipped_stderr(&output),
402	            })
403	        }
404	        AcceptanceCheck::FileExists { path, must_pass } => {
405	            let path = render_template(working_dir, &path);
406	            let exists = path.exists();
407	            Ok(AcceptanceCheckResult {
408	                kind: "file_exists".to_string(),
409	                passed: exists,
410	                must_pass,
411	                detail: if exists {
412	                    format!("{} exists", path.display())
413	                } else {
414	                    format!("{} is missing", path.display())
415	                },
416	                command: None,
417	                cwd: None,
418	                duration_ms: None,
419	                stdout: None,
420	                stderr: None,
421	            })
422	        }
423	        AcceptanceCheck::ContentMatch {
424	            path,
425	            pattern,
426	            must_pass,
427	        } => {
428	            let path = render_template(working_dir, &path);
429	            let body = std::fs::read_to_string(&path).unwrap_or_default();
430	            let matched = regex::Regex::new(&pattern)
431	                .map(|regex| regex.is_match(&body))
432	                .unwrap_or_else(|_| body.contains(&pattern));
433	            Ok(AcceptanceCheckResult {
434	                kind: "content_match".to_string(),
435	                passed: matched,
436	                must_pass,
437	                detail: if matched {
438	                    format!("{} matches {:?}", path.display(), pattern)
439	                } else {
440	                    format!("{} does not match {:?}", path.display(), pattern)
441	                },
442	                command: None,
443	                cwd: None,
444	                duration_ms: None,
445	                stdout: None,
446	                stderr: None,
447	            })
448	        }
449	        AcceptanceCheck::BuildSuccess { cwd, must_pass } => {
450	            let cwd = render_template(working_dir, &cwd);
451	            let started = Instant::now();
452	            let output = Command::new("cargo")
453	                .arg("build")
454	                .current_dir(&cwd)
455	                .output()
456	                .map_err(|source| DeadreckonError::Io {
457	                    path: cwd.join("Cargo.toml"),
458	                    source,
459	                })?;
460	            Ok(AcceptanceCheckResult {
461	                kind: "build_success".to_string(),
462	                passed: output.status.success(),
463	                must_pass,
464	                detail: format!(
465	                    "cargo build in {} exited with {}",
466	                    cwd.display(),
467	                    output.status
468	                ),
469	                command: Some("cargo build".to_string()),
470	                cwd: Some(cwd),
471	                duration_ms: Some(duration_ms(started)),
472	                stdout: clipped_stdout(&output),
473	                stderr: clipped_stderr(&output),
474	            })
475	        }
476	        AcceptanceCheck::Shell {
477	            command,
478	            cwd,
479	            must_pass,
480	        } => {
481	            let cwd = cwd
482	                .map(|cwd| render_template(working_dir, &cwd))
483	                .unwrap_or_else(|| working_dir.to_path_buf());
484	            let started = Instant::now();
485	            let output = Command::new("sh")
486	                .arg("-lc")
487	                .arg(&command)
488	                .current_dir(&cwd)
489	                .output()
490	                .map_err(|source| DeadreckonError::Io {
491	                    path: cwd.clone(),
492	                    source,
493	                })?;
494	            Ok(AcceptanceCheckResult {
495	                kind: "shell".to_string(),
496	                passed: output.status.success(),
497	                must_pass,
498	                detail: format!(
499	                    "shell {:?} in {} exited with {}",
500	                    command,
501	                    cwd.display(),
502	                    output.status
503	                ),
504	                command: Some(command),
505	                cwd: Some(cwd),
506	                duration_ms: Some(duration_ms(started)),
507	                stdout: clipped_stdout(&output),
508	                stderr: clipped_stderr(&output),
509	            })
510	        }
511	    }
512	}
513	
514	fn duration_ms(started: Instant) -> u64 {
515	    started.elapsed().as_millis().min(u128::from(u64::MAX)) as u64
516	}
517	
518	fn clipped_stdout(output: &Output) -> Option<String> {
519	    clipped_output(&output.stdout)
520	}
521	
522	fn clipped_stderr(output: &Output) -> Option<String> {
523	    clipped_output(&output.stderr)
524	}
525	
526	fn clipped_output(bytes: &[u8]) -> Option<String> {
527	    let text = String::from_utf8_lossy(bytes).trim().to_string();
528	    if text.is_empty() {
529	        None
530	    } else {
531	        Some(clip_text(&text, 4096))
532	    }
533	}
534	
535	fn clip_text(text: &str, limit: usize) -> String {
536	    if text.len() <= limit {
537	        return text.to_string();
538	    }
539	    let mut clipped = text
540	        .char_indices()
541	        .take_while(|(idx, _)| *idx < limit)
542	        .map(|(_, ch)| ch)
543	        .collect::<String>();
544	    clipped.push_str("\n... output truncated ...");
545	    clipped
546	}
547	
548	fn format_command(base: &str, args: &[String]) -> String {
549	    if args.is_empty() {
550	        base.to_string()
551	    } else {
552	        format!("{base} {}", args.join(" "))
553	    }
554	}
555	
556	fn parse_acceptance_checks(raw: &str) -> Result<Vec<AcceptanceCheck>> {
557	    let root: YamlValue = serde_yaml::from_str(raw).map_err(|source| {
558	        DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(format!("invalid acceptance.yaml: {source}"))
559	    })?;
560	    let mut checks = Vec::new();
561	    for item in yaml_seq(yaml_get(&root, "checks")) {
562	        checks.push(parse_check_value(item, None)?);
563	    }
564	    for item in yaml_seq(yaml_get(&root, "required")) {
565	        checks.push(parse_check_value(item, Some(true))?);
566	    }
567	    for item in yaml_seq(yaml_get(&root, "optional")) {
568	        checks.push(parse_check_value(item, Some(false))?);
569	    }
570	    for item in yaml_seq(yaml_get(&root, "tests")) {
571	        checks.push(parse_shell_check(item, true)?);
572	    }
573	    for item in yaml_seq(yaml_get(&root, "file-exists")) {
574	        checks.push(parse_file_exists_check(item, true)?);
575	    }
576	    for item in yaml_seq(yaml_get(&root, "content-match")) {
577	        checks.push(parse_content_match_check(item, true)?);
578	    }
579	    for item in yaml_seq(yaml_get(&root, "build-success")) {
580	        checks.push(parse_build_success_check(item, true));
581	    }
582	    Ok(checks)
583	}
584	
585	fn parse_check_value(value: &YamlValue, force_must_pass: Option<bool>) -> Result<AcceptanceCheck> {
586	    if let Ok(mut check) = serde_yaml::from_value::<AcceptanceCheck>(value.clone()) {
587	        if let Some(must_pass) = force_must_pass {
588	            check.set_must_pass(must_pass);
589	        }
590	        return Ok(check);
591	    }
592	    if let Some(command) = yaml_string(value) {
593	        return Ok(AcceptanceCheck::Shell {
594	            command,
595	            cwd: None,
596	            must_pass: force_must_pass.unwrap_or(true),
597	        });
598	    }
599	    let Some((kind, body)) = single_key_mapping(value) else {
600	        return Err(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(format!(
601	            "invalid acceptance check: {:?}",
602	            value
603	        )));
604	    };
605	    let must_pass = force_must_pass.unwrap_or(true);
606	    match kind.as_str() {
607	        "file-exists" | "file_exists" => parse_file_exists_check(body, must_pass),
608	        "content-match" | "content_match" => parse_content_match_check(body, must_pass),
609	        "build-success" | "build_success" => Ok(parse_build_success_check(body, must_pass)),
610	        "shell" | "test" => parse_shell_check(body, must_pass),
611	        "cargo-test" | "cargo_test" => Ok(AcceptanceCheck::CargoTest {
612	            args: yaml_string(body).map(|arg| vec![arg]).unwrap_or_default(),
613	            must_pass,
614	        }),
615	        other => Err(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(format!(
616	            "unknown acceptance check kind {other}"
617	        ))),
618	    }
619	}
620	
621	fn parse_file_exists_check(value: &YamlValue, must_pass: bool) -> Result<AcceptanceCheck> {
622	    let path = yaml_string(value)
623	        .or_else(|| yaml_get(value, "path").and_then(yaml_string))
624	        .ok_or_else(|| DeadreckonError::InvalidInput("file-exists requires path".to_string()))?;
625	    Ok(AcceptanceCheck::FileExists { path, must_pass })
626	}
627	
628	fn parse_content_match_check(value: &YamlValue, must_pass: bool) -> Result<AcceptanceCheck> {
629	    let path = yaml_get(value, "path")
630	        .and_then(yaml_string)
631	        .ok_or_else(|| DeadreckonError::InvalidInput("content-match requires path".to_string()))?;
632	    let pattern = yaml_get(value, "pattern")
633	        .and_then(yaml_string)
634	        .ok_or_else(|| {
635	            DeadreckonError::InvalidInput("content-match requires pattern".to_string())
636	        })?;
637	    Ok(AcceptanceCheck::ContentMatch {
638	        path,
639	        pattern,
640	        must_pass,
641	    })
642	}
643	
644	fn parse_build_success_check(value: &YamlValue, must_pass: bool) -> AcceptanceCheck {
645	    let cwd = yaml_string(value)
646	        .or_else(|| yaml_get(value, "cwd").and_then(yaml_string))
647	        .unwrap_or_else(|| "{working_dir}".to_string());
648	    AcceptanceCheck::BuildSuccess { cwd, must_pass }
649	}
650	
651	fn parse_shell_check(value: &YamlValue, must_pass: bool) -> Result<AcceptanceCheck> {
652	    let command = yaml_string(value)
653	        .or_else(|| yaml_get(value, "command").and_then(yaml_string))
654	        .ok_or_else(|| DeadreckonError::InvalidInput("shell check requires command".to_string()))?;
655	    let cwd = yaml_get(value, "cwd").and_then(yaml_string);
656	    Ok(AcceptanceCheck::Shell {
657	        command,
658	        cwd,
659	        must_pass,
660	    })
661	}
662	
663	fn yaml_get<'a>(value: &'a YamlValue, key: &str) -> Option<&'a YamlValue> {
664	    value.as_mapping()?.get(YamlValue::String(key.to_string()))
665	}
666	
667	fn yaml_seq(value: Option<&YamlValue>) -> Vec<&YamlValue> {
668	    match value {
669	        Some(YamlValue::Sequence(values)) => values.iter().collect(),
670	        Some(value) => vec![value],
671	        None => Vec::new(),
672	    }
673	}
674	
675	fn yaml_string(value: &YamlValue) -> Option<String> {
676	    value.as_str().map(ToString::to_string)
677	}
678	
679	fn single_key_mapping(value: &YamlValue) -> Option<(String, &YamlValue)> {
680	    let mapping = value.as_mapping()?;
681	    if mapping.len() != 1 {
682	        return None;
683	    }
684	    let (key, value) = mapping.iter().next()?;
685	    Some((key.as_str()?.to_string(), value))
686	}
687	
688	impl AcceptanceCheck {
689	    fn set_must_pass(&mut self, value: bool) {
690	        match self {
691	            AcceptanceCheck::CargoTest { must_pass, .. }
692	            | AcceptanceCheck::FileExists { must_pass, .. }
693	            | AcceptanceCheck::ContentMatch { must_pass, .. }
694	            | AcceptanceCheck::BuildSuccess { must_pass, .. }
695	            | AcceptanceCheck::Shell { must_pass, .. } => *must_pass = value,
696	        }
697	    }
698	}
699	
700	fn render_template(working_dir: &Path, value: &str) -> PathBuf {
701	    PathBuf::from(value.replace("{working_dir}", &working_dir.to_string_lossy()))
702	}
703	
704	fn marker_signature(run_root: &Path, marker: &AcceptanceMarker) -> Result<String> {
705	    let nonce_path = gate_nonce_path_for_run_root(run_root);
706	    let nonce = std::fs::read_to_string(&nonce_path).with_path(&nonce_path)?;
707	    let mut hasher = DefaultHasher::new();
708	    nonce.trim().hash(&mut hasher);
709	    marker.schema_version.hash(&mut hasher);
710	    marker.run_id.hash(&mut hasher);
711	    marker.status.hash(&mut hasher);
712	    marker.produced_by.hash(&mut hasher);
713	    marker.checked_at.to_rfc3339().hash(&mut hasher);
714	    marker.working_dir.hash(&mut hasher);
715	    marker.check_count.hash(&mut hasher);
716	    for check in &marker.checks {
717	        check.hash(&mut hasher);
718	    }
719	    Ok(format!("{:016x}", hasher.finish()))
720	}
721	
722	fn default_must_pass() -> bool {
723	    true
724	}

1	use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
2	
3	use chrono::{DateTime, Utc};
4	use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
5	
6	use crate::error::{DeadreckonError, IoContext, JsonContext, Result};
7	use crate::state::PipelineState;
8	
9	pub const CANCEL_MARKER: &str = "cancel.marker";
10	
11	#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
12	pub struct CancelMarker {
13	    pub run_id: String,
14	    pub requested_at: DateTime<Utc>,
15	    pub reason: String,
16	}
17	
18	pub fn cancel_marker_path(state: &PipelineState) -> PathBuf {
19	    cancel_marker_path_for_run_root(&state.run_root)
20	}
21	
22	pub fn cancel_marker_path_for_run_root(run_root: &Path) -> PathBuf {
23	    run_root.join(CANCEL_MARKER)
24	}
25	
26	pub fn write_cancel_marker(state: &PipelineState, reason: impl Into<String>) -> Result<PathBuf> {
27	    let path = cancel_marker_path(state);
28	    let marker = CancelMarker {
29	        run_id: state.run_id.clone(),
30	        requested_at: Utc::now(),
31	        reason: reason.into(),
32	    };
33	    if let Some(parent) = path.parent() {
34	        std::fs::create_dir_all(parent).with_path(parent)?;
35	    }
36	    std::fs::write(
37	        &path,
38	        serde_json::to_vec_pretty(&marker).with_json_path(&path)?,
39	    )
40	    .with_path(&path)?;
41	    Ok(path)
42	}
43	
44	pub fn clear_cancel_marker(state: &PipelineState) -> Result<()> {
45	    let path = cancel_marker_path(state);
46	    match std::fs::remove_file(&path) {
47	        Ok(()) => Ok(()),
48	        Err(source) if source.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => Ok(()),
49	        Err(source) => Err(DeadreckonError::Io { path, source }),
50	    }
51	}
52	
53	pub fn cancel_marker_present(state: &PipelineState) -> bool {
54	    cancel_marker_path(state).exists()
55	}
56

380	### 5.2 Runtime tree (`/Users/gdc/.deadreckon/`)
381	
382	```
383	/Users/gdc/.deadreckon/
384	├── config.toml                   # BYOK keys, defaults, fallback chain
385	├── runstate/
386	│   └── <scope>/                  # scope = "<repo-basename>-<fnv1a32-hash>"
387	│       ├── current/
388	│       │   └── <task_key>.json   # CurrentRunPointer for the active run per task
389	│       └── runs/
390	│           └── <run_id>/         # uuid simple-form
391	│               ├── state.json
392	│               ├── working/      # before promotion; library/... after
393	│               ├── snapshots/
394	│               │   └── turn-<N>/  # per-turn full working-tree copy
395	│               ├── turns/
396	│               │   └── turn-<N>/  # provider stdout, prompt.md
397	│               ├── proofs/
398	│               │   ├── turn-acceptance.json       # AcceptanceMarker
399	│               │   └── acceptance-progress.jsonl  # streaming AcceptanceProgressEntry
400	│               ├── gate/
401	│               │   └── nonce      # uuid; only dr-gate can read for signing
402	│               ├── child-pids/
403	│               │   └── *.pid      # per-subprocess PID files
404	│               ├── sandbox/       # per-run Seatbelt profile (if mac) or bwrap args
405	│               ├── traces.jsonl
406	│               ├── provenance.jsonl
407	│               ├── spend.jsonl
408	│               ├── events.jsonl
409	│               ├── history.json   # narrative tool-call summaries
410	│               └── acceptance.yaml   # optional spec for dr-gate
411	├── locks/
412	│   └── <scope>--<task_key>.lock   # one lock per task
413	└── library/
414	    └── <scope>/
415	        └── <run_id>/
416	            ├── manifest.json      # PromotionManifest
417	            └── ...                # promoted working tree
418	```
419	
420	The split between `runstate/` (mutable working state) and `library/` (durable promoted artifacts) is deliberate: `runstate/` is per-scope and ephemeral; `library/` is global and intended to outlive cleanup. The `state.working_dir` field starts pointing at `runstate/.../working/` and is rewritten to `library/<scope>/<run_id>/` after promotion.
421	
422	### 5.3 Path derivation
423	
424	`crates/deadreckon-core/src/paths.rs:9-65` exposes:
425	
426	```rust
427	impl DeadreckonPaths {
428	    pub fn home(&self) -> &Path                              // ~/.deadreckon (or DEADRECKON_HOME)
429	    pub fn config_path(&self) -> PathBuf                     // home/config.toml
430	    pub fn runstate_dir(&self) -> PathBuf                    // home/runstate
431	    pub fn scope_root(&self, scope: &str) -> PathBuf
432	    pub fn current_pointer_path(&self, scope, task_key) -> PathBuf
433	    pub fn run_root(&self, scope, run_id) -> PathBuf
434	    pub fn locks_dir(&self) -> PathBuf                       // home/locks
435	    pub fn library_dir(&self, scope, run_id) -> PathBuf
436	}
437	```
438	
439	Scope (`paths.rs:67-86`) derives from `DEADRECKON_SCOPE_ROOT` env var, or the nearest `.git` root, or `cwd`. The literal scope string is `"<sanitized-basename>-<fnv1a32-hex>"` of the canonical path — unique per worktree, stable per checkout.
440	
441	Task key (`paths.rs:88-99`) is `"<slug-of-goal>-<fnv1a32-hex-of-goal>"` (slug capped at 48 chars). Two runs with the same goal share a task key (and a lock).

1311	## 19. Configuration & BYOK
1312	
1313	### 19.1 `config.toml`
1314	
1315	Lives at `/Users/gdc/.deadreckon/config.toml` (overridable via `DEADRECKON_HOME`). Schema (`crates/deadreckon-providers/src/types.rs`):
1316	
1317	```rust
1318	pub struct ProviderConfigFile {
1319	    pub default_provider: Option<String>,
1320	    pub fallback: Option<Vec<String>>,
1321	    pub providers: BTreeMap<String, ProviderEntry>,
1322	}
1323	
1324	pub struct ProviderEntry {
1325	    pub kind: Option<ProviderKind>,
1326	    pub api_key: Option<String>,
1327	    pub api_key_env: Option<String>,
1328	    pub base_url: Option<String>,
1329	    pub model: Option<String>,
1330	    pub input_cost_per_million: Option<f64>,
1331	    pub output_cost_per_million: Option<f64>,
1332	    pub binary: Option<String>,
1333	    pub extra_args: Vec<String>,
1334	}
1335	```
1336	
1337	Example:
1338	
1339	```toml
1340	default_provider = "cli:codex"
1341	fallback = ["cli:codex", "cli:claude-code", "anthropic", "openai"]
1342	
1343	[defaults]
1344	max_spend = 10
1345	provider = "cli:codex"
1346	sandbox = "auto"
1347	
1348	[providers."cli:codex"]
1349	binary = "codex"
1350	extra_args = []
1351	kind = "cli-codex"
1352	model = "gpt-5.1-codex" # optional; omitted means provider default
1353	
1354	[providers.anthropic]
1355	api_key_env = "ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"
1356	base_url = "https://api.anthropic.com"
1357	model = "claude-sonnet-4-5"
1358	input_cost_per_million = 3.0
1359	output_cost_per_million = 15.0
1360	```
1361	
1362	Operator affordances: `deadreckon run --preview "goal"` renders the selected
1363	provider route, source, and model before state is created; `run --model <model>`
1364	and `extend --model <model>` override one run; `deadreckon config provider
1365	<route>` and `deadreckon config model <model> --provider <route>` persist the
1366	defaults. `init`, `config provider`, primary run/extend, orchestration roles,
1367	resume/doc polish, and provider-selection display all route through
1368	`crates/deadreckon/src/setup.rs`, which reports provider role, route, model,
1369	source (`flag`, `config`, `auto_subscription`, `run_provider`,
1370	`built_in_default`, or `none`), credential state, warnings, and `try:` lines
1371	without adding durable state. CLI providers pass explicit model overrides
1372	through to the underlying tool (`codex exec --model ...`, `claude --model ...`)
1373	and otherwise display `provider default`.
1374	
1375	Route resolution (`configured_route_names` in `crates/deadreckon-providers/src/router.rs`) now puts `default_provider` at the head of the chain, then appends `fallback` entries that aren't already present, then falls back to the built-in chain (`cli:claude-code` → `cli:codex` → `anthropic` → `openai` → `openai-compatible`) only if neither is configured. `read_config` (`config.rs`) backfills `default_provider` from a top-level `[defaults] provider` key when it's omitted, so the same TOML stanza drives both `init`-style defaults and the router. `--provider` on the CLI still short-circuits the whole chain.
1376	
1377	### 19.2 BYOK posture
1378	
1379	Three credential paths:
1380	
1381	1. **HTTP key.** Set `api_key` directly or `api_key_env = "FOO"` to read at runtime.
1382	2. **CLI subscription.** Run with `--provider cli:claude-code` or `cli:codex`. The binary's presence in `$PATH` is the credential. No key required.
1383	3. **OpenAI-compatible.** Plug an OpenRouter or `llama.cpp` endpoint into `base_url` + `api_key`.
1384	
1385	`deadreckon init` walks the user through option (1) or (2): it queries the provider registry for any subscription CLI provider whose binary is available (`setup::auto_subscription_cli_provider`) and offers the first match — `cli:claude-code`, `cli:codex`, `cli:gemini`, `cli:opencode`, `cli:copilot`, or `cli:pi`, depending on what's installed — before asking for keys. The chosen route is immediately validated through the shared setup resolver, and the generated config preserves a `cli:*` route in the fallback chain rather than overwriting with the historic claude/codex default.
1386

68	        let shutdown = CancellationToken::new();
69	        let task_shutdown = shutdown.clone();
70	        let handle = tokio::spawn(async move {
71	            let mut interval = tokio::time::interval(Duration::from_millis(500));
72	            loop {
73	                tokio::select! {
74	                    _ = task_shutdown.cancelled() => break,
75	                    _ = interval.tick() => recorder.poll(&state)?,
76	                }
77	            }
78	            Ok(recorder)
79	        });
80	        Self { shutdown, handle }

126	        state.turn = from_turn;
127	        save_state(state)?;
128	    }

131	        if should_cancel_run(state, &run_token) {

133	            state.failure_reason = Some("run cancelled".to_string());

138	        let turn_token = run_token.child_token();

703	fn should_cancel_run(state: &PipelineState, token: &CancellationToken) -> bool {
704	    state.status == RunStatus::Killed || token.is_cancelled() || cancel_marker_present(state)
705	}

715	struct CancelMarkerGuard {
716	    shutdown: CancellationToken,
717	    handle: tokio::task::JoinHandle<()>,
718	}
719	
720	impl CancelMarkerGuard {
721	    fn spawn(run_root: &Path, run_token: CancellationToken) -> Self {
722	        let shutdown = CancellationToken::new();
723	        let shutdown_for_task = shutdown.clone();
724	        let marker = cancel_marker_path_for_run_root(run_root);
725	        let handle = tokio::spawn(async move {
726	            loop {
727	                tokio::select! {
728	                    _ = shutdown_for_task.cancelled() => break,
729	                    _ = tokio::time::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(50)) => {
730	                        if marker.exists() {
731	                            run_token.cancel();
732	                            break;
733	                        }
734	                    }
735	                }
736	            }
737	        });
738	        Self { shutdown, handle }
739	    }
740	}
741	
742	impl Drop for CancelMarkerGuard {
743	    fn drop(&mut self) {
744	        self.shutdown.cancel();
745	        self.handle.abort();
746	    }
747	}
748	
749	// SAFETY: `RunLoopOutcome` is the stable event vocabulary used at call sites.
750	#[allow(clippy::needless_pass_by_value)]
751	fn emit_run_completed(
752	    state: &PipelineState,
753	    sender: Option<&broadcast::Sender<RunEvent>>,
754	    outcome: RunLoopOutcome,
755	) -> Result<()> {
756	    let status = match outcome {
757	        RunLoopOutcome::Done => "completed",
758	        RunLoopOutcome::PausedAtCap => "paused",
759	        RunLoopOutcome::Killed => "killed",
760	        RunLoopOutcome::Failed => "failed",
761	    };
762	    emit_event(
763	        state,
764	        sender,
765	        RunEventKind::RunCompleted {
766	            status: status.to_string(),
767	        },
768	    )
769	}

593	## 9. The Turn Loop
594	
595	The load-bearing function lives in `/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon-runtime/src/turn_loop.rs`.
596	
597	### 9.1 `RunLoopConfig`
598	
599	`crates/deadreckon-runtime/src/turn_loop.rs` defines:
600	
601	```rust
602	pub struct RunLoopConfig {
603	    pub provider: Option<String>,
604	    pub max_spend_usd: Option<f64>,
605	    pub max_wall_seconds: Option<f64>,
606	    pub sandbox_backend: SandboxBackend,
607	    pub max_turns: u32,             // hard cap, currently 12
608	    pub from_turn: Option<u32>,     // resume override
609	    pub event_sender: Option<broadcast::Sender<RunEvent>>,
610	    pub cancellation_token: Option<CancellationToken>,
611	}
612	```
613	
614	### 9.2 Top-level signature
615	
616	The top-level signature is:
617	
618	```rust
619	pub async fn run_turn_loop(
620	    state: &mut PipelineState,
621	    router: &ProviderRouter,
622	    config: RunLoopConfig,
623	) -> Result<RunLoopOutcome>
624	```
625	
626	### 9.3 Loop body (paraphrased; see `crates/deadreckon-runtime/src/turn_loop.rs`)
627	
628	```text
629	load_or_reconstruct_history()      # lines 69, 550-631
630	set Phase(40)=Executing            # line 70
631	save_state(); save_history()       # line 71
632	
633	for turn in (state.turn+1)..=max_turns:
634	    if cancelled or status=Killed:
635	        return Killed
636	    emit TurnStarted event
637	    snapshot_working(turn-1)        # capture pre-turn state
638	    prompt = build_prompt(state, history) [or build_cli_subagent_prompt]
639	    request = ProviderRequest{
640	        prompt, max_output_tokens=2048, cwd, output_path, sandbox_backend,
641	        pid_file=run_root/child-pids/provider-turn-N.pid,
642	        cancellation_token=turn_token,
643	    }
644	    response = router.complete(&request).await
645	    append_trace(llm.complete, latency, response.trace)
646	    state.total_spend_usd += response.spend.cost_usd
647	    state.total_wall_seconds += response.spend.wall_time_seconds
648	    append_spend(...)
649	    if max_spend exceeded: return PausedAtCap
650	    if subscription and max_wall_seconds exceeded: return PausedAtCap
651	
652	    if response is cli_subagent:
653	        changed = changed_files_since_snapshot(turn-1)
654	        if changed.is_empty: return Failed
655	        snapshot_working(turn)
656	        append_trace(tool.cli_subagent, files=changed)
657	        append_provenance_for_files(turn, tool_call_id, model, changed)
658	        run_acceptance_gate(state)        # dr-gate
659	        validate_acceptance_marker(state) # signed?
660	        promote_if_ready(state)           # working → library
661	        set Phase(60)=Completed
662	        return Done
663	
664	    parse Action from response.content (serde tag="action"):
665	        Bash { tool_call_id, command } =>
666	            run_sandbox(SandboxSpec{
667	                program=sh, args=[-lc, command], cwd=working_dir,
668	                pid_file, cancellation_token=turn_token.child_token(),
669	                read_allowlist=[working_dir],
670	                allow_network=false,
671	            }).await
672	            append_trace(tool.bash, stdout, stderr, status)
673	            snapshot_working(turn); append_provenance(turn, changed_files)
674	            history.push("tool {id} result: status={...}")
675	        WriteFile { tool_call_id, path, content } =>
676	            safe_working_path(path); write_file
677	            append_trace(tool.write_file); snapshot_working(turn)
678	            append_provenance(turn, [path])
679	            history.push("tool {id} result: wrote file")
680	        Done { summary } =>
681	            run_acceptance_gate; validate_marker; promote_if_ready
682	            set Phase(60)=Completed
683	            return Done
684	
685	    state.turn = turn; save_history(); save_state()
686	
687	# loop exited via max_turns
688	state.failure_reason = Some("max turn budget exhausted")
689	set Phase(40)=Failed; save_state()
690	return Failed
691	```
692	
693	### 9.4 Action enum
694	
695	Inline in `crates/deadreckon-runtime/src/turn_loop.rs` (paraphrased):
696	
697	```rust
698	#[derive(Debug, Deserialize)]
699	#[serde(tag = "action", rename_all = "snake_case")]
700	enum Action {
701	    Bash { tool_call_id: String, command: String },
702	    WriteFile { tool_call_id: String, path: PathBuf, content: String },
703	    Done { summary: Option<String> },
704	}
705	```
706	
707	Providers return JSON; the loop parses one action per turn. The CLI sub-agent path is detected by `response.trace["kind"] == "cli_subagent"` before action parsing — those providers do their own tool calls inside the subprocess and return a narrative, not an action JSON.
708	
709	### 9.5 No smoke fallback in the default path
710	
711	`grep -r "coding_turn_script\|hardcoded_smoke" /Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/` returns empty. The deterministic-script path lives entirely inside `ScriptedSmokeProvider` (`crates/deadreckon-providers/src/smoke.rs`), reachable only via `deadreckon run --smoke` (which selects the `smoke` provider, not via a bypass of the run loop).
712	
713	### 9.6 Error handling
714	
715	The loop does **not** retry on errors:
716	
717	- Provider error → propagates and the run fails.
718	- Tool-call non-zero exit → result fed back to history, next turn's prompt sees the failure; the model decides whether to retry.
719	- Acceptance failure → run fails; no auto-retry.
720	
721	The bound is `max_turns` (currently 12), not an error budget.
722

```text
725	## 10. Provider Model
726	
727	### 10.1 The `Provider` trait
728	
729	`crates/deadreckon-providers/src/types.rs`:
730	
731	```rust
732	pub trait Provider: Send + Sync {
733	    fn name(&self) -> &str;
734	    fn kind(&self) -> ProviderKind;
735	    fn model(&self) -> &str;
736	    fn has_credential(&self) -> bool;
737	    fn estimate_spend(&self, usage: ProviderUsage) -> SpendEstimate;
738	    fn complete<'a>(&'a self, request: &'a ProviderRequest) -> ProviderFuture<'a>;
739	}
740	```
741	
742	`ProviderRequest` (`types.rs:89`) carries: `prompt`, `max_output_tokens`, optional `cwd`, optional `output_path`, optional `sandbox_backend`, optional `pid_file`, optional `cancellation_token`.
743	
744	`ProviderResponse` (`types.rs:100`) carries: `provider`, `model`, `content`, `usage`, `spend`, `trace` (JSON value).
745	
746	### 10.2 Kinds
747	
748	`types.rs:18`:
749	
750	```rust
751	pub enum ProviderKind {
752	    Anthropic,
753	    OpenAi,
754	    OpenAiCompatible,
755	    CliClaudeCode,
756	    CliCodex,
757	    ScriptedSmoke,
758	    Generic(String),
759	}
760	```
761	
762	### 10.3 HTTP adapters
763	
764	A single `ProviderAdapter` (`lib.rs:135-323`) handles all three HTTP kinds via shared `reqwest::Client`:
765	
766	| Kind | Endpoint | Auth header | Default model |
767	|---|---|---|---|
768	| Anthropic | `{base_url}/v1/messages` | `x-api-key: <key>` + `anthropic-version: 2023-06-01` | `claude-sonnet-4-5` |
769	| OpenAI | `{base_url}/chat/completions` | `Authorization: Bearer <key>` | configurable |
770	| OpenAI-compatible | `{base_url}/chat/completions` | `Authorization: Bearer <key>` | configurable |
771	
772	Pricing defaults (`lib.rs:531-617`): Anthropic $3/$15 per million in/out; OpenAI $1.25/$10 per million; OpenAI-compatible $0/$0 (user-configured).
773	
774	Response parsing: `parse_anthropic_response` (`lib.rs:688-705`) extracts `content[0].text` + `usage.{input_tokens, output_tokens}`; `parse_openai_response` (`lib.rs:669-686`) extracts `choices[0].message.content` + `usage.{prompt_tokens, completion_tokens}`. The `Action` tag-typed enum is parsed in the **turn loop**, not the provider; providers return text.
775	
776	Cancellation: `tokio::select!` on `token.cancelled()` vs `client.post().send()` (`lib.rs:226-263`).
777	
778	### 10.4 CLI sub-agent adapters
779	
780	**`cli:claude-code` (`crates/deadreckon-providers/src/cli_claude_code.rs:1-127`).** Invocation:
781	
782	```zsh
783	claude [--model <model>] --dangerously-skip-permissions -p "<prompt>"
784	```
785	
786	The `--dangerously-skip-permissions` flag is non-negotiable (no human is in the loop). The subprocess runs **inside** the deadreckon sandbox profile, so Claude's bypass only disables its own permission gate; deadreckon's outer Seatbelt/bwrap still scopes the process. Stdout is captured to `request.output_path` (the turn's `claude.out`).
787	
788	**`cli:codex` (`crates/deadreckon-providers/src/cli_codex.rs:1-143`).** Invocation:
789	
790	```zsh
791	codex --ask-for-approval never exec --skip-git-repo-check --sandbox <mode> -- "<prompt>"
792	```
793	
794	`<mode>` (`cli_codex.rs:121-131`) is `workspace-write` when the outer sandbox is `None`/`SandboxBackend::None` (safer, codex limits itself to cwd), and `danger-full-access` when an outer sandbox is active (the outer sandbox is doing the isolating; codex needs full filesystem access inside).
795	
796	The trailing `--` delimiter is non-negotiable: doc-polish prompts often begin with YAML frontmatter (`---`), which `clap`-based Codex CLIs otherwise interpret as an option-like argument. Adding `--` forces the prompt to be parsed as the positional value.
797	
798	**Descriptor-backed CLI providers.** The provider registry now owns compiled-in TOML descriptors plus `providers.d` overrides. Generic CLI descriptors (`ProviderKind::Generic(id)` where the descriptor kind is `cli`) are launched by `GenericCliProvider`, which renders `exec_template.args_template` with `{prompt}`, `{sandbox}`, and `{cwd}` placeholders and applies the descriptor `model_arg` near the prompt without splitting prompt-value flags like `-p <prompt>`. `cli:gemini`, `cli:opencode`, `cli:copilot`, and `cli:pi` are built-in generic CLIs; `cli:claude-code` and `cli:codex` remain concrete adapters for compatibility with their established launch quirks. Copilot launches as `copilot -p <prompt> --output-format json --stream off --no-color --allow-all`; Pi launches as `pi --mode json --print <prompt>` so its default saved sessions remain available to the TUI.
799	
800	**Shared subprocess machinery (`cli_common.rs:22-120`).** Builds a `SandboxSpec` with explicit allowlists (`cli_common.rs:154-166`):
801	
802	- Write allowlist: descriptor `sandbox_writes` for registered CLIs, with concrete compatibility fallbacks for codex and claude.
803	- Read allowlist: binary location + `~/.bun`, `~/.local`, `~/.npm-global`, `~/.opencode`.
804	- `allow_network: true` (CLI agents need outbound for their own API calls).
805	
806	**Spend (subscription).** Per `cli_claude_code.rs:100-110` and the equivalent in `cli_codex.rs`:
807	
808	```rust
809	SpendEstimate {
810	    cost_usd: 0.0,
811	    subscription: true,
812	    wall_time_seconds: Some(elapsed),
813	}
814	```
815	
816	The wall-clock is what `--max-wall-seconds` caps (§9.3).
817	
818	### 10.5 Scripted smoke provider
819	
820	`crates/deadreckon-providers/src/smoke.rs`. In-memory `VecDeque<String>` initialized with three responses:
821	
822	1. `{"action": "bash", "tool_call_id": "smoke-bash-1", "command": "..."}`
823	2. `{"action": "write_file", "tool_call_id": "smoke-write-2", "path": "README.md", "content": "..."}`
824	3. `{"action": "done", "summary": "tiny Rust project created"}`
825	
826	Zero cost, no subscription. Reachable only via `--smoke` flag. The trace records `{"kind": "scripted_smoke", "remaining_steps": N}`.
827	
828	### 10.6 `ProviderRouter` and fallback chain
829	
830	`crates/deadreckon-providers/src/router.rs`. Reads config (TOML), loads the provider registry with `providers.d` overrides, resolves a route list (`fallback` array > `default_provider` > built-in chain `cli:claude-code` → `cli:codex` → `anthropic` → `openai` → `openai-compatible`), and constructs a `Box<dyn Provider>` per route. Concrete providers handle Anthropic/OpenAI/OpenAI-compatible/smoke/Codex/Claude; descriptor-backed generic CLI providers handle any registered CLI descriptor that does not need a concrete adapter. On `complete()`:
831	
832	```rust
833	for route in &self.routes {
834	    if !route.has_credential() { failures.push(...); continue; }
835	    match route.complete(request).await {
836	        Ok(resp) => return Ok(resp),
837	        Err(e) => failures.push(format!("{}: {e}", route.name())),
838	    }
839	}
840	Err(ProviderError::NoRoute(failures.join("; ")))
841	```
842	
843	First credentialed route to succeed wins. All errors aggregate into the failure message.
844

```text
51	## 1. System Overview & Mental Model
52	
53	deadreckon is a Rust 2024 CLI harness whose default flow is **unattended long-running coding tasks**: `deadreckon run <goal>` creates durable run state, picks a BYOK provider route, executes turns inside a platform-native sandbox, writes spend/provenance/trace records after every turn, and exits only when the LLM declares done, a budget caps the run, or the operator kills it. The CLI is the user-facing layer; `deadreckon-runtime` owns orchestration across providers, sandboxes, docs, and promotion; `deadreckon-core` owns deterministic primitives and durable schemas.
54	
55	```
56	┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
57	│ USER                                                                      │
58	│ deadreckon run "make a hello-world Rust binary" --max-spend 5             │
59	└────────────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────────────┘
60	                                 │
61	┌────────────────────────────────▼──────────────────────────────────────────┐
62	│ CLI LAYER (crates/deadreckon)                                             │
63	│   cli.rs       clap parser definitions                                    │
64	│   main.rs      command handlers, ratatui rendering, post-run summary       │
65	└────────────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────────────┘
66	                                 │ create_run → acquire_lock → runtime loop
67	                                 ▼
68	┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
69	│ RUNTIME ORCHESTRATION (crates/deadreckon-runtime)                         │
70	│                                                                           │
71	│  turn_loop.rs  provider turns, sandboxed tool dispatch, cancellation,      │
72	│                acceptance gate invocation, promotion orchestration         │
73	│  polish.rs     optional end-of-run doc polish via a doc-provider           │
74	└──┬──────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────┬────────────────┘
75	   │ durable primitives       │ ProviderRouter::complete  │ run_sandbox
76	   ▼                          ▼                          ▼
77	┌──────────────────────────┐  ┌──────────────────────┐  ┌──────────────────────┐
78	│ CORE LIBRARY             │  │ PROVIDERS            │  │ SANDBOX              │
79	│ state, paths, locks      │  │ HTTP: anthropic,     │  │ sandbox-exec, bwrap, │
80	│ artifacts, docs, events  │  │ openai, compatible   │  │ docker, none, auto   │
81	│ gate, promotion, chains  │  │ CLI: claude, codex   │  │ policy, PID/cancel   │
82	│ adapter-free schemas     │  │ TEST: smoke          │  │ doctor checks        │
83	└────────────┬─────────────┘  └──────────┬───────────┘  └──────────┬───────────┘
84	             │                           │                         │
85	             └───────────────────────────┴─────────────┬───────────┘
86	                                                       ▼
87	┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
88	│ RUNTIME STATE (~/.deadreckon/)                                            │
89	│ runstate/<scope>/runs/<run-id>, library/<scope>/<run-id>, locks, config   │
90	└───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
91	```
92	
93	Why this shape works:
94	
95	- **The CLI is thin.** It parses args, sets up state, hands off to `deadreckon-runtime`, and prints summaries. Durable schemas and atomic file operations live in `deadreckon-core`.
96	- **State is on disk before every meaningful change.** `state.json` is atomic-written via temp+rename after every phase transition, snapshot, spend record, and tool call.
97	- **The agent cannot mark its own gate.** `dr-gate` is a separate binary that signs an acceptance marker against a nonce only it can read; the deadreckon binary refuses to mark a run `Completed` without that signed marker.
98	- **Sandboxes are platform-native.** macOS uses Seatbelt; Linux uses Bubblewrap; Docker is opt-in. No daemon, no `bollard`, no Lima.
99	- **BYOK extends to subscriptions.** Subscription-bearing users drive deadreckon by routing turns through their local `claude` or `codex` CLIs; no API key required.

fn start_or_coalesce_run_narrative_refresh_job(
    job: &mut Option<AttachRunNarrativeRefreshJob>,
    request: AttachRunNarrativeRefreshRequest,
    now: DateTime<Utc>,
) -> String {
    if let Some(active) = job.as_mut() {
        return active.state.coalesce(request.kind, now);
    }

    let token = CancellationToken::new();
    let refresh_state = AttachNarrativeRefreshState::new(request.kind, now, token.clone());
    let notice = refresh_state.start_notice();
    let handle = tokio::spawn(async move {
        let AttachRunNarrativeRefreshRequest {
            paths,
            state,
            spend,
            traces,
            events,
            live,
            tui_state,
            config,
            kind,
        } = request;
        refresh_run_narrative_with_provider_for_kind_with_token(
            &paths,
            &RunNarrativeRenderInput {
                state: &state,
                spend: &spend,
                traces: &traces,
                events: &events,
                live: &live,
                tui_state: &tui_state,
            },
            &config,
            kind,
            Some(token),
        )
        .await
        .unwrap_or_else(|err| {
            format!(
                "provider refresh failed: {}",
                one_line(&err.to_string(), 120)
            )
        })
    });
    *job = Some(AttachRunNarrativeRefreshJob {
        state: refresh_state,
        handle,
    });
    notice
}

fn start_or_coalesce_plan_narrative_refresh_job(
    job: &mut Option<AttachPlanNarrativeRefreshJob>,
    request: AttachPlanNarrativeRefreshRequest,
    now: DateTime<Utc>,
) -> String {
    if let Some(active) = job.as_mut()
        && active.plan_id == request.plan.plan_id
    {
        return active.state.coalesce(request.kind, now);
    }
    cancel_plan_narrative_refresh_job(job);

    let token = CancellationToken::new();
    let plan_id = request.plan.plan_id.clone();
    let refresh_state = AttachNarrativeRefreshState::new(request.kind, now, token.clone());
    let notice = refresh_state.start_notice();
    let handle = tokio::spawn(async move {
        let AttachPlanNarrativeRefreshRequest {
            paths,
            plan,
            messages,
            plan_events,
            feed_events,
            selected,
            config,
            kind,
        } = request;
        refresh_plan_narrative_with_provider_for_kind(PlanNarrativeProviderRefresh {
            paths: &paths,
            plan: &plan,
            messages: &messages,
            plan_events: &plan_events,
            feed_events: &feed_events,
            selected,
            config: &config,
            kind,
            cancellation_token: Some(token),
        })
        .await
        .unwrap_or_else(|err| {
            format!(
                "provider refresh failed: {}",
                one_line(&err.to_string(), 120)
            )
        })
    });
    *job = Some(AttachPlanNarrativeRefreshJob {
        plan_id,
        state: refresh_state,
        handle,
    });
    notice
}

async fn poll_run_narrative_refresh_job(
    job: &mut Option<AttachRunNarrativeRefreshJob>,
) -> Option<String> {
    if !job
        .as_ref()
        .is_some_and(|active| active.handle.is_finished())
    {
        return None;
    }
    let AttachRunNarrativeRefreshJob { mut state, handle } = job.take()?;
    match handle.await {
        Ok(notice) => state.completion_notice_once(notice),
        Err(err) if err.is_cancelled() => None,
        Err(err) => Some(format!(
            "provider refresh failed: {}",
            one_line(&err.to_string(), 120)
        )),
    }
}

async fn poll_plan_narrative_refresh_job(
    job: &mut Option<AttachPlanNarrativeRefreshJob>,
) -> Option<String> {
    if !job
        .as_ref()
        .is_some_and(|active| active.handle.is_finished())
    {
        return None;
    }
    let AttachPlanNarrativeRefreshJob {
        mut state, handle, ..
    } = job.take()?;
    match handle.await {
        Ok(notice) => state.completion_notice_once(notice),
        Err(err) if err.is_cancelled() => None,
        Err(err) => Some(format!(
            "provider refresh failed: {}",
            one_line(&err.to_string(), 120)
        )),
    }
}

fn cancel_run_narrative_refresh_job(job: &mut Option<AttachRunNarrativeRefreshJob>) -> bool {
    let Some(active) = job.take() else {
        return false;
    };
    active.state.cancel();
    active.handle.abort();
    true
}

fn cancel_plan_narrative_refresh_job(job: &mut Option<AttachPlanNarrativeRefreshJob>) -> bool {
    let Some(active) = job.take() else {
        return false;
    };
    active.state.cancel();
```

847	## 11. Sandbox Model
848	
849	`crates/deadreckon-sandbox/src/lib.rs` is a public facade over focused modules that abstract four backends behind one entry point.
850	
851	### 11.1 `SandboxBackend`
852	
853	`crates/deadreckon-sandbox/src/backend.rs`:
854	
855	```rust
856	#[serde(rename_all = "kebab-case")]
857	pub enum SandboxBackend {
858	    Auto,
859	    SandboxExec,
860	    Bwrap,
861	    Docker,
862	    None,
863	}
864	```
865	
866	### 11.2 Auto resolution
867	
868	`lib.rs:208-244`. Platform-conditional:
869	
870	- macOS: probes `sandbox-exec` via `which`. Falls back to `None` with a warning if unavailable.
871	- Linux: probes `bwrap`. Falls back to `None` with a warning.
872	- Other: `None` with platform-unavailable warning.
873	
874	The fallback to `None` is loud — the warning ends up in `SandboxRunOutput.warning` and is surfaced in the trace.
875	
876	### 11.3 `run(SandboxSpec) -> SandboxRunOutput`
877	
878	`lib.rs:111-169` is the single dispatch entry point. It:
879	
880	1. Calls `build_command(spec)` to construct the per-backend invocation.
881	2. Spawns the child via `tokio::process::Command`, capturing stdout + stderr piped.
882	3. Persists the child PID to `spec.pid_file` (line 129) for `kill` supervision.
883	4. Reads stdout/stderr in parallel async tasks (`read_pipe`, lines 171–181).
884	5. Runs the cancellation `tokio::select!` (lines 131–151).
885	6. Returns `SandboxRunOutput { stdout, stderr, status_code, pid, backend, warning }`.
886	
887	### 11.4 macOS Seatbelt profile
888	
889	`lib.rs:390-441` generates a per-run profile string:
890	
891	```
892	(version 1)
893	(allow default)
894	{ssh_deny}                    ; deny file-read* / file-write* (subpath "$HOME/.ssh")
895	{network}                     ; (deny network*) unless allow_network=true
896	(allow file-read*
897	{read_rules})                 ; cwd + system framework subpaths + spec.read_allowlist
898	(allow file-write*
899	    (subpath "<cwd>")
900	    (subpath "/private/tmp")
901	    (subpath "/tmp")
902	{write_rules})                ; spec.write_allowlist
903	```
904	
905	Optionally writes the profile to `spec.profile_dir` for debugging (`lib.rs:436-439`). Otherwise inline via `sandbox-exec -p '<profile>' -- <program> <args...>`.
906	
907	### 11.5 Linux Bubblewrap
908	
909	`lib.rs:303-357`. Constructs `bwrap` args with:
910	
911	- `--die-with-parent --unshare-pid --unshare-ipc --unshare-uts`
912	- `--tmpfs <cwd>/.deadreckon-home` and `--setenv HOME <cwd>/.deadreckon-home` (ephemeral tmpfs `$HOME`)
913	- `--ro-bind <path> <path>` for each entry in `system_read_allowlist(cwd, spec.read_allowlist)`
914	- `--bind <path> <path>` for each entry in `spec.write_allowlist`
915	- `--bind <cwd> <cwd>`, `--proc /proc`, `--dev /dev`, `--chdir <cwd>`
916	- `--unshare-net` unless `allow_network=true`
917	
918	### 11.6 Docker
919	
920	`lib.rs:359-388`. Constructs `docker run --rm -v <cwd>:<cwd> -w <cwd> [--network none] [-e KEY=VAL]... rust:1 <program> <args...>`. Hardcoded base image is `rust:1`. Only the cwd is mounted.
921	
922	### 11.7 None
923	
924	`lib.rs:191-203`. No isolation. Always returns a warning: `"sandbox backend none is unsafe; use only for explicit local verification"`. The warning lands in the trace.
925	
926	### 11.8 SIGTERM/SIGKILL escalation
927	
928	`lib.rs:131-151`:
929	
930	```rust
931	if let Some(token) = spec.cancellation_token.as_ref() {
932	    tokio::select! {
933	        _ = token.cancelled() => {
934	            if let Some(pid) = pid {
935	                signal_pid(pid, false);                      // SIGTERM
936	                sleep(Duration::from_secs(2)).await;         // 2s grace
937	                if child.try_wait()?.is_none() {
938	                    signal_pid(pid, true);                   // SIGKILL
939	                }
940	            }
941	            let _ = child.wait().await;
942	            if let Some(pid_file) = spec.pid_file.as_ref() {
943	                let _ = tokio::fs::remove_file(pid_file).await;
944	            }
945	            return Err(SandboxError::Cancelled);
946	        }
947	        status = child.wait() => status
948	    }
949	}
950	```
951	
952	`signal_pid` is defined at `lib.rs:473-483` (uses `nix::sys::signal::kill`).
953	
954	---
955	
956	## 12. Cancellation & Supervision
957	
958	### 12.1 Cancellation tokens
959	
960	The turn loop owns `run_token = CancellationToken::new()`; per turn it creates `turn_token = run_token.child_token()`; per tool call it can further create `tool_token = turn_token.child_token()`. The token threads through:
961	
962	- HTTP providers: `tokio::select!` on `token.cancelled()` vs the `reqwest` future.
963	- CLI providers: passed to `cli_common::run_cli` → `SandboxSpec.cancellation_token` → the sandbox layer.
964	- Tool dispatch (`Action::Bash`): passed to `run_sandbox(SandboxSpec { cancellation_token: Some(tool_token), ... })`.
965	
966	### 12.2 Child PID supervision
967	
968	Multiple sources contribute PIDs to track:
969	
970	- `state.child_pids: Vec<u32>` — populated by the CLI itself (`main.rs:333`).
971	- Per-subprocess PID files at `run_root/child-pids/*.pid` — written by the sandbox layer (`lib.rs:129`) and read by `supervised_pids()` (`main.rs:923`).
972	
973	`kill_command` reads both, releases the lock, sets `state.status = Killed`, and signals every PID. Without `--escalate`, it tries the graceful signal, waits 1.5s, then SIGKILLs anything still alive.
974	
975	### 12.3 What `kill` cannot do
976

```text
2085	
2086	`deadreckon learn export <run-id|proposal-id> --redacted` writes a redacted JSON bundle with section hashes for episodes, signals, insights, and proposals. `deadreckon learn import-bundle <path> --preview` verifies schema, redaction, and hashes without writing state; `--yes` imports the bundle into the local learning files. Bundles redact `DEADRECKON_HOME`, project/home paths, and secret-like values, and they do not contain raw provider logs.
2087	
2088	### 34.3 Self-Run Candidates
2089	
2090	`deadreckon improve self <proposal-id|goal-file> --preview` prints the proposal, isolated-worktree posture, done criteria, provider resolver posture, and PR mode without side effects. `--yes` requires a clean source worktree, refuses a configured `defaults.sandbox = "none"` unless local learning policy allows it, creates `deadreckon/self/<candidate-id>` in a git worktree under `DEADRECKON_HOME/learning/candidates/<candidate-id>/worktree`, writes focused self-run acceptance criteria, then launches a normal `deadreckon run` in that isolated worktree using the existing provider resolver. The coordinator commits candidate changes locally with a deterministic author, records changed files and diff stats, runs focused learning verification, computes an evidence score, performs a simple redaction/secrets scan over the candidate diff, and writes candidate/eval/evidence files.
2091	
2092	### 34.4 Evidence-Gated PR Opening
2093	
2094	`deadreckon improve self <proposal-id> --pr-dry-run` finds the latest candidate for that proposal, evaluates the same evidence gate used by live open, writes the exact PR title/body to the candidate directory, and appends `pr-events.jsonl` without network or push. `--open-pr` first runs the same evidence gate, then calls a small PR adapter; the production adapter pushes the candidate branch and calls `gh pr create` with the generated body only if the gate is eligible. Tests use a fake adapter and verify it is not called when the gate refuses.
2095	
2096	The gate requires explicit opt-in, isolated worktree evidence, non-empty proposal done criteria, accepted self-run, focused verification passing, redaction passing, an evidence score at or above policy, a changed head commit, and no high-risk paths when high-risk blocking is enabled. High-risk paths include acceptance/gate code, sandbox code, provider credential/config handling, release workflows/scripts, and privacy/redaction weakening. PR bodies are fixed-section evidence packets: Summary, Stimulus and Proposal, Evidence Packet, Verification, Risk Classification, Rollback, and Files Changed.
2097	
2098	### 34.5 Privacy, Redaction, And Limits
2099	
2100	Learning is local-first. No cloud sync, background telemetry, raw provider logs, credentials, or home-directory paths are exported by default. Provider-backed reflection sees redacted episode/signal summaries rather than raw provider-owned logs. Imported-only evidence can produce proposals, but it is not enough by itself to justify live PR opening without local corroborating run evidence. The alpha implementation does not train or fine-tune models, run multi-candidate evolutionary search, automatically change provider routing defaults, auto-merge into `main`, provide a learning TUI dashboard, or make audit logs cryptographically tamper-proof. Those remain V1 candidates.

async fn attach_tui(
    paths: &DeadreckonPaths,
    run_id: &str,
    show_completion_actions: bool,
    initial_view: AttachViewMode,
    initial_visual: NarrativeVisualMode,
    narrative_config: NarrativeAttachConfig,
) -> Result<()> {
    attach_tui_with_parent(
        paths,
        run_id,
        show_completion_actions,
        None,
        initial_view,
        initial_visual,
        narrative_config,
    )
    .await
}

async fn attach_tui_with_parent(
    paths: &DeadreckonPaths,
    run_id: &str,
    show_completion_actions: bool,
    parent_plan: Option<AttachParentPlan>,
    initial_view: AttachViewMode,
    initial_visual: NarrativeVisualMode,
    narrative_config: NarrativeAttachConfig,
) -> Result<()> {
    let initial_state = load_run(paths, run_id)?;
    let mut event_feed =
        tui_events::TuiEventFeed::file_tail(initial_state.run_root.join(RUN_EVENTS_JSONL));
    let mut events = event_feed.refresh(std::time::Duration::ZERO).await?;
    enable_raw_mode()?;
    let mut stdout = io::stdout();
    execute!(stdout, EnterAlternateScreen, EnableMouseCapture)?;
    let backend = CrosstermBackend::new(stdout);
    let mut terminal = Terminal::new(backend)?;
    let mut tui_state = AttachTuiState {
        show_completion_actions,
        parent_plan,
        view: initial_view,
        visual: initial_visual,
        ..AttachTuiState::default()
    };
    let mut quiet_tracker = NarrativeQuietRefreshTracker::new(Utc::now());
    let mut acceptance_tracker = NarrativeAcceptanceRefreshTracker::default();
