321	pub fn capture_diff_samples(
322	    state: &PipelineState,
323	    turn: u32,
324	    files: &[PathBuf],
325	) -> Result<Vec<FileChange>> {
326	    let previous_root = state
327	        .run_root
328	        .join("snapshots")
329	        .join(format!("turn-{}", turn.saturating_sub(1)));
330	    let mut changes = Vec::new();
331	    let mut seen = BTreeSet::new();
332	    for path in files {
333	        let Some(relative) = normalize_file(state, path) else {
334	            continue;
335	        };
336	        if !seen.insert(relative.clone()) {
337	            continue;
338	        }
339	        let current = if path.is_absolute() {
340	            path.clone()
341	        } else {
342	            state.working_dir.join(path)
343	        };
344	        let previous = previous_root.join(&relative);
345	        changes.push(diff_sample_for_file(&relative, &previous, &current)?);
346	    }
347	    Ok(changes)
348	}

350	pub fn read_turn_records(working_dir: &Path) -> Result<Vec<TurnRecord>> {
351	    let path = incremental_path(working_dir);
352	    if !path.exists() {
353	        return Ok(Vec::new());
354	    }
355	    let raw = fs::read_to_string(&path).with_path(&path)?;
356	    let mut records = Vec::new();
357	    for line in raw.lines().filter(|line| !line.trim().is_empty()) {
358	        records.push(
359	            serde_json::from_str(line).map_err(|source| DeadreckonError::Json {
360	                path: path.clone(),
361	                source,
362	            })?,
363	        );
364	    }
365	    Ok(records)
366	}

368	pub fn rewrite_templated_docs(state: &PipelineState, doc_writer: &str) -> Result<()> {
369	    fs::create_dir_all(docs_dir(&state.working_dir)).with_path(docs_dir(&state.working_dir))?;
370	    let records = read_turn_records(&state.working_dir)?;
371	    let parent = parent_run_id(&state.working_dir);
372	    let fields = FrontmatterFields {
373	        last_updated: Utc::now(),
374	        doc_writer: doc_writer.to_string(),
375	        parent_run_id: parent.clone(),
376	    };
377	    write_file(
378	        narrative_path(&state.working_dir),
379	        render_narrative(state, &fields, &records, parent.as_deref()),
380	    )?;
381	    write_file(
382	        as_built_path(&state.working_dir),
383	        render_as_built(state, &fields, &records),
384	    )?;
385	    write_file(
386	        decisions_path(&state.working_dir),
387	        render_decisions(state, &fields, &records),
388	    )?;
389	    maybe_write_delta(state, &records)?;
390	    Ok(())
391	}

393	pub fn publish_docs_for_promotion(state: &PipelineState) -> Result<()> {
394	    let internal = docs_dir(&state.working_dir);
395	    if !internal.is_dir() {
396	        return Ok(());
397	    }
398	    let public = public_docs_dir(&state.working_dir);
399	    fs::create_dir_all(&public).with_path(&public)?;
400	    for name in [RUN_NARRATIVE, RUN_AS_BUILT, RUN_DECISIONS, AS_BUILT_DELTA] {
401	        let source = internal.join(name);
402	        if source.exists() {
403	            let dest = public.join(name);
404	            if name == RUN_DECISIONS {
405	                let mut raw = fs::read_to_string(&source).with_path(&source)?;
406	                if implementation_notes_path(&state.working_dir).exists() {
407	                    raw = raw.replace(
408	                        &format!("](../../{IMPLEMENTATION_NOTES_HTML})"),
409	                        &format!("](../{IMPLEMENTATION_NOTES_HTML})"),
410	                    );
411	                }
412	                write_file(dest, raw)?;
413	            } else {
414	                fs::copy(&source, dest).with_path(&source)?;
415	            }
416	        }
417	    }
418	    if delta_path(&state.working_dir).exists() {
419	        let named = format!("AS-BUILT-DELTA-{}.md", short_id(&state.run_id));
420	        fs::copy(delta_path(&state.working_dir), public.join(named))
421	            .with_path(delta_path(&state.working_dir))?;
422	    }
423	    mirror_trace_file(state)?;
424	    commit_docs_if_worktree(state)?;
425	    Ok(())
426	}

428	pub fn docs_status_for_state(state: &PipelineState) -> DocsStatus {
429	    let path = polish_path(&state.working_dir);
430	    if path.exists()
431	        && let Ok(raw) = fs::read_to_string(&path)
432	        && let Ok(value) = serde_json::from_str::<serde_json::Value>(&raw)
433	    {
434	        return match value.get("status").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str) {
435	            Some("polished") => DocsStatus::Polished,
436	            Some("incremental") | Some("skipped") => DocsStatus::Incremental,
437	            Some(_) => DocsStatus::Failed,
438	            None => DocsStatus::Incremental,
439	        };
440	    }
441	    if narrative_path(&state.working_dir).exists()
442	        || public_doc_path(&state.working_dir, RUN_NARRATIVE).exists()
443	    {
444	        DocsStatus::Incremental
445	    } else {
446	        DocsStatus::NotAvailable
447	    }
448	}

453	    if public.exists() {
454	        return Some(public);
455	    }
456	    let internal = docs_dir(working_dir).join(file);
457	    if internal.exists() {
458	        return Some(internal);
459	    }
460	    None
461	}

483	pub enum ImplementationNotesStatus {
484	    Current,
485	    Missing,
486	    MissingSections(Vec<&'static str>),
487	    Stale {
488	        notes_turn: Option<u32>,
489	        implementation_turn: u32,
490	    },
491	}
492	
493	impl ImplementationNotesStatus {
494	    pub fn is_current(&self) -> bool {
495	        matches!(self, Self::Current)
496	    }
497	
498	    pub fn reason(&self) -> String {
499	        match self {
500	            Self::Current => "implementation notes are current".to_string(),
501	            Self::Missing => format!("{IMPLEMENTATION_NOTES_HTML} is missing"),
502	            Self::MissingSections(sections) => {
503	                format!(
504	                    "{IMPLEMENTATION_NOTES_HTML} is missing required sections: {}",
505	                    sections.join(", ")
506	                )
507	            }
508	            Self::Stale {
509	                notes_turn,
510	                implementation_turn,
511	            } => format!(
512	                "{IMPLEMENTATION_NOTES_HTML} is stale; latest notes turn {}, latest implementation turn {implementation_turn}",
513	                notes_turn
514	                    .map(|turn| turn.to_string())
515	                    .unwrap_or_else(|| "none".to_string())
516	            ),
517	        }
518	    }
519	}

521	pub fn check_implementation_notes_current(
522	    state: &PipelineState,
523	) -> Result<ImplementationNotesStatus> {
524	    let path = implementation_notes_path(&state.working_dir);
525	    if !path.exists() {
526	        return Ok(ImplementationNotesStatus::Missing);
527	    }
528	    let raw = fs::read_to_string(&path).with_path(&path)?;
529	    let missing = missing_implementation_note_sections(&raw);
530	    if !missing.is_empty() {
531	        return Ok(ImplementationNotesStatus::MissingSections(missing));
532	    }
533	    let records = read_turn_records(&state.working_dir)?;
534	    let notes_turn = latest_notes_turn(&records);
535	    let implementation_turn = latest_implementation_turn(&records);
536	    if let Some(implementation_turn) = implementation_turn
537	        && notes_turn
538	            .map(|notes_turn| notes_turn < implementation_turn)
539	            .unwrap_or(true)
540	    {
541	        return Ok(ImplementationNotesStatus::Stale {
542	            notes_turn,
543	            implementation_turn,
544	        });
545	    }
546	    Ok(ImplementationNotesStatus::Current)
547	}

549	pub fn coalesce_into_phases(records: &[TurnRecord]) -> Vec<Phase> {
550	    if records.is_empty() {
551	        return Vec::new();
552	    }
553	    let mut groups: Vec<Vec<TurnRecord>> = Vec::new();
554	    let mut current = vec![records[0].clone()];
555	    for turn in records.iter().skip(1) {
556	        let overlap = file_overlap(&current, turn);
557	        let same_kind_run = same_tool_kind_consecutive_count(&current, &turn.tool_kind);
558	        if overlap > 0.5 || same_kind_run > 0 && same_kind_run < 3 {
559	            current.push(turn.clone());
560	        } else {
561	            groups.push(current);
562	            current = vec![turn.clone()];
563	        }
564	    }
565	    groups.push(current);
566	    while groups.len() > 8 {
567	        let idx = smallest_neighbor_index(&groups);
568	        let next = groups.remove(idx + 1);
569	        groups[idx].extend(next);
570	    }
571	    groups
572	        .into_iter()
573	        .enumerate()
574	        .map(|(index, turns)| phase_from_group(index + 1, turns))
575	        .collect()
576	}

587	pub fn auto_title(response: &str, tool_kind: &str, files: &[String], turn: u32) -> String {
588	    if let Some(capture) = ill_regex().captures(response)
589	        && let Some(value) = capture.get(1)
590	    {
591	        return title_case_words(value.as_str(), 6);
592	    }
593	    if let Some(file) = files.first() {
594	        let basename = Path::new(file)
595	            .file_name()
596	            .and_then(|name| name.to_str())
597	            .unwrap_or(file);
598	        return match tool_kind {
599	            "write_file" => format!("Write {basename}"),
600	            "bash" => format!("Run {basename}"),
601	            "cli_subagent" => format!("Edit {basename}"),
602	            other => format!("{} {}", title_case_words(other, 2), basename),
603	        };
604	    }
605	    match tool_kind {
606	        "bash" => "Run command".to_string(),
607	        "done" => "Complete run".to_string(),
608	        _ => format!("Turn {turn}"),
609	    }
610	}

638	pub fn source_layout(records: &[TurnRecord], working_dir: &Path) -> String {
639	    let files = all_files(records);
640	    let mut out = String::new();
641	    out.push_str("| Layer | Responsibilities | Key entrypoints |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n");
642	    let component_rows = component_rows(records);
643	    if component_rows.is_empty() {
644	        out.push_str("| (none inferred) | No mapped component paths changed | - |\n");
645	    } else {
646	        for row in component_rows {
647	            out.push_str(&format!(
648	                "| {} | {} | `{}` |\n",
649	                row.layer, row.responsibility, row.entrypoint
650	            ));
651	        }
652	    }
653	    if let Some(topology) = topology_for_files(working_dir, &files) {
654	        out.push_str("\n```text\n");
655	        out.push_str(&topology);
656	        out.push_str("\n```\n");
657	    }
658	    out
659	}

661	pub fn diff_samples_markdown(records: &[TurnRecord]) -> String {
662	    let mut out = String::new();
663	    for record in records {
664	        let files = record
665	            .files
666	            .iter()
667	            .filter(|file| is_documentable_path(&file.path))
668	            .collect::<Vec<_>>();
669	        if files.is_empty() {
670	            continue;
671	        }
672	        out.push_str(&format!("### Turn {}\n\n", record.turn));
673	        for file in files {
674	            out.push_str(&format!(
675	                "- `{}`: +{}/-{}{}\n",
676	                file.path,
677	                file.adds,
678	                file.dels,
679	                if file.is_binary { " (binary)" } else { "" }
680	            ));
681	            if !file.largest_hunk_excerpt.trim().is_empty() {
682	                out.push_str("  ```diff\n");
683	                out.push_str(&file.largest_hunk_excerpt);
684	                out.push_str("\n  ```\n");
685	            }
686	        }
687	    }
688	    if out.trim().is_empty() {
689	        "No diff samples recorded.".to_string()
690	    } else {
691	        out
692	    }
693	}

695	pub fn tool_stdio_markdown(records: &[TurnRecord]) -> String {
696	    let mut out = String::new();
697	    for record in records {
698	        if record.tool_stdout.is_none() && record.tool_stderr.is_none() {
699	            continue;
700	        }
701	        out.push_str(&format!(
702	            "### Turn {} `{}`\n\n",
703	            record.turn, record.tool_kind
704	        ));
705	        if let Some(stdout) = record.tool_stdout.as_deref()
706	            && !stdout.trim().is_empty()
707	        {
708	            out.push_str("stdout:\n\n```text\n");
709	            out.push_str(stdout.trim());
710	            out.push_str("\n```\n\n");
711	        }
712	        if let Some(stderr) = record.tool_stderr.as_deref()
713	            && !stderr.trim().is_empty()
714	        {
715	            out.push_str("stderr:\n\n```text\n");
716	            out.push_str(stderr.trim());
717	            out.push_str("\n```\n\n");
718	        }
719	    }
720	    if out.trim().is_empty() {
721	        "No bash stdout/stderr captured.".to_string()
722	    } else {
723	        out
724	    }
725	}

741	pub fn append_parent_narrative_update(parent: &PipelineState, child: &PipelineState) -> Result<()> {
742	    for path in [
743	        parent.working_dir.join("docs/RUN-NARRATIVE.md"),
744	        parent.working_dir.join(".deadreckon/docs/RUN-NARRATIVE.md"),
745	    ] {
746	        if !path.exists() {
747	            continue;
748	        }
749	        let mut raw = fs::read_to_string(&path).with_path(&path)?;
750	        if raw.contains(&format!("child run `{}`", child.run_id)) {
751	            continue;
752	        }
753	        raw.push_str("\n\n## Updates since\n\n");
754	        raw.push_str(&format!(
755	            "- Extended by child run `{}` for goal: {}. Child narrative: `library/{}/{}/docs/RUN-NARRATIVE.md`.\n",
756	            child.run_id, child.goal, child.scope, child.run_id
757	        ));
758	        fs::write(&path, raw).with_path(path)?;
759	    }
760	    Ok(())
761	}

763	fn render_narrative(
764	    state: &PipelineState,
765	    fields: &FrontmatterFields,
766	    records: &[TurnRecord],
767	    parent_run_id: Option<&str>,
768	) -> String {
769	    let mut out = frontmatter(state, fields);
770	    if let Some(parent) = parent_run_id {
771	        out.push_str(&format!(
772	            "> **Reading order:** Start with the parent narrative in `library/{}/{}/docs/RUN-NARRATIVE.md`, then read the \"Updates since the parent run\" section below.\n\n",
773	            state.scope, parent
774	        ));
775	    }
776	    out.push_str("## Goal\n\n");
777	    out.push_str(&state.goal);
778	    out.push_str("\n\n## Why now\n\n");
779	    out.push_str("This run was meant to leave a usable project handoff: what changed, which files matter, how the work was checked, and what still needs attention.\n\n");
780	    out.push_str("## High-level approach\n\n");
781	    out.push_str(&high_level_approach(records));
782	    out.push_str("\n\n## What shipped in this run\n\n");
783	    let phases = coalesce_into_phases(records);
784	    if phases.is_empty() {
785	        out.push_str("- No turn activity recorded yet.\n\n");
786	    } else {
787	        for phase in phases {
788	            out.push_str(&format!(
789	                "### Phase {} - {} ({})\n\n",
790	                phase.index,
791	                phase.title,
792	                phase
793	                    .commit_sha
794	                    .as_deref()
795	                    .map(|sha| format!("commit `{sha}`"))
796	                    .unwrap_or_else(|| "commit `-`".to_string())
797	            ));
798	            out.push_str(&phase_paragraph(&phase));
799	            out.push_str("\n\n");
800	            out.push_str("| File | Change | Largest hunk |\n| --- | ---: | --- |\n");
801	            for file in phase_file_changes(&phase) {
802	                out.push_str(&format!(
803	                    "| `{}` | +{} / -{} | {} |\n",
804	                    file.path,
805	                    file.adds,
806	                    file.dels,
807	                    hunk_inline(&file.largest_hunk_excerpt)
808	                ));
809	            }
810	            if phase.files.is_empty() {
811	                out.push_str("| - | +0 / -0 | no file changes recorded |\n");
812	            }
813	            out.push('\n');
814	            for turn in &phase.turns {
815	                out.push_str(&render_turn_section(turn));
816	            }
817	            out.push('\n');
818	        }
819	    }
820	    if let Some(parent) = parent_run_id {
821	        out.push_str("## Updates since the parent run\n\n");
822	        let files = records
823	            .iter()
824	            .flat_map(TurnRecord::file_paths)
825	            .collect::<BTreeSet<_>>();
826	        if files.is_empty() {
827	            out.push_str(&format!(
828	                "- Extends parent `{}`; no changed files recorded yet.\n\n",
829	                short_id(parent)
830	            ));
831	        } else {
832	            for file in files {
833	                out.push_str(&format!(
834	                    "- `{file}` changed after parent `{}`. Trace: [turns](../traces.jsonl).\n",
835	                    short_id(parent)
836	                ));
837	            }
838	            out.push('\n');
839	        }
840	    }
841	    out.push_str("## Open threads\n\n");
842	    let open_threads = open_threads(records);
843	    if open_threads.is_empty() {
844	        out.push_str("- No open threads recorded by deadreckon.\n\n");
845	    } else {
846	        for thread in open_threads {
847	            out.push_str(&format!("- {thread}\n"));
848	        }
849	        out.push('\n');
850	    }
851	    out.push_str("## Cross-references\n\n");
852	    out.push_str(&format!(
853	        "- Traces: `traces.jsonl` ({} turns)\n",
854	        records.len()
855	    ));
856	    out.push_str("- Provenance: `provenance.jsonl`\n");
857	    out.push_str(&format!(
858	        "- Snapshots: `snapshots/turn-0/` through `snapshots/turn-{}`\n",
859	        state.turn
860	    ));
861	    if let Ok(record) = read_codebase_record(&state.working_dir)
862	        && let Some(branch) = record.branch_name.as_deref()
863	    {
864	        out.push_str(&format!(
865	            "- Branch: `{branch}` at `{}`\n",
866	            current_worktree_sha(state).unwrap_or_else(|| "-".to_string())
867	        ));
868	    }
869	    out.push_str("- Acceptance: `proofs/turn-acceptance.json`\n");
870	    out
871	}

873	fn render_turn_section(record: &TurnRecord) -> String {
874	    let mut out = String::new();
875	    let files = record
876	        .files
877	        .iter()
878	        .filter(|file| is_documentable_path(&file.path))
879	        .collect::<Vec<_>>();
880	    out.push_str(&format!(
881	        "\n#### Turn {} - {} ({})\n\n",
882	        record.turn,
883	        record.title,
884	        record
885	            .commit_sha
886	            .as_deref()
887	            .map(|sha| format!("commit `{sha}`"))
888	            .unwrap_or_else(|| "commit `-`".to_string())
889	    ));
890	    out.push_str(&format!(
891	        "- Tool: {} ({})\n",
892	        record.tool_kind,
893	        record
894	            .latency_ms
895	            .map(|ms| format!("{ms}ms"))
896	            .unwrap_or_else(|| "latency not recorded".to_string())
897	    ));
898	    if files.is_empty() && record.files.is_empty() {
899	        out.push_str("- Files: none recorded\n");
900	    } else if files.is_empty() {
901	        out.push_str("- Files: generated/vendor artifacts omitted from the handoff\n");
902	    } else {
903	        out.push_str(&format!(
904	            "- Files: {}\n",
905	            files
906	                .iter()
907	                .map(|file| format!("`{}`", file.path))
908	                .collect::<Vec<_>>()
909	                .join(", ")
910	        ));
911	        for file in files {
912	            out.push_str(&format!(
913	                "  - `{}`: +{} / -{}{}\n",
914	                file.path,
915	                file.adds,
916	                file.dels,
917	                if file.is_binary { " (binary)" } else { "" }
918	            ));
919	            if !file.largest_hunk_excerpt.trim().is_empty() {
920	                out.push_str("    ```diff\n");
921	                for line in file.largest_hunk_excerpt.lines().take(3) {
922	                    out.push_str("    ");
923	                    out.push_str(line);
924	                    out.push('\n');
925	                }
926	                out.push_str("    ```\n");
927	            }
928	        }
929	    }
930	    out.push_str(&format!("- Outcome: {}\n", record.outcome));
931	    out.push_str(&format!(
932	        "- Trace: [turn {}]({})\n",
933	        record.turn, record.trace_link
934	    ));
935	    out.push_str(&format!("- Snapshot: `{}`\n", record.snapshot_link));
936	    out
937	}

982	fn missing_implementation_note_sections(raw: &str) -> Vec<&'static str> {
983	    let lower = raw.to_ascii_lowercase();
984	    IMPLEMENTATION_NOTE_SECTIONS
985	        .iter()
986	        .filter_map(|(id, heading)| {
987	            let has_id =
988	                lower.contains(&format!("id=\"{id}\"")) || lower.contains(&format!("id='{id}'"));
989	            let has_heading = lower.contains(&heading.to_ascii_lowercase());
990	            (!has_id || !has_heading).then_some(*heading)
991	        })
992	        .collect()
993	}

1020	fn is_implementation_notes_file(path: &str) -> bool {
1021	    path.trim_start_matches("./").replace('\\', "/") == IMPLEMENTATION_NOTES_HTML
1022	}

1024	fn implementation_note_markdown_sections(working_dir: &Path) -> BTreeMap<&'static str, String> {
1025	    let path = implementation_notes_path(working_dir);
1026	    let raw = fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap_or_default();
1027	    IMPLEMENTATION_NOTE_SECTIONS
1028	        .iter()
1029	        .map(|(id, heading)| {
1030	            let value = extract_html_section(&raw, id)
1031	                .map(|section| html_fragment_to_markdown(&section))
1032	                .filter(|section| !section.trim().is_empty())
1033	                .unwrap_or_else(|| "None.".to_string());
1034	            (*heading, value)
1035	        })
1036	        .collect()
1037	}
1038	
1039	fn extract_html_section(raw: &str, id: &str) -> Option<String> {
1040	    let lower = raw.to_ascii_lowercase();
1041	    let id_double = format!("id=\"{id}\"");
1042	    let id_single = format!("id='{id}'");
1043	    let id_index = lower.find(&id_double).or_else(|| lower.find(&id_single))?;
1044	    let start_tag = lower[..id_index].rfind("<section")?;
1045	    let content_start = lower[start_tag..].find('>')? + start_tag + 1;
1046	    let content_end = lower[content_start..].find("</section>")? + content_start;
1047	    Some(raw[content_start..content_end].to_string())
1048	}
1049	
1050	fn html_fragment_to_markdown(fragment: &str) -> String {
1051	    let mut prepared = fragment
1052	        .replace("\r\n", "\n")
1053	        .replace("<li>", "\n- ")
1054	        .replace("</li>", "\n")
1055	        .replace("</p>", "\n\n")
1056	        .replace("<br>", "\n")
1057	        .replace("<br/>", "\n")
1058	        .replace("<br />", "\n")
1059	        .replace("</div>", "\n")
1060	        .replace("</section>", "\n");
1061	    prepared = strip_html_tags(&prepared);
1062	    let decoded = decode_html_entities(&prepared);
1063	    let lines = decoded
1064	        .lines()
1065	        .map(str::trim)
1066	        .filter(|line| !line.is_empty())
1067	        .filter(|line| {
1068	            !IMPLEMENTATION_NOTE_SECTIONS
1069	                .iter()
1070	                .any(|(_, heading)| line.eq_ignore_ascii_case(heading))
1071	        })
1072	        .collect::<Vec<_>>();
1073	    if lines.is_empty() {
1074	        "None.".to_string()
1075	    } else {
1076	        lines.join("\n")
1077	    }
1078	}
1079	
1080	fn strip_html_tags(raw: &str) -> String {
1081	    let mut out = String::with_capacity(raw.len());
1082	    let mut in_tag = false;
1083	    for ch in raw.chars() {
1084	        match ch {
1085	            '<' => in_tag = true,
1086	            '>' => in_tag = false,
1087	            _ if !in_tag => out.push(ch),
1088	            _ => {}
1089	        }
1090	    }
1091	    out
1092	}
1093	
1094	fn html_escape(raw: &str) -> String {
1095	    raw.replace('&', "&amp;")
1096	        .replace('<', "&lt;")
1097	        .replace('>', "&gt;")
1098	        .replace('"', "&quot;")
1099	}
1100	
1101	fn decode_html_entities(raw: &str) -> String {
1102	    raw.replace("&lt;", "<")
1103	        .replace("&gt;", ">")
1104	        .replace("&quot;", "\"")
1105	        .replace("&#39;", "'")
1106	        .replace("&amp;", "&")
1107	}

1118	    ));
1119	    out.push_str("This document describes the subsystem changed by this run. For chronology, see [`RUN-NARRATIVE.md`](./RUN-NARRATIVE.md).\n\n");

1121	    out.push_str(&high_level_approach(records));
1122	    out.push_str("\n\n**What's load-bearing:** The changed entrypoints listed below are the files future maintainers should inspect first.\n\n");
1123	    out.push_str("**Where the seams are:** The boundaries are inferred from source paths, manifests, tests, and docs; generated, vendor, cache, and build-output paths are intentionally left out.\n\n");

1145	    }
1146	    out.push_str("## File-system layout (changed/added paths)\n\n```text\n");
1147	    if files.is_empty() {
1148	        out.push_str("(no changed paths recorded)\n");
1149	    } else {
1150	        for file in &files {
1151	            out.push_str(file);

1154	    }
1155	    out.push_str("```\n\n## External interactions\n\n");
1156	    out.push_str("- Provider: ");

1162	    out.push_str("- Decisions: [`RUN-DECISIONS.md`](./RUN-DECISIONS.md)\n");
1163	    out.push_str("\n### Turn citations\n\n");

1168	fn render_decisions(
1169	    state: &PipelineState,
1170	    fields: &FrontmatterFields,
1171	    records: &[TurnRecord],
1172	) -> String {
1173	    let mut out = frontmatter(state, fields);

1177	    ));

1199	    }
1200	    for (idx, record) in decisions.into_iter().enumerate() {
1201	        out.push_str(&format!(

1212	        ));

1214	            "**Trace:** [turn {}](../traces.jsonl)\n",

1216	        ));
1217	        let files = record.file_paths();
1218	        if files.is_empty() {
1219	            out.push_str("**Files affected:** none recorded\n\n");
1220	        } else {
1221	            out.push_str(&format!(
1222	                "**Files affected:** {}\n\n",
1223	                files
1224	                    .iter()
1225	                    .map(|file| format!("`{file}`"))
1226	                    .collect::<Vec<_>>()
1227	                    .join(", ")
1228	            ));
1229	        }
1230	    }
1231	    out.push_str("## Turn citations\n\n");
1232	    out.push_str(&render_turn_citations(records));

1236	fn maybe_write_delta(state: &PipelineState, records: &[TurnRecord]) -> Result<()> {
1237	    let files = all_files(records);
1238	    if should_emit_delta(state, &files)? {
1239	        let mut out = frontmatter(
1240	            state,
1241	            &FrontmatterFields {
1242	                last_updated: Utc::now(),
1243	                doc_writer: "templated only".to_string(),
1244	                parent_run_id: parent_run_id(&state.working_dir),
1245	            },
1246	        );
1247	        out.push_str(&format!(
1248	            "> deadreckon proposes (run {}): update the project AS-BUILT for this change set.\n\n",
1249	            short_id(&state.run_id)
1250	        ));
1251	        out.push_str("### Proposed new section: \"Run-produced changes\"\n\n");
1252	        out.push_str(&format!(
1253	            "> deadreckon proposes (run {}):\n>\n> This run changed: {}.\n",
1254	            short_id(&state.run_id),
1255	            files
1256	                .iter()
1257	                .map(|file| format!("`{file}`"))
1258	                .collect::<Vec<_>>()
1259	                .join(", ")
1260	        ));
1261	        write_file(delta_path(&state.working_dir), out)?;
1262	    } else {
1263	        let path = delta_path(&state.working_dir);
1264	        if path.exists() {
1265	            fs::remove_file(&path).with_path(&path)?;
1266	        }
1267	    }
1268	    Ok(())
1269	}

1271	pub fn should_emit_delta(state: &PipelineState, files: &[String]) -> Result<bool> {
1272	    let Ok(record) = read_codebase_record(&state.working_dir) else {
1273	        return Ok(false);
1274	    };
1275	    if record.mode != CodebaseMode::Worktree {
1276	        return Ok(false);
1277	    }
1278	    if !source_has_as_built(&state.working_dir, files) {
1279	        return Ok(false);
1280	    }
1281	    if files.len() >= 3 {
1282	        return Ok(true);
1283	    }
1284	    for file in files {
1285	        let path = state.working_dir.join(file);
1286	        if let Ok(raw) = fs::read_to_string(path)
1287	            && (raw.contains("pub fn ") || raw.contains("pub struct ") || raw.contains("export "))
1288	        {
1289	            return Ok(true);
1290	        }
1291	    }
1292	    Ok(false)
1293	}
1294	
1295	fn source_has_as_built(working_dir: &Path, files: &[String]) -> bool {
1296	    ["AS-BUILT-ARCHITECTURE.md", "AS-BUILT.md"]
1297	        .iter()
1298	        .any(|name| working_dir.join(name).exists())
1299	        || files.iter().any(|file| {
1300	            let parent = Path::new(file).parent().unwrap_or_else(|| Path::new(""));
1301	            ["AS-BUILT-ARCHITECTURE.md", "AS-BUILT.md"]
1302	                .iter()
1303	                .any(|name| working_dir.join(parent).join(name).exists())
1304	        })
1305	}

1309	    if first.is_empty() {
1310	        "deadreckon run".to_string()
1311	    } else {
1312	        first.to_string()
1313	    }
1314	}

1316	fn commit_or_working_lines(state: &PipelineState) -> Vec<String> {
1317	    let Ok(record) = read_codebase_record(&state.working_dir) else {
1318	        return Vec::new();
1319	    };
1320	    match record.mode {
1321	        CodebaseMode::Worktree => {

1386	fn normalize_file(state: &PipelineState, path: &Path) -> Option<String> {
1387	    let relative = if path.is_absolute() {

1391	    };
1392	    let normalized = relative.to_string_lossy().replace('\\', "/");
1393	    is_documentable_path(&normalized).then_some(normalized)
1394	}

1137	
1138	## 15. Resume Semantics
1139	
1140	`crates/deadreckon/src/main.rs:940-1000` is the `resume_command` handler.
1141	
1142	### 15.1 The Completed guard
1143	
1144	`main.rs:947`:
1145	
1146	```rust
1147	if state.status == RunStatus::Completed {
1148	    println!("run {} is already completed", state.run_id);
1149	    return Ok(());
1150	}
1151	```
1152	
1153	Completed runs cannot be resumed. They can be re-promoted (idempotent) but not re-entered into the loop. The only forward path for a completed run today is to start a new run.
1154	
1155	### 15.2 The replay process
1156	
1157	For non-Completed runs (`Failed`, `Killed`, `Paused`):
1158	
1159	1. Acquire the task lock.
1160	2. Clear `failure_reason`, `pause_reason`, `killed_at`.
1161	3. Set `status = Planned`.
1162	4. Optionally extend `max_wall_seconds` from the resume flag.
1163	5. Set `child_pids = vec![cli_pid]`.
1164	6. `save_state()`.
1165	7. Call `run_turn_loop` with `RunLoopConfig.from_turn = <CLI flag>`.
1166	8. The loop calls `load_or_reconstruct_history(state, from_turn)` in `crates/deadreckon-runtime/src/turn_loop.rs`, which loads `history.json` if present, else reconstructs from `traces.jsonl`. With `from_turn = N`, history is truncated to N entries and `state.turn = N`.
1167	
1168	History reconstruction tolerates a `traces.jsonl` that ends mid-tool-call by ignoring incomplete entries — the next turn re-runs that turn.
1169	
1170	See `/Users/gdc/deadreckon/docs/RESUME-SEMANTICS.md` for the contract.
1171	
1172	---
1173	
1174	## 16. Cross-Tool Import
1175	
1176	`deadreckon import <source>` reads from external coding-agent histories and synthesizes a completed deadreckon run from one concrete imported session, or from an explicit `--all` root import. It is read-only with respect to provider-owned transcript roots and writes only deadreckon run-state files.

```text
1249	## 18. TUI (`attach`)
1250	
1251	`crates/deadreckon/src/main.rs:874-1289` houses `attach_command` plus the rendering helpers.
1252	
1253	### 18.1 Behavior
1254	
1255	- On a TTY: `attach_tui()` enables raw mode, alternate screen, and renders a `ratatui` UI.
1256	- Off-TTY: prints a plain-text summary + locations.
1257	
1258	`attach` dispatches by id kind: a run id opens the run TUI documented below, a chain id opens the chain attach view (`Chains`, §28), and a plan id opens the plan attach TUI (`Plans`, §30.3 / §32.3). All three TUIs draw from the same palette (`ui::TUI_PALETTE`, §26.7) and the same key conventions (`q`/`Esc`/`Ctrl-D` detach; `d` toggles docs view in the run TUI; `Enter` drills into a child run from plan attach).
1259	
1260	`attach <id> --view narrative` adds a calmer operator projection for runs, plans, and plan child refs. The default remains `activity`, so raw tool/provider lines still open first unless the user requests the narrative view. In narrative mode, `n` toggles back to raw activity, `v` cycles `architecture -> agents -> files -> evidence -> none`, and `r` requests a provider-backed refresh when a configured route is available. While the TTY narrative view is open, meaningful run and plan events also request a provider refresh: errors, completions, tool milestones, docs checkpoints, acceptance running/pass/fail transitions, child-run discovery, task terminal states, and merge-repair milestones. Long-running quiet periods request a refresh after the narrative quiet window when the run or plan is still running. Provider refreshes are bounded: the prompt is built from redacted evidence windows, the provider must return strict cited JSON, graph labels may only target deterministic graph ids, and failures persist a stale deterministic projection instead of breaking attach.
1261	
1262	### 18.2 Layout
1263	
1264	`attach_panel_layout` (`main.rs:~10225`):
1265	
1266	```rust
1267	let vertical = Layout::default()
1268	    .direction(Direction::Vertical)
1269	    .constraints([
1270	        Constraint::Length(5),    // top band: header + spend (if metered) + context + acceptance
1271	        Constraint::Min(10),      // tool calls + provider activity + live files
1272	        Constraint::Length(4),    // processes/status
1273	        Constraint::Length(2),    // keybindings footer (multi-line during long ops)
1274	    ])
1275	    .split(area);
1276	```
1277	
1278	The top band is split horizontally into three panels for subscription providers (header 66 / context 17 / acceptance 17) and four for metered API providers (header 55 / spend 15 / context 15 / acceptance 15):
1279	
1280	- **Header** (short run id, status, phase, provider, sandbox, turn timer, truncated goal, working/artifact path; degrades to an identity strip when live status is unavailable).
1281	- **Spend meter** only for metered API providers; CLI subscription providers omit cost and emphasize context/wall time.
1282	- **Context meter**: compact token/window summary with green/yellow/red thresholds.
1283	- **Acceptance meter**: derived from `AcceptanceLive` (`collect_acceptance_live` in `main.rs:~10172`). When `proofs/acceptance-progress.jsonl` exists, the panel tails it and surfaces `running 2/5`, `passed`, or `failed` with the offending check; once `turn-acceptance.json` is signed, it pivots to a marker view (`acceptance_live_from_marker`). Color thresholds are owned by `acceptance_color`.
1284	- **Center, left**: wide streaming list of tool calls + provider activity + recent events. Acceptance lines from `acceptance_activity_lines` are interleaved so the operator sees the same progress in the activity stream and the meter.
1285	- **Narrative view**: `--view narrative` or `n` swaps the center-left activity pane for prose sections under the `Narrated` operator heading: freshness/coverage, headline, current work, architecture notes, risks, next likely action, and citations. Wide terminals split that pane with a right-side visual map; narrow terminals collapse to prose first. Run narratives cite `proofs/acceptance-progress.jsonl` or `proofs/turn-acceptance.json` when acceptance evidence exists, so failed done criteria point at the durable proof artifact. Plain/off-TTY narrative attach prints the same projection with citations and ASCII map lines when `--visual` is not `none`; `--json --view narrative` emits the structured state, snapshot, and graph objects. Non-TTY narrative attach stays deterministic and does not call a provider unless a future explicit refresh surface opts in. Chain narrative attach currently returns an unsupported response with `try:` lines for run and plan narrative attach.
1286	- **Completed docs view**: pressing `d` toggles the center-left panel from provider activity or narrative view to `RUN-NARRATIVE.md` rendered through `pulldown-cmark` into ratatui `Line`/`Span`s. Headings, bullets, inline code, fenced code blocks, links, task markers, math, and horizontal rules receive terminal styles and remain scrollable. The docs view remains a separate completed-run artifact rather than being merged into the live narrative projection.
1287	- **Center, right**: narrower live files list with count/bytes in the panel title.
1288	- **Bottom**: supervised PIDs + their `ps` lines (alive/dead annotation).
1289	- **Footer**: action-first completed footer (`[d] Docs` / `[d] Activity`, `[a] Apply`, `[b] Abandon`, `[s] Show`) or scroll/detach help while running. The footer's second line carries `deadreckoning_status_line` while long operations are in flight.
1290	
1291	### 18.3 Data source
1292	
1293	The run TUI still polls run files on disk every 500 ms: `spend.jsonl`, `traces.jsonl`, `events.jsonl`, `proofs/acceptance-progress.jsonl`, `proofs/turn-acceptance.json`, plus provider-native logs when the active provider writes them. `collect_provider_activity` now resolves provider ingest through descriptor `[ingest]` metadata: candidate roots, env overrides, cwd matching, storage kind, file glob, freshness window, and schema key. `deadreckon import` reuses the same descriptor metadata for provider transcript discovery and adds import-only session selection, manifest writing, and normalized trace/provenance event creation. `cli:codex` reads `~/.codex/sessions/**.jsonl` and matches `session_meta.payload.cwd`; `cli:claude-code` reads `~/.claude/projects/<cwd-slug>/*.jsonl` using Claude Code's path-to-project mapping and matches top-level `cwd`; `cli:gemini` reads Gemini JSON/JSONL file logs; `cli:opencode` reads OpenCode file-mode `storage/session`, `storage/message`, and `storage/part` JSON; `cli:copilot` reads `~/.copilot/session-state/*.jsonl` plus nested `events.jsonl` and matches `data.context.cwd`; `cli:pi` reads `~/.pi/agent/sessions/<encoded-cwd>/*.jsonl`, validates the first nonblank row is a Pi `session`, and matches the header `cwd`. The shared collector handles candidate discovery, recency filtering, run matching, stream capping, and context telemetry. Schema-specific adapters only decode rows into common activity lines (`agent`, `thinking`, `tool`, `result`, `todo`, `tokens`) and normalize tool labels through `deadreckon_providers::taxonomy`.
1294	
1295	Same-process run attaches can use the `RunEventBus` broadcast channel directly; cross-process run attaches still poll. Plan attach is different after the live-UX slice: it consumes `PlanEventBus` / `PlanEventFeed`, which owns `plan-events.jsonl` replay/tailing, emits plan snapshots, tolerates malformed or partial plan-event rows, and multiplexes discovered child and repair run `events.jsonl` streams into the plan activity pane. The production feed remains durable-file backed for cross-process attach, with a broadcast-capable API available for same-process plan streams.
1296	
1297	### 18.4 Narrative projection files
1298	
1299	Narrative attach writes projection files, not source-of-truth state. Run projections live under `<run-root>/narrative/`; plan projections live under `<plan-dir>/narrative/`.
1300	
1301	- `state.json` records the latest snapshot id/status, coverage, cadence, provider source, provider call count, cost/wall-clock accounting, and last refresh error.
1302	- `snapshots.jsonl` is append-only. Each row contains cited `current_work`, `architecture_notes`, `risks`, `next_likely`, citations, and plan-only agent/coordination sections. Malformed rows are skipped when reading the latest snapshot.
1303	- `architecture-graph.json` is a deterministic graph over run files, provider ids, checkpoints, plan tasks, dependencies, child runs, and citation ids. The TUI renders architecture, agent, file, and evidence views from this graph using ASCII-compatible labels and color-independent badges.
1304	
1305	Plan projections prefer each child run's latest narrative snapshot when one exists. The plan agent table cites that child snapshot and uses its headline as the child summary, then falls back to child run state when no child narrative exists. Plan graphs also roll up file nodes from child narrative graphs so the plan-level files visual can show cross-agent touched file evidence without copying child logs into `plan-events.jsonl`.
1306	
1307	Provider-backed narration is an overlay on these projections. Manual `r` refresh, TTY narrative-view event refreshes, and TTY narrative-view quiet-threshold refreshes build a redacted prompt from the deterministic projection, send only bounded evidence summaries to the selected provider route, validate all returned claims against known evidence ids, reject invented graph ids, and persist a new fresh snapshot only after validation. The default narrator route is `cli:claude-code` with model override `sonnet`, which the Claude Code adapter launches as `claude --model sonnet --dangerously-skip-permissions -p <prompt>`; `--narrative-provider` overrides the route and leaves model selection to that provider/config entry, while `--no-narrative-provider` keeps attach deterministic-only. Event refreshes can bypass the ordinary freshness interval for meaningful deltas, while quiet-threshold refreshes still obey the freshness interval; budget, provider availability, JSON validation, citation validation, graph validation, and redaction guards always apply. If the provider is missing, over budget, behind cadence, returns malformed JSON, cites unknown evidence, emits secret-like text, or fails, attach keeps running and persists a stale deterministic snapshot with the error in `state.json`.
1308

1707	## 26. Coherence Pass (alpha)
1708	
1709	> **Status (2026-05-24):** The May 2026 coherence pass and closure pass are alpha-complete. Glossary labels, style helpers, `print_kv_block`, flag-truth, prompt builder, attach/kill parity, shared TUI palette, provider-route wording, provider/done-criteria setup, JSON parity, orchestration commands, plan attach, and polymorphic lifecycle ids now share the same user-facing model. The closure briefs are at `docs/goals/2026-05-13-1900-deadreckon-coherence-goal.md`, `docs/goals/2026-05-17-1403-deadreckon-coherence-closure-goal.md`, and `docs/goals/2026-05-24-1426-deadreckon-provider-done-setup-goal.md`; the closure matrix is `docs/design/USER-FACING-MATRIX.md`, with larger follow-ups explicitly deferred to `docs/V1-CANDIDATES.md`. The pass is intentionally schema-preserving: no `RunStatus`/`ChainStatus`/`PlanTaskStatus` variant names changed, only display strings changed via `glossary.rs` and runtime setup helpers.
1710	
1711	### 26.1 Glossary
1712	
1713	`crates/deadreckon-core/src/glossary.rs` is the display vocabulary source for statuses and primary nouns. Stored enum variants keep their alpha schema names, including `RunStatus::Executing`, but user-facing run and phase text now renders `running`. Chains, chain steps, plan status, and plan-child status use the same helper family, so `attach <plan-id> --plain`, `merge <plan-id>`, and `status <run-id>` agree on `running`.
1714	
1715	### 26.2 Style Helpers
1716	
1717	`crates/deadreckon/src/ui.rs` owns ANSI rendering through `Tone`, `Stream`, `write`, `writeln`, `hint`, and `kv_block`. The small CLI facade (`ui_heading`, `ui_muted`, `ui_id`, `ui_command`, `ui_ok`, `ui_warn`, `ui_note`, `ui_status`, and `ui_error`) also lives there, so `main.rs` imports style intent instead of defining its own wrappers. Raw ANSI escapes are confined to `ui.rs`, and status labels route through `ui::status_tone` before choosing a tone. `failed`/`killed`, `paused`, `warning`, and `note` are separate style intents even when two intents currently share the same terminal color. 1721	### 26.3 Key/Value Layout
1722	
1723	`print_kv_block` wraps `ui::kv_block` for CLI cards. Run start banners, run summaries, run locations, status cards, plan creation, and plan summaries now use lowercase keys, padded colons, and six-decimal spend where applicable.
1724	
1725	### 26.4 Flag Truth
1726	
1727	The alpha CLI names intent before force. Kill paths use `--escalate`; destination overwrites use `--overwrite`; override paths use `--anyway`; chain and cleanup cross-scope commands use `--all-scopes`; status uses `--global`; run branch naming uses `--branch-name`; apply/finish target branches use `--into`, and apply output says work landed `into` the target branch; doc polish uses `--max-spend`; apply and finish git behavior use `--git-strategy`. Strategy words are scoped: `merge --strategy` is plan composition, `apply`/`finish --git-strategy` is git apply behavior, chain `--apply-mode` controls chain policy, and chain `--apply-strategy` controls the per-step git operation. The old spellings stay as hidden aliases for one alpha. Chain branch policy displays `linear-merge` while accepting the old `merge` value. Cross-project help says "all project scopes" on run, chain, history, cleanup, and library surfaces; provider `--all` remains provider inventory rather than project scope.

1729	Every visible `--plain` flag uses the same help definition: "Plain output without TUI, spinner, or ANSI affordances." Individual commands still implement their own plain-mode effect, such as `attach --plain` choosing the text summary instead of ratatui.
1730	
1731	Output and scripting flags have a visible policy in `deadreckon help-all`. `--yes` confirms preflight previews for start/update-style commands. `--no-confirm` skips destructive or follow-up confirmations after the target is known. `--quiet` suppresses success chatter and post-action hints, never requested data or errors. `--plain` disables TUI, spinner, and ANSI affordances without implying quiet. `--json` is reserved for inspection/list surfaces and wins over styling and hints. `--no-hints` suppresses optional next-step hints; `DEADRECKON_HINTS=0|false|off|no` disables them globally for the process.
1732	
1733	`deadreckon help-all` also carries the spend-cap glossary. A run cap is `run --max-spend` for one run, a per-child cap is `orchestrate`/`fork --max-spend` for each child run, an aggregate chain cap is `chain --max-spend`, and a doc polish cap is `doc --max-spend`.

1736

1739	The user-facing skip model is split by timing. `--yes` belongs to preflight preview acceptance on commands such as `run`, `orchestrate`, `chain`, and shell-channel `update`; `--no-confirm` belongs to direct destructive or follow-up actions such as `finish`, `apply`, `cleanup`, chain recovery commands, and doc polish.

1742

1747	`ui::TUI_PALETTE` names the shared TUI color slots for focused borders, acceptance states, run states, and spend thresholds. The chain attach poll cadence matches the run TUI at 200 ms. Applied chain steps render `◉`, so applied and running no longer share `●`. The spend gauge keeps the green, yellow, red, and cap-paused magenta thresholds; above 60 percent, the title exposes the budget percentage so the label remains readable at narrow widths.

1750	
1751	Provider displays use the provider/route/model/kind vocabulary consistently. Human provider lists and detection rows use the same `kind=cli|http|local-http|scripted` tokens, and the configured route is marked with `*` in the selection and registry views. `setup.rs` owns runtime provider setup rows for config/default-provider, primary run, doc polish, planner, child, coder, reviewer, and repair roles; it validates unknown routes before writes, reports source/credential/install state, and leaves built-in fallback routing unforced for normal run defaults. `show --why-failed` and `chain show --why-failed` now route through one failure-summary renderer with shared `status:`, `reason:`, `evidence:`, and `try:` sections.

Normal user surfaces say provider route/model/kind; descriptor remains registry documentation vocabulary.

User-facing previews and orchestration preflights say `done criteria`; technical files, gate proofs, and hidden compatibility commands may still say `acceptance.yaml` or `gate`.

JSON mode disables ANSI and optional hints. State-changing start/merge/fork/update actions remain text-first in alpha.

1774	
1775	### 27.2 Sleep Prevention
1776	
1777	`deadreckon run --prevent-sleep <auto|on|off>` defaults through `[defaults].prevent_sleep`. `auto` arms only for interactive runs; `on` forces a platform attempt; `off` skips. macOS launches `caffeinate -di` for the run-loop lifetime. Linux re-execs under `systemd-inhibit` with a trusted tmpdir ready-file handshake before run state is created, then writes run-local metadata from the inhibited child. Windows reports unsupported and remains a V1 candidate.
1778	
1779	Sleep state is file-based, not a `PipelineState` field: `working/.deadreckon/sleep-prevention.json` records mode, pid, binary, arm time, reason, and skip reason. The RAII handle removes the file and reaps the inhibitor on drop.
1780	
1781	### 27.3 Unattended-Git Hardening
1782	
1783	`crates/deadreckon-core/src/git.rs` is the production git boundary. It exports `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` for every git child and inserts `-c commit.gpgsign=false -c tag.gpgsign=false -c gpg.format=` for commit-family verbs (`commit`, `merge`, `cherry-pick`, `rebase`, `tag`, `am`, `revert`). A grep-style depth test rejects raw production `Command::new("git")` outside that helper.
1784	
1785	### 27.4 Honest Spend Display
1786	
1787	`deadreckon_core::spend_summary` replays `spend.jsonl` and reports total USD, token totals, wall seconds, and sticky `any_subscription_turn` / `any_estimated_turn` flags. Exit cards render `~$N.NNNNNN` when either flag is true so subscription and estimated dollar displays do not imply more precision than the data has.

1790	
1791	## 28. Chains & Autonomous Goal Chaining
1792	
1793	### 28.1 Mental Model
1794	
1795	A chain is an ordered list of step goals plus branch, apply, budget, and stop policy. The conductor is a CLI process entered by `deadreckon chain ...` or `deadreckon chain run <id>`. It acquires a chain lock, spawns each step as a normal `deadreckon run --worktree`, waits for that run to complete and pass acceptance, applies it to the source branch when policy allows, then bases the next step on the updated head.
1796	
1797	Chain state is separate from `PipelineState`: no run schema fields were added. Files live under `~/.deadreckon/chains/<chain-id>/`.
1798	
1799	### 28.2 `chain.json`
1800	
1801	`crates/deadreckon-core/src/chain.rs` defines `Chain`, `ChainStep`, and `ConductorState`. The top-level chain records `chain_id`, `root_goal`, ordered `steps`, `branch_policy`, `apply_mode`, `apply_strategy`, `apply_allowlist`, `on_fail`, circuit-breaker counters, aggregate spend/wall caps, scope, base branch/SHA, cwd, provider/model/sandbox, status, pause/failure reason, conductor pid, timestamps, and deadreckon version.
1802	
1803	Each `ChainStep` records index, goal, status, run id, applied timestamp/SHA, failure reason, step cap, and actual spend. `ConductorState` is the live-process pointer in `conductor.json`: conductor pid, live step, live run id, and live child pid.

1	<p align="center">
2	  <img src="docs/assets/deadreckon-wordmark.png" alt="deadreckon logo" width="640">

4	
5	# deadreckon
6	
7	**A harness around the agent CLI you already use, so you can actually walk away.**
8	
9	Claude Code, Codex, Cursor CLI, and the rest are good at writing code. They are not built to run unattended for hours and tell you, honestly, whether the work got done. deadreckon is.
10	
11	You bring the agent CLI you already trust. You tell deadreckon what "done" looks like in plain English. It runs the work in an isolated sandbox, saves every turn, and uses a separate watchdog process to decide when the run is actually finished: a watchdog the agent cannot fool.
12	
13	```bash
14	deadreckon def-done "users can sign up, log in, and save a drawing"
15	deadreckon run "build the app"
16	# walk away, attach later from any terminal
17	deadreckon attach latest
18	```
19	
20	> [!TIP]
21	> deadreckon is alpha software. The core lifecycle (isolated runs, signed gates, durable state, undo, docs, and apply) is implemented and tested, but expect rough edges and breaking changes.
22	
23	## How it works
24	
25	1. **You write "done" in plain English.** deadreckon compiles it into executable checks: tests that must pass, files that must exist, scripts that must succeed.
26	2. **The agent runs in an isolated worktree**, inside a sandbox. Your real checkout is never touched.
27	3. **Every turn is saved** (state, spend, traces, file provenance, snapshots) so you can attach, kill, resume, undo, or audit any moment.
28	4. **A separate watchdog process (`dr-gate`) decides when the work is done.** It holds a secret the agent process cannot read, and signs the result with that secret. The agent cannot forge the signature, so it cannot mark its own work as accepted.
29	5. **If the checks fail, the loop keeps going.** The agent gets another turn. When the watchdog finally signs off for real, the run is atomically promoted to a reviewable artifact: narrative, decisions, file provenance, full audit trail.
30	
31	The loop is the product. The agent CLI does the coding. deadreckon decides when "done" actually means done.
32	
33	## Why this matters
34	
35	- **You can leave a long run going and trust the result.** The agent can't lie its way out of the gate.
36	- **Use whichever agent CLI you prefer.** Claude Code, Codex, Cursor CLI, or direct Anthropic / OpenAI API: deadreckon supervises any of them.
37	- **You get an auditable artifact, not a chat transcript.** Narrative, decisions, file lineage, spend, traces, all on disk.
38	- **If anything dies (terminal, network, the model) the run survives.** Attach from a new terminal, resume from any turn, undo a bad step.
39	
40	## Why "deadreckon"?
41	
42	Dead reckoning is navigation without perfect visibility: track every move so you know where you are now. Unattended agents are the same problem: long task, partial context, the terminal may be gone when you look back. The name is the contract: don't trust the final answer, navigate by evidence.
43	
44	The questions deadreckon is built to answer:
45	
46	- Where did the agent run, and what did it spend?
47	- Can I attach after closing my laptop?
48	- Can I undo turn 7 without rolling back the whole project?
49	- Can I prove the agent did not mark its own work as accepted?
50	
51	## Features
52	
53	### Your Checkout Is Never Touched (Isolated Worktrees By Default)
54	
55	In a git repo, `deadreckon run` creates a separate `git worktree` on a `dr/...` branch under `~/.deadreckon/worktrees/`. Your checkout is left untouched until you explicitly run:
56	
57	```bash
58	deadreckon apply <run-id>
59	```
60	
61	Run ids accept unique prefixes, and most commands also accept `latest` for the
62	newest run in the current project.
63	
64	You can also run in copy mode, fresh mode, or explicit in-place mode:
65	
66	```bash
67	deadreckon run "goal" --from .
68	deadreckon run "goal" --fresh
69	deadreckon run "goal" --in-place --i-know-its-a-lot
70	```
71	
72	### Use The Agent CLI You Already Trust
73	
74	Route turns through whichever provider you prefer:
75	
76	- **Local CLIs** (subscription): `cli:claude-code`, `cli:codex`
77	- **Direct APIs** (BYOK): `anthropic`, `openai`, OpenAI-compatible endpoints
78	- **Smoke** (keyless): `--smoke` for local verification
79	
80	The CLI does the coding; deadreckon owns the run boundary around it.
81	
82	### Crash-Proof: Every Turn Is Saved To Disk
83	
84	Every turn writes state, traces, spend, file provenance, and a working-directory snapshot under `~/.deadreckon/runstate/`. If the terminal dies, attach from another. If the run itself crashes, resume from the last completed turn.
85	
86	### Walk Away, Attach From Any Terminal
87	
88	```bash
89	deadreckon attach latest
90	```
91	
92	The TUI shows live status, current step, spend, recent file edits, and provider activity. Completed runs render `RUN-NARRATIVE.md` inline. Press `Ctrl-D` to detach without killing the run.
93	
94	For longer or multi-agent work, use `deadreckon attach latest --view narrative` for a cited operator overview with an evidence-backed visual map. Raw activity stays one key away with `n`; `v` cycles architecture, agent, file, and evidence views.
95	
96	Provider-backed narrative refresh defaults to local Claude Code on Sonnet when available; use `--narrative-provider <route>` to override the narrator, or `--no-narrative-provider` for deterministic-only attach.
97	
98	### Set A Budget And A Time Limit, Then Walk Away
99	
100	Every provider response appends a spend record and updates totals. API routes track token cost. Subscription CLI routes can be capped by wall-clock time.
101	
102	```bash
103	deadreckon run "large refactor" --max-spend 15
104	deadreckon run "large refactor" --max-wall-seconds 1800
105	```
106	
107	High spend requires explicit confirmation, so scripts do not accidentally launch expensive runs.
108	
109	### Undo A Single Bad Turn Without Losing The Rest
110	
111	deadreckon snapshots the working directory at turn boundaries:
112	
113	```bash
114	deadreckon undo --run <run-id>
115	deadreckon undo --run <run-id> --turn 3
116	```
117	
118	This is not just `git reset`. It works against the run's own snapshot trail and records the undo in the run trace.
119	
120	### Write "Done" In English, Verified By A Watchdog
121	
122	Tell deadreckon what success looks like in plain language. It compiles your sentence into executable checks that an independent watchdog runs:
123	
124	```bash
125	deadreckon def-done "build, load in a browser, and show no console errors"
126	deadreckon def-done add "users can save drawings"
127	deadreckon def-done check
128	deadreckon run "finish the app"
129	```
130	
131	`deadreckon run` and `deadreckon chain run` prompt interactively when a project has no acceptance file yet. Generated files live under `.deadreckon/`.
132	
133	**Why the watchdog matters.** The watchdog holds a secret the agent process cannot read. It stamps the result with that secret. Without a valid stamp, the run can't terminate, and the agent can't produce the stamp itself.
134	
135	If no acceptance file is configured, the default is "the working directory exists and `cargo test` passes" (when `Cargo.toml` is present).
136	
137	You can still edit the compiled YAML directly:
138	
139	```yaml
140	name: notes check
141	checks:
142	  - kind: file_exists
143	    path: "{working_dir}/notes.md"
144	  - kind: content_match
145	    path: "{working_dir}/notes.md"
146	    pattern: "dead reckoning"
147	  - kind: build_success
148	    cwd: "{working_dir}"
149	```
150	
151	Supported executable check kinds are `cargo_test`, `file_exists`, `content_match`, `build_success`, and `shell`. `content_match` treats `pattern` as a regex when valid, with substring fallback for simple text.
152	
153	### Get An Auditable Artifact, Not A Transcript
154	
155	deadreckon records which model/tool call touched which files, then writes self-documenting artifacts for the completed run:
156	
157	```bash
158	deadreckon doc <run-id>
159	deadreckon doc <run-id> --kind as-built
160	deadreckon doc <run-id> --kind decisions
161	deadreckon doc <run-id> --kind delta
162	```
163	
164	Each accepted run produces a review packet:
165	
166	- `RUN-NARRATIVE.md` explains what happened.
167	- `RUN-AS-BUILT.md` captures the subsystem shape after the run.
168	- `RUN-DECISIONS.md` records the implementation decision ledger: design decisions, deviations, tradeoffs, open questions, and multi-alternative decision details.
169	- `implementation-notes.html` is the live working copy the agent maintains while changing files.
170	- `AS-BUILT-DELTA.md` proposes architecture-doc updates when the run is broad enough.
171	- `manifest.json` records what was built and from what.
172	
173	Agentic CLIs usually leave you with a patch and a transcript. deadreckon turns
174	the session into a local published artifact you can inspect, export, extend, or
175	apply.
176	
177	### Resume, Kill, Extend, Or Export Any Run
178	
179	Runs are lifecycle objects, not one terminal session:
180	
181	```bash
182	deadreckon list
183	deadreckon status
184	deadreckon show latest
185	deadreckon kill latest
186	deadreckon resume latest
187	deadreckon resume latest --from-turn 2
188	deadreckon extend latest "add tests and polish the UI"
189	deadreckon finish latest
190	deadreckon export latest --dest ./finished-project
191	deadreckon cleanup --completed
192	```
193	
194	Resume reconstructs history from durable traces and ignores incomplete trailing trace entries.
195	
196	### Autonomous Chains For Multi-Step Work
197	
198	Some tasks are too big for one goal. Chains let you break work into ordered steps that run end-to-end, with the same gate enforcement and the same lifecycle commands per step:
199

2011	## 32. Plan Observability
2012	
2013	### 32.1 Event Stream
2014	
2015	Plans now have their own append-only timeline at `~/.deadreckon/plans/<plan-id>/plan-events.jsonl`. Each row is a `PlanEvent` with UTC timestamp, `plan_id`, and a snake-case tagged `PlanEventKind`. The core helper pair is `append_plan_event` / `read_plan_events`, exported from `deadreckon-core`; the path helper is `DeadreckonPaths::plan_events`.
2016	
2017	The stream is orchestration-level only. It records plan and task lifecycle edges, child run discovery, merge edges, semantic repair planning/execution edges, kill edges, and final failure/completion. It does not copy child turn/tool traces. A selected child remains a normal run with its own `events.jsonl`, `traces.jsonl`, provider logs, acceptance proofs, spend records, and attach renderer.
2018	
2019	### 32.2 Emission Points
2020	
2021	`plan` appends `plan_created` after `plan.json` is saved. `fork` appends `plan_started` exactly once per invocation, then `task_ready` for each task in the ready batch, `task_started` before each child spawn, `task_run_discovered` when a PID or run id becomes known, and one of `task_completed` / `task_failed` / `task_blocked` / `task_killed` on each terminal transition (including dependency-blocker events). `merge` appends `merge_started`, optional `merge_conflict`, then the optional repair sequence (`merge_repair_planned` / `merge_repair_started` / `merge_repair_run_discovered` / `merge_repaired` or `merge_repair_failed`), then `merge_completed` and `plan_completed`. Idempotency and ordering are covered by depth tests added in commit `4fcb7f9`. `kill <plan-id>` appends `task_killed` per child, then `plan_killed` and `plan_failed`, preserving discovered run ids and PIDs even if a child already reached a terminal state before the kill sweep loaded it so recovery commands can still map live processes back to durable state.
2022	
2023	### 32.3 User Surfaces
2024	
2025	`attach <plan-id>` now renders `PlanEventBus` feed activity in the plan activity pane, falling back to coordinator messages only before the event file exists. The feed replays durable plan events, emits snapshots when plan status or child run ids change, and multiplexes discovered child and repair run events without copying child traces into `plan-events.jsonl`. `Enter` on a child with a run id suspends the plan TUI and opens the existing run attach view with a breadcrumb like `plan <prefix> / task-1`; `q`, `Esc`, or `Ctrl-D` returns to the same plan attach context.
2026	
2027	Plain/off-TTY `attach <plan-id>` prints the latest plan event, merge repair status when sidecars exist, and an explicit `deadreckon attach <plan-id>` hint. `history grep <pattern> --plan <plan-id>` searches `plan-events.jsonl` before child run trace/provenance files, so repair events are grep-visible. `show <plan-id> --why-failed` includes the latest plan event and merge repair sidecar paths alongside failed child rows and blocker messages.
2028	
2029	`attach <plan-id> --view narrative` uses the same plan feed plus current `Plan` state to render a plan-level operator story. The narrative pane lists plan status, task/role/provider rows, dependency and coordination notes, risks, next likely orchestration moves, and an agent or architecture visual. The narrative footer keeps `n`/`v`/`r` controls visible even before the selected task has a child run, then appends the `Enter waits`/`try: deadreckon fork` hint so raw activity remains one key away. It does not copy child traces into `plan-events.jsonl`; child runs remain normal runs with their own narrative projections and flight files.
2030	
2031	### 32.4 Current Limits
2032	
2033	The plan event stream is durable and replayable, and plan attach now subscribes to a single `PlanEventBus` feed abstraction. The feed is broadcast-capable in-process, but production plan writers still primarily communicate through append-only JSONL so cross-process attach remains reliable. A future embedded attach mode could pass a long-lived broadcaster through every plan writer for lower-latency same-process delivery.
2034	
2035	---
2036	
2037	## 33. Provider Flight Recorder & Rewind
2038	
2039	### 33.1 Durable Flight Files
2040	
2041	CLI-backed providers (`cli:*` and `cli-*`) are no longer represented only as one opaque `tool.cli_subagent` turn. `deadreckon-core/src/flight.rs` defines the durable flight layer:
2042	
2043	- `flight-manifest.json` records one `FlightSession` per provider invocation with provider id, schema, DeadReckon turn, attempt number, status, source paths, and checkpoint policy.
2044	- `flight-events.jsonl` records normalized provider-native rows with ordered `seq`, source path/line/hash, kind (`agent`, `thinking`, `tool`, `result`, `todo`, `tokens`, `session`, `checkpoint`, `warning`, `error`), file references, token usage, and optional checkpoint id.
2045	- `checkpoints/<id>/manifest.json` records delta checkpoints with created/modified/deleted files, base turn snapshot, trigger (`provider_tool`, `file_quiet`, `provider_exit`, or `manual`), and optional full anchors.
2046	- `rewind-events.jsonl` records preview/apply/refusal attempts for audit.
2047	
2048	Checkpoints copy full after-bytes for created/modified files into `checkpoints/<id>/files/...` and record deleted files in the manifest. Materialization starts from the base turn snapshot or nearest anchor and replays deltas through the target checkpoint.
2049

```text
200	```bash
201	deadreckon chain plan "ship a working SaaS billing flow" --n 4
202	deadreckon chain run latest
203	deadreckon chain attach latest
204	deadreckon chain kill latest
205	```
206	
207	Each chain step is a real run with its own signed acceptance gate. If a step fails its gate, the chain stops there; later steps don't start. Killing a chain cascades to whatever step is live. The attach TUI shows the whole chain timeline, not just the current turn, so you can see where you are in the plan without leaving the dashboard.
208	
209	You can also extend a finished run into a follow-up step instead of planning the whole chain up front:
210	
211	```bash
212	deadreckon chain extend latest "add billing webhooks and retry logic"
213	```
214	
215	## The Mental Model
216	
217	```text
218	your repo
219	  |
220	  | deadreckon def-done "what 'finished' looks like, in English"
221	  | deadreckon run  "what to build"
222	  v
223	isolated worktree or copy   ◄── your real checkout untouched
224	  |
225	  | provider route: cli:codex, cli:claude-code, anthropic, openai, ...
226	  v
227	sandboxed turn loop         ◄── agent works here
228	  |
229	  | every turn: trace, spend, provenance, snapshot, docs
230	  | check fails? agent gets another turn
231	  v
232	dr-gate watchdog            ◄── separate process, holds hidden nonce
233	  |                              agent CANNOT produce a valid marker
234	  | checks pass + signature valid?
235	  v
236	promoted artifact           ◄── narrative, decisions, file lineage
237	  |
238	  | inspect, doc, apply, discard, extend, export, cleanup
239	  v
240	your branch or library
241	```
242	
243	For multi-step work, `deadreckon chain` wraps this whole loop and runs N of them in order, stopping on the first gate failure.
244	
245	The agent owns the coding. deadreckon owns the boundary.
246	
247	## Quickstart
248	
249	Build once:
250	
251	```bash
252	cargo build --release
253	```
254	
255	The binary is `./target/release/deadreckon`. Add it to your `PATH` or alias it; the rest of this README just says `deadreckon`.
256	
257	Install shell tab completion. `deadreckon init` does this automatically when it
258	can detect your shell; this command repairs or installs it later:
259	
260	```bash
261	deadreckon completion install
262	```
263	
264	For raw generated scripts or shell overrides, run `deadreckon completion --help`.
265	
266	Configure and run a task end-to-end:
267	
268	```bash
269	deadreckon init --provider cli:claude-code --sandbox auto --max-spend 10
270	
271	deadreckon def-done   "users can sign up, log in, and save a drawing"
272	deadreckon run    "build the app"
273	deadreckon attach latest    # watch live, Ctrl-D to detach
274	deadreckon doc    latest    # read the narrative once done
275	deadreckon apply  latest --autostash --cleanup
276	```
277	
278	`run` prints the run id and attach command immediately, and shows a preview of mode, branch, base ref, and worktree path before creating anything. Use `--preview` to print the preview and exit.
279	
280	### Try It Without API Keys
281	
282	```bash
283	DEADRECKON_HOME=$PWD/.deadreckon-smoke \
284	  deadreckon run "tiny hello rust" --smoke --sandbox none --max-spend 1
285	```
286	
287	The provider response is faked, but every other moving part (turn loop, sandbox, snapshots, spend, traces, gate) is real.
288	
289	## Configuration
290	
291	Switch providers, models, or defaults:
292	
293	```bash
294	deadreckon init --provider cli:codex --sandbox auto --max-spend 10
295	deadreckon init --provider anthropic --api-key "$ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"
296	deadreckon config provider cli:claude-code
297	deadreckon config model sonnet --provider cli:claude-code
298	deadreckon config set defaults.max_spend 15
299	```
300	
301	Override per run:
302	
303	```bash
304	deadreckon run "goal" --provider cli:codex --model gpt-5.1-codex
305	deadreckon run --preview "goal"     # show route and model, don't start
306	```
307	
308	Runtime config lives at `~/.deadreckon/config.toml`. Set `DEADRECKON_HOME` for isolated local runs or tests.
309	
310	### Sandbox Backends
311	
312	| Backend | What it is |
313	|---|---|
314	| `auto` | Picks the right native sandbox for your OS (default) |
315	| `sandbox-exec` | macOS native |
316	| `bwrap` | Linux native (bubblewrap) |
317	| `docker` | Opt-in container sandbox |
318	| `none` | Off (unsafe for real unattended work) |
319	
320	Check what your machine supports with `deadreckon doctor`.
321	
322	## Compared With Agentic Coding CLIs
323	
324	deadreckon doesn't replace Claude Code, Codex, or Cursor CLI; it supervises them. Use deadreckon when the task is too long, risky, or expensive to "run the agent in my checkout and hope I can reconstruct what happened."
325	
326	| Operational concern | Agentic CLI alone | deadreckon supervising the CLI |
327	|---|---|---|
328	| Workspace safety | Often runs where you start it | Creates an isolated worktree by default and leaves your checkout untouched |
329	| Long-running attach | Usually tied to the current terminal session | Run state is durable; attach from another terminal later |
330	| Process control | Kill/resume behavior varies by tool | Tracks child PIDs, kills live work, resumes from durable state |
331	| Spend control | Token/cost visibility varies by provider | Writes `spend.jsonl`, tracks totals, enforces spend and wall-clock caps |
332	| Undo | Usually git-level or manual | Snapshots every turn and restores a specific turn with `deadreckon undo` |
333	| Provenance | Conversation history may not map cleanly to file changes | Records model/tool/file linkage in `provenance.jsonl` |
334	| Observability | Tool logs are tool-specific | Writes normalized `events.jsonl`, `traces.jsonl`, spend, docs, and run state |
335	| Done criteria | The agent may declare itself done | Requires a signed `dr-gate` marker before promotion |
336	| Applying work | Patch review/apply flow is tool-specific | `apply`, `discard`, `export`, `extend`, and `cleanup` are first-class lifecycle actions |
337	| Multi-run coordination | Usually left to the operator | Scope/task locks prevent conflicting same-task runs |
338	
339	Use the agentic CLI for intelligence. Use deadreckon for isolation, supervision, evidence, recovery, and promotion.
340	
341	## Command Surface
342	
343	Core lifecycle:
344	
345	```text
346	init          create local config
347	config        inspect or edit config keys
348	run           start an unattended coding run
349	attach        open the live dashboard
350	status        latest run and next action for this project
351	list          list runs (current project; --all for every scope)
352	show          inspect state, lineage, spend, files
353	doc           print or export run documentation
354	apply         apply a completed worktree run to your branch
355	abandon       remove a worktree run and temporary branch
356	export        copy a completed artifact to a normal directory
357	extend        continue from a completed run
358	resume        continue an interrupted run
359	kill          stop a live run and child processes
360	undo          restore a previous turn snapshot
361	cleanup       clean abandoned, stale, or completed worktrees
362	finish        choose apply or export from completed run
363	import        normalize histories from other coding tools
364	doctor        check config, providers, sandboxes, disk, runtime
365	```
366	
367	Aliases: `keep` → `apply`, `materialize` → `export`, `discard` → `abandon`, `prune` → `cleanup`, `follow-up` → `extend`, `continue` → `resume`, `stop` → `kill`, `next` → `status`.
368	
369	## Verification
370	
371	Full local verification:
372	
373	```bash
374	make verify
375	```
376	
377	Useful targeted checks:
378	
379	```bash
380	make build
381	make smoke
382	make doctor
383	STRESS_SECONDS=30 make stress
384	```
385	
386	The workspace test suite covers provider routing, mock OpenAI-compatible runs, CLI-provider wrappers, kill/resume behavior, signed gates, snapshots, provenance/trace linkage, worktree/copy/in-place modes, lifecycle actions, docs generation, and multi-run locking.
387	
388	## Status
389	
390	deadreckon is alpha software. The core lifecycle (isolated runs, signed gates, durable state, undo, docs, and apply) is implemented and tested.
391	
392	The V1 candidate list is deliberately short. The next big feature is explicit sub-agent forking:
393	
394	```text
395	deadreckon fork <run-id> --prompt "..."
396	```
397

```text
fn chain_attach_tui(paths: &DeadreckonPaths, chain_id: &str) -> Result<()> {
    enable_raw_mode()?;
    let mut stdout = io::stdout();
    execute!(stdout, EnterAlternateScreen, EnableMouseCapture)?;
    let backend = CrosstermBackend::new(stdout);
    let mut terminal = Terminal::new(backend)?;
    let mut tui_state = ChainAttachTuiState::default();

    let result = loop {
        let mut tick = AttachTickTiming::new(AttachSurface::Chain, AttachTickBudget::default());
        let stage_started = Instant::now();
        let chain = load_chain(paths, chain_id)?;
        tick.record_since(AttachLoopStage::LoadState, stage_started);
        let stage_started = Instant::now();
        let events = read_jsonl::<ChainEvent>(&paths.chain_events(chain_id))?;
        tick.record_since(AttachLoopStage::ReadJsonl, stage_started);
        tui_state.clamp(&chain);
        let stage_started = Instant::now();
        terminal.draw(|frame| render_chain_attach(frame, &chain, &events, &tui_state))?;
        tick.record_since(AttachLoopStage::Draw, stage_started);

        let stage_started = Instant::now();
        let input_ready = event::poll(Duration::from_millis(200))?;
        tick.record_since(AttachLoopStage::InputPoll, stage_started);
        drop(tick.slow_sync_stages());
        drop(tick.slow_stage_labels());
        let _ = tick.frame_exceeded();
        if input_ready {
            match event::read()? {
                Event::Key(key) if attach_should_quit(key) => break Ok(()),
                Event::Key(key) => match key.code {
                    KeyCode::Enter => {
                        suspend_tui(&mut terminal)?;
                        if let Some(run_id) = chain
                            .steps
                            .get(tui_state.selected_step)
                            .and_then(|step| step.run_id.clone())
                        {
                            let _ = show_command(&run_id, None, false, false, false, false, None);
                        } else {
                            eprintln!("selected step has no run yet");
                        }
                        let _ = prompt::open("press Enter to return to chain attach...", None);
                        resume_tui(&mut terminal)?;
                    }
                    KeyCode::Char('r') => {
                        suspend_tui(&mut terminal)?;
                        let action = chain_redo_command(
                            paths,
                            chain_id,
                            Some(tui_state.selected_step as u32 + 1),
                            None,
                            false,
                        );
                        if let Err(err) = &action {
                            print_error(err);
                        }
                        let _ = prompt::open("press Enter to return to chain attach...", None);
                        resume_tui(&mut terminal)?;
                    }
                    KeyCode::Char('e') => {
                        suspend_tui(&mut terminal)?;
                        let goal = prompt::open("new chain step goal: ", None)?;
                        if !goal.trim().is_empty() {
                            let action = chain_extend_command(paths, chain_id, goal, None, None);
                            if let Err(err) = &action {
                                print_error(err);
