```text
100	Every provider response appends a spend record and updates totals. API routes track token cost. Subscription CLI routes can be capped by wall-clock time.
101	
102	```bash
103	deadreckon run "large refactor" --max-spend 15
104	deadreckon run "large refactor" --max-wall-seconds 1800
105	```
106	
107	High spend requires explicit confirmation, so scripts do not accidentally launch expensive runs.
108	
109	### Undo A Single Bad Turn Without Losing The Rest
110	
111	deadreckon snapshots the working directory at turn boundaries:
112	
113	```bash
114	deadreckon undo --run <run-id>
115	deadreckon undo --run <run-id> --turn 3
116	```
117	
118	This is not just `git reset`. It works against the run's own snapshot trail and records the undo in the run trace.
119	
120	### Write "Done" In English, Verified By A Watchdog
121	
122	Tell deadreckon what success looks like in plain language. It compiles your sentence into executable checks that an independent watchdog runs:
123	
124	```bash
125	deadreckon def-done "build, load in a browser, and show no console errors"
126	deadreckon def-done add "users can save drawings"
127	deadreckon def-done check
128	deadreckon run "finish the app"
129	```
130	
131	`deadreckon run` and `deadreckon chain run` prompt interactively when a project has no acceptance file yet. Generated files live under `.deadreckon/`.
132	
133	**Why the watchdog matters.** The watchdog holds a secret the agent process cannot read. It stamps the result with that secret. Without a valid stamp, the run can't terminate, and the agent can't produce the stamp itself.
134	
135	If no acceptance file is configured, the default is "the working directory exists and `cargo test` passes" (when `Cargo.toml` is present).
136	
137	You can still edit the compiled YAML directly:
138	
139	```yaml
140	name: notes check
141	checks:
142	  - kind: file_exists
143	    path: "{working_dir}/notes.md"
144	  - kind: content_match
145	    path: "{working_dir}/notes.md"
146	    pattern: "dead reckoning"
147	  - kind: build_success
148	    cwd: "{working_dir}"
149	```
150	
151	Supported executable check kinds are `cargo_test`, `file_exists`, `content_match`, `build_success`, and `shell`. `content_match` treats `pattern` as a regex when valid, with substring fallback for simple text.
152	
153	### Get An Auditable Artifact, Not A Transcript
154	
155	deadreckon records which model/tool call touched which files, then writes self-documenting artifacts for the completed run:
156	
157	```bash
158	deadreckon doc <run-id>
159	deadreckon doc <run-id> --kind as-built
160	deadreckon doc <run-id> --kind decisions
161	deadreckon doc <run-id> --kind delta
162	```
163	
164	Each accepted run produces a review packet:
165	
166	- `RUN-NARRATIVE.md` explains what happened.
167	- `RUN-AS-BUILT.md` captures the subsystem shape after the run.
168	- `RUN-DECISIONS.md` records the implementation decision ledger: design decisions, deviations, tradeoffs, open questions, and multi-alternative decision details.
169	- `implementation-notes.html` is the live working copy the agent maintains while changing files.
170	- `AS-BUILT-DELTA.md` proposes architecture-doc updates when the run is broad enough.
171	- `manifest.json` records what was built and from what.
172	
173	Agentic CLIs usually leave you with a patch and a transcript. deadreckon turns
174	the session into a local published artifact you can inspect, export, extend, or
175	apply.
176	
177	### Resume, Kill, Extend, Or Export Any Run
178	
179	Runs are lifecycle objects, not one terminal session:
180	
181	```bash
182	deadreckon list
183	deadreckon status
184	deadreckon show latest
185	deadreckon kill latest
186	deadreckon resume latest
187	deadreckon resume latest --from-turn 2
188	deadreckon extend latest "add tests and polish the UI"
189	deadreckon finish latest
190	deadreckon export latest --dest ./finished-project
191	deadreckon cleanup --completed
192	```
193	
194	Resume reconstructs history from durable traces and ignores incomplete trailing trace entries.
195	
196	### Autonomous Chains For Multi-Step Work
197	
198	Some tasks are too big for one goal. Chains let you break work into ordered steps that run end-to-end, with the same gate enforcement and the same lifecycle commands per step:
199	
200	```bash
201	deadreckon chain plan "ship a working SaaS billing flow" --n 4
202	deadreckon chain run latest
203	deadreckon chain attach latest
204	deadreckon chain kill latest
205	```
206	
207	Each chain step is a real run with its own signed acceptance gate. If a step fails its gate, the chain stops there; later steps don't start. Killing a chain cascades to whatever step is live. The attach TUI shows the whole chain timeline, not just the current turn, so you can see where you are in the plan without leaving the dashboard.
208	
209	You can also extend a finished run into a follow-up step instead of planning the whole chain up front:
210	
211	```bash
212	deadreckon chain extend latest "add billing webhooks and retry logic"
213	```
214	
215	## The Mental Model
216	
217	```text
218	your repo
219	  |
220	  | deadreckon def-done "what 'finished' looks like, in English"
221	  | deadreckon run  "what to build"
222	  v
223	isolated worktree or copy   ◄── your real checkout untouched
224	  |
225	  | provider route: cli:codex, cli:claude-code, anthropic, openai, ...
226	  v
227	sandboxed turn loop         ◄── agent works here
228	  |
229	  | every turn: trace, spend, provenance, snapshot, docs
230	  | check fails? agent gets another turn
231	  v
232	dr-gate watchdog            ◄── separate process, holds hidden nonce
233	  |                              agent CANNOT produce a valid marker
234	  | checks pass + signature valid?
235	  v
236	promoted artifact           ◄── narrative, decisions, file lineage
237	  |
238	  | inspect, doc, apply, discard, extend, export, cleanup
239	  v
240	your branch or library
241	```
242	
243	For multi-step work, `deadreckon chain` wraps this whole loop and runs N of them in order, stopping on the first gate failure.
244	
245	The agent owns the coding. deadreckon owns the boundary.
246	
247	## Quickstart
248	
249	Build once:
250	
251	```bash
252	cargo build --release
253	```
254	
255	The binary is `./target/release/deadreckon`. Add it to your `PATH` or alias it; the rest of this README just says `deadreckon`.
256	
257	Install shell tab completion. `deadreckon init` does this automatically when it
258	can detect your shell; this command repairs or installs it later:
259	
260	```bash
261	deadreckon completion install
262	```
263	
264	For raw generated scripts or shell overrides, run `deadreckon completion --help`.
265	
266	Configure and run a task end-to-end:
267	
268	```bash
269	deadreckon init --provider cli:claude-code --sandbox auto --max-spend 10
270	
271	deadreckon def-done   "users can sign up, log in, and save a drawing"
272	deadreckon run    "build the app"
273	deadreckon attach latest    # watch live, Ctrl-D to detach
274	deadreckon doc    latest    # read the narrative once done
275	deadreckon apply  latest --autostash --cleanup
276	```
277	
278	`run` prints the run id and attach command immediately, and shows a preview of mode, branch, base ref, and worktree path before creating anything. Use `--preview` to print the preview and exit.
279

284	  deadreckon run "tiny hello rust" --smoke --sandbox none --max-spend 1
285	```
286	
287	The provider response is faked, but every other moving part (turn loop, sandbox, snapshots, spend, traces, gate) is real.

310	### Sandbox Backends
311	
312	| Backend | What it is |
313	|---|---|
314	| `auto` | Picks the right native sandbox for your OS (default) |
315	| `sandbox-exec` | macOS native |
316	| `bwrap` | Linux native (bubblewrap) |
317	| `docker` | Opt-in container sandbox |
318	| `none` | Off (unsafe for real unattended work) |
319	
320	Check what your machine supports with `deadreckon doctor`.
321	
322	## Compared With Agentic Coding CLIs
323	
324	deadreckon doesn't replace Claude Code, Codex, or Cursor CLI; it supervises them. Use deadreckon when the task is too long, risky, or expensive to "run the agent in my checkout and hope I can reconstruct what happened."
325	
326	| Operational concern | Agentic CLI alone | deadreckon supervising the CLI |
327	|---|---|---|
328	| Workspace safety | Often runs where you start it | Creates an isolated worktree by default and leaves your checkout untouched |
329	| Long-running attach | Usually tied to the current terminal session | Run state is durable; attach from another terminal later |
330	| Process control | Kill/resume behavior varies by tool | Tracks child PIDs, kills live work, resumes from durable state |
331	| Spend control | Token/cost visibility varies by provider | Writes `spend.jsonl`, tracks totals, enforces spend and wall-clock caps |
332	| Undo | Usually git-level or manual | Snapshots every turn and restores a specific turn with `deadreckon undo` |
333	| Provenance | Conversation history may not map cleanly to file changes | Records model/tool/file linkage in `provenance.jsonl` |
334	| Observability | Tool logs are tool-specific | Writes normalized `events.jsonl`, `traces.jsonl`, spend, docs, and run state |
335	| Done criteria | The agent may declare itself done | Requires a signed `dr-gate` marker before promotion |
336	| Applying work | Patch review/apply flow is tool-specific | `apply`, `discard`, `export`, `extend`, and `cleanup` are first-class lifecycle actions |
337	| Multi-run coordination | Usually left to the operator | Scope/task locks prevent conflicting same-task runs |
338	
339	Use the agentic CLI for intelligence. Use deadreckon for isolation, supervision, evidence, recovery, and promotion.
340	
341	## Command Surface
342	
343	Core lifecycle:
344	
345	```text
346	init          create local config
347	config        inspect or edit config keys
348	run           start an unattended coding run
349	attach        open the live dashboard
350	status        latest run and next action for this project
351	list          list runs (current project; --all for every scope)
352	show          inspect state, lineage, spend, files
353	doc           print or export run documentation
354	apply         apply a completed worktree run to your branch
355	abandon       remove a worktree run and temporary branch
356	export        copy a completed artifact to a normal directory
357	extend        continue from a completed run
358	resume        continue an interrupted run
359	kill          stop a live run and child processes
360	undo          restore a previous turn snapshot
361	cleanup       clean abandoned, stale, or completed worktrees
362	finish        choose apply or export from completed run
363	import        normalize histories from other coding tools
364	doctor        check config, providers, sandboxes, disk, runtime
365	```
366	
367	Aliases: `keep` → `apply`, `materialize` → `export`, `discard` → `abandon`, `prune` → `cleanup`, `follow-up` → `extend`, `continue` → `resume`, `stop` → `kill`, `next` → `status`.
368	
369	## Verification
370	
371	Full local verification:
372	
373	```bash
374	make verify
375	```
376	
377	Useful targeted checks:
378	
379	```bash
380	make build
381	make smoke
382	make doctor
383	STRESS_SECONDS=30 make stress
384	```
385	
386	The workspace test suite covers provider routing, mock OpenAI-compatible runs, CLI-provider wrappers, kill/resume behavior, signed gates, snapshots, provenance/trace linkage, worktree/copy/in-place modes, lifecycle actions, docs generation, and multi-run locking.
387	
388	## Status
389	
390	deadreckon is alpha software. The core lifecycle (isolated runs, signed gates, durable state, undo, docs, and apply) is implemented and tested.
391	
392	The V1 candidate list is deliberately short. The next big feature is explicit sub-agent forking:
393	
394	```text
395	deadreckon fork <run-id> --prompt "..."
396	```

84	Every turn writes state, traces, spend, file provenance, and a working-directory snapshot under `~/.deadreckon/runstate/`. If the terminal dies, attach from another. If the run itself crashes, resume from the last completed turn.
85	
86	### Walk Away, Attach From Any Terminal
87	
88	```bash
89	deadreckon attach latest
90	```
91	
92	The TUI shows live status, current step, spend, recent file edits, and provider activity. Completed runs render `RUN-NARRATIVE.md` inline. Press `Ctrl-D` to detach without killing the run.
93	
94	For longer or multi-agent work, use `deadreckon attach latest --view narrative` for a cited operator overview with an evidence-backed visual map. Raw activity stays one key away with `n`; `v` cycles architecture, agent, file, and evidence views.
95	
96	Provider-backed narrative refresh defaults to local Claude Code on Sonnet when available; use `--narrative-provider <route>` to override the narrator, or `--no-narrative-provider` for deterministic-only attach.
97	
98	### Set A Budget And A Time Limit, Then Walk Away
99	
100	Every provider response appends a spend record and updates totals. API routes track token cost. Subscription CLI routes can be capped by wall-clock time.
101	
102	```bash
103	deadreckon run "large refactor" --max-spend 15
104	deadreckon run "large refactor" --max-wall-seconds 1800
105	```
106	
107	High spend requires explicit confirmation, so scripts do not accidentally launch expensive runs.
108	
109	### Undo A Single Bad Turn Without Losing The Rest
110	
111	deadreckon snapshots the working directory at turn boundaries:
112	
113	```bash
114	deadreckon undo --run <run-id>
115	deadreckon undo --run <run-id> --turn 3
116	```
117	
118	This is not just `git reset`. It works against the run's own snapshot trail and records the undo in the run trace.
119	
120	### Write "Done" In English, Verified By A Watchdog
121	
122	Tell deadreckon what success looks like in plain language. It compiles your sentence into executable checks that an independent watchdog runs:
123	
124	```bash
125	deadreckon def-done "build, load in a browser, and show no console errors"
126	deadreckon def-done add "users can save drawings"
127	deadreckon def-done check
128	deadreckon run "finish the app"
129	```
130	
131	`deadreckon run` and `deadreckon chain run` prompt interactively when a project has no acceptance file yet. Generated files live under `.deadreckon/`.
132	
133	**Why the watchdog matters.** The watchdog holds a secret the agent process cannot read. It stamps the result with that secret. Without a valid stamp, the run can't terminate, and the agent can't produce the stamp itself.

```text
### 18.4 Narrative projection files

Narrative attach writes projection files, not source-of-truth state. Run projections live under `<run-root>/narrative/`; plan projections live under `<plan-dir>/narrative/`.

- `state.json` records the latest snapshot id/status, coverage, cadence, provider source, provider call count, cost/wall-clock accounting, and last refresh error.
- `snapshots.jsonl` is append-only. Each row contains cited `current_work`, `architecture_notes`, `risks`, `next_likely`, citations, and plan-only agent/coordination sections. Malformed rows are skipped when reading the latest snapshot.
- `architecture-graph.json` is a deterministic graph over run files, provider ids, checkpoints, plan tasks, dependencies, child runs, and citation ids. The TUI renders architecture, agent, file, and evidence views from this graph using ASCII-compatible labels and color-independent badges.

Plan projections prefer each child run's latest narrative snapshot when one exists. The plan agent table cites that child snapshot and uses its headline as the child summary, then falls back to child run state when no child narrative exists. Plan graphs also roll up file nodes from child narrative graphs so the plan-level files visual can show cross-agent touched file evidence without copying child logs into `plan-events.jsonl`.

Provider-backed narration is an overlay on these projections. Manual `r` refresh, TTY narrative-view event refreshes, and TTY narrative-view quiet-threshold refreshes build a redacted prompt from the deterministic projection, send only bounded evidence summaries to the selected provider route, validate all returned claims against known evidence ids, reject invented graph ids, and persist a new fresh snapshot only after validation. The default narrator route is `cli:claude-code` with model override `sonnet`, which the Claude Code adapter launches as `claude --model sonnet --dangerously-skip-permissions -p <prompt>`; `--narrative-provider` overrides the route and leaves model selection to that provider/config entry, while `--no-narrative-provider` keeps attach deterministic-only. Event refreshes can bypass the ordinary freshness interval for meaningful deltas, while quiet-threshold refreshes still obey the freshness interval; budget, provider availability, JSON validation, citation validation, graph validation, and redaction guards always apply. If the provider is missing, over budget, behind cadence, returns malformed JSON, cites unknown evidence, emits secret-like text, or fails, attach keeps running and persists a stale deterministic snapshot with the error in `state.json`.

---
```
</details></tool-use>

### §14 Telemetry: §14.4 events.jsonl — internal contradiction

**Finding 2 — events bus parenthetical contradicts §18.3 and §22; and the actual code tells a third story**

The doc says: "Also published on a `tokio::sync::broadcast` channel (`events.rs`) for in-process subscribers (the TUI uses this when implemented; today the TUI polls files instead — see §22)."

§18.3 (line 1295) says: "Same-process run attaches can use the `RunEventBus` broadcast channel directly."
§22 (line 1488) says: "Event-backed TUI attach: same-process attaches use `RunEventBus`; cross-process attaches replay `events.jsonl` incrementally."

The code reality (`tui_events.rs:26-37`, `main.rs:23540`): `TuiEventFeed::from_broadcast` is gated `#[cfg(test)]`. Production `attach_tui_with_parent` uses `TuiEventFeed::file_tail` unconditionally — even for same-process runs. The broadcast is emitted to the channel and also written to file simultaneously (`events.rs:99-101`), but the TUI only reads the file. So §18.3 and §22's claim that "same-process attaches use RunEventBus" is currently false at the production path. §14.4's old parenthetical "today the TUI polls files instead" was actually correct at the attach level, but incorrect to say the bus is unused — it's just unused by the TUI itself (used by tests only).

The right fix is to update §14.4 to accurately describe what `emit_event` does (both writes file and sends on channel), note that the TUI always reads via file tail even in-process, and update §18.3/§22 to match.

For §14.4:

EDIT old: `Also published on a \`tokio::sync::broadcast\` channel (\`events.rs\`) for in-process subscribers (the TUI uses this when implemented; today the TUI polls files instead — see §22).`

EDIT new: `Also published on a \`tokio::sync::broadcast\` channel (\`events.rs\`) for in-process subscribers. The \`emit_event\` function writes to \`events.jsonl\` and sends on the channel simultaneously (\`events.rs:89-104\`). Production \`attach\` always reads via \`TuiEventFeed::file_tail\` — even for same-process runs (\`main.rs:23540\`); the broadcast-receiver path in \`TuiEventFeed::from_broadcast\` is \`#[cfg(test)]\` only (\`tui_events.rs:25-37\`). The file tail is the authoritative live-events path; the broadcast channel is available for future same-process subscribers.`

For §18.3 (line 1295):

EDIT old: `Same-process run attaches can use the \`RunEventBus\` broadcast channel directly; cross-process run attaches still poll.`

EDIT new: `Both same-process and cross-process run attaches read via \`TuiEventFeed::file_tail\`, which tails \`events.jsonl\` on disk (\`main.rs:23540\`, \`tui_events.rs:39-43\`). The \`RunEventBus\` broadcast path in \`TuiEventFeed::from_broadcast\` is compiled in test builds only. The run loop's \`emit_event\` writes to file and sends on the channel simultaneously, so the file tail is always up to date.`

For §22 (line 1488):

EDIT old: `Event-backed TUI attach: same-process attaches use \`RunEventBus\`; cross-process attaches replay \`events.jsonl\` incrementally.`

EDIT new: `Event-backed TUI attach: both same-process and cross-process attaches tail \`events.jsonl\` incrementally via \`TuiEventFeed::file_tail\`; the \`RunEventBus\` broadcast path is test-only.`

1954:Merge creates a normal promoted run so existing `materialize`, `library`, and run inspection paths keep working. Plan ids resolve through the same prefix-matching path as run ids, so `apply <plan-id>`, `finish <plan-id>`, `export <plan-id>`, and `materialize <plan-id>` all accept either a full plan id or an unambiguous prefix and route through `resolve_plan_result_run` (`main.rs:12508`) onto the merged promoted run. `apply <plan-id>` lands the merged tree on the source branch (with `--autostash` / `--cleanup` honored exactly as for normal runs); `finish <plan-id>` picks `apply` for git worktrees and `export` for non-git sources; `export <plan-id> --dest <path>` writes the merged library to disk. The promoted library also gets `deadreckon-plan-manifest.json` with plan id, root goal, mode, provider roles, capability preview, task graph, child run ids, summary paths, coordinator message counts, and recorded conflicts.

```text
1795:A chain is an ordered list of step goals plus branch, apply, budget, and stop policy. The conductor is a CLI process entered by `deadreckon chain ...` or `deadreckon chain run <id>`. It acquires a chain lock, spawns each step as a normal `deadreckon run --worktree`, waits for that run to complete and pass acceptance, applies it to the source branch when policy allows, then bases the next step on the updated head.
1936:Every child run receives an inline copy of its worker spec in the prompt. The spec includes root goal, exact task scope, provider, role, dependency context, capability preview, and hygiene rules such as staying within scope and not spawning subagents. The current worker-spec posture borrows Claude Code's coordinator rules: the spec is the complete brief, children should not inspect sibling transcripts, corrections stay with the worker that has the failure context, and reviewer lanes verify independently rather than inheriting coder assumptions.
2021:`plan` appends `plan_created` after `plan.json` is saved. `fork` appends `plan_started` exactly once per invocation, then `task_ready` for each task in the ready batch, `task_started` before each child spawn, `task_run_discovered` when a PID or run id becomes known, and one of `task_completed` / `task_failed` / `task_blocked` / `task_killed` on each terminal transition (including dependency-blocker events). `merge` appends `merge_started`, optional `merge_conflict`, then the optional repair sequence (`merge_repair_planned` / `merge_repair_started` / `merge_repair_run_discovered` / `merge_repaired` or `merge_repair_failed`), then `merge_completed` and `plan_completed`. Idempotency and ordering are covered by depth tests added in commit `4fcb7f9`. `kill <plan-id>` appends `task_killed` per child, then `plan_killed` and `plan_failed`, preserving discovered run ids and PIDs even if a child already reached a terminal state before the kill sweep loaded it so recovery commands can still map live processes back to durable state.
2052:`deadreckon-runtime/src/flight.rs` implements `ProviderFlightRecorder`. The run loop starts it after the pre-turn `snapshot_working(turn-1)` and before the CLI provider subprocess. The recorder loads provider descriptor ingest metadata, marks rerun/resume sessions at or after the new turn as `superseded`, assigns `flight-turn-<n>-attempt-<m>`, and spawns a sidecar polling loop while the provider runs.
```

| Module | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `artifacts.rs` | `copy_tree`, `snapshot_working`, `restore_snapshot`, `append_{spend,trace,provenance}`, `inventory_files` |

| `chain.rs` | autonomous goal-chain records, `ChainStatus`, `ChainStep`, `ConductorState`, chain event bus |
| `codebase.rs` | `CodebaseMode`, `CodebaseRecord`, worktree/copy/fresh/in-place materialization, `create_worktree` |
| `docs.rs` | run-doc templates (`RUN_NARRATIVE`, `RUN_AS_BUILT`, `RUN_DECISIONS`), frontmatter, inventory, delta JSONL, polish records |
| `error.rs` | `DeadreckonError`, `Result<T>`, `is_retryable()`, `is_fatal()` |
| `events.rs` | `RunEvent`, `RunEventBus`, `RunEventKind`, `tokio::sync::broadcast` channel, JSONL emit |
| `flight.rs` | `FlightManifest`, `FlightSession`, checkpoint policy, provider log capture, rewind event recording (`flight-manifest.json`, `flight-events.jsonl`, `rewind-events.jsonl`, `checkpoints/`) |
| `gate.rs` | `AcceptanceMarker`, `AcceptanceSpec`, `AcceptanceCheck`, signature validation, anti-self-attestation, progress JSONL |

EDIT old:
``lib.rs:111-169` is the single dispatch entry point. It:
1. Calls `build_command(spec)` to construct the per-backend invocation.
2. Spawns the child via `tokio::process::Command`, capturing stdout + stderr piped.
3. Persists the child PID to `spec.pid_file` (line 129) for `kill` supervision.
4. Reads stdout/stderr in parallel async tasks (`read_pipe`, lines 171–181).

6. Returns `SandboxRunOutput { stdout, stderr, status_code, pid, backend, warning }`.`

2. Spawns the child via `tokio::process::Command`, capturing stdout + stderr piped.
3. Persists the child PID to `spec.pid_file` (`process.rs:36-41`) for `kill` supervision.
4. Reads stdout/stderr in parallel async tasks (`read_pipe`, `process.rs:82-92`).
5. Runs the cancellation `tokio::select!` (`process.rs:42-62`).
6. Returns `SandboxRunOutput { stdout, stderr, status_code, pid, backend, warning }`.`

## README drift (my area)

**The `fork` nomenclature collision**: README "Status" section (line 392-396) says:

> The next big feature is explicit sub-agent forking:
> ```text
> deadreckon fork <run-id> --prompt "..."
> ```

But `deadreckon fork <plan-id>` already exists as the command that starts child runs for an orchestration plan (confirmed at cli.rs:738-773). The README is describing a *run-level* sub-agent fork (spawning an ad-hoc child from any run), which is distinct from the *plan-level* `fork` that executes ready plan tasks. The run-level fork described in the README ("fork from any run with a --prompt") is NOT the same as `deadreckon fork <plan-id>` — plan fork requires a prior `deadreckon plan` step and executes pre-specified tasks. The README "next big feature" refers to an ad-hoc sub-agent fork that does not appear to be built yet in any form.

EDIT old: `"The next big feature is explicit sub-agent forking:\n\n```text\ndeadreckon fork <run-id> --prompt \"...\"\n```"`
EDIT new: `"The next big feature is run-level sub-agent forking: spawning a child agent from any run id with a fresh prompt. Note: ``deadreckon fork <plan-id>`` already exists for plan orchestration, which starts pre-specified worker tasks. The V1 candidate described here (``deadreckon fork <run-id> --prompt \"...\"``) is a different capability — ad-hoc mid-run sub-agent spawning — that is not yet implemented."`

**README omits major built features**: The Command Surface table (lines 343-367) omits:
- `chain` (present only in "Autonomous Chains" feature section prose, not in the command surface table)
- `plan` / `fork` / `merge` / `orchestrate` (multi-agent orchestration entirely absent from command table)
- `rewind` (flight recorder/rewind — entirely absent)
- `learn` / `improve` (self-improvement loop — entirely absent)
- `flight` as a show flag (show --flight)

These warrant mention in the README command surface table since they are all built and tested. Minimal additions for `chain`, `plan`/`fork`/`merge`, `rewind`, and `learn`/`improve` would make the command surface accurate.

fn collect_acceptance_live(state: &deadreckon_core::PipelineState) -> AcceptanceLive {
    let marker_path = marker_path_for_run_root(&state.run_root);
    if marker_path.exists()
        && let Ok(bytes) = fs::read(&marker_path)
        && let Ok(marker) = serde_json::from_slice::<AcceptanceMarker>(&bytes)
    {
        return acceptance_live_from_marker(&marker);
    }

    let progress_path = acceptance_progress_path_for_run_root(&state.run_root);
    if progress_path.exists()
        && let Ok(entries) = read_jsonl::<AcceptanceProgressEntry>(&progress_path)
        && !entries.is_empty()
    {
        return acceptance_live_from_progress(&entries);
    }

    let spec_path = acceptance_spec_path_for_run_root(&state.run_root);
    if spec_path.exists()
        && let Ok(raw) = fs::read_to_string(&spec_path)
        && let Ok(count) = acceptance_check_count(&raw)
    {
        return AcceptanceLive {
            status: AcceptanceUiStatus::Configured,
            total: count,
            latest_detail: Some("runs after provider completion".to_string()),
            ..AcceptanceLive::default()
        };
    }

    AcceptanceLive {
        latest_detail: Some("inferred from project files".to_string()),
        ..AcceptanceLive::default()
    }
}

    state: &deadreckon_core::PipelineState,
    provider_activity: ProviderActivity,
) -> AttachLive {
    let inventory = attach_live_inventory(&state.working_dir);

        .into_iter()
        .map(live_pid)
        .collect::<Vec<_>>();
    let acceptance = collect_acceptance_live(state);
    AttachLive {
        file_count: inventory.file_count,
        total_bytes: inventory.total_bytes,
        files: inventory.files,
        pids,
        provider_context_tokens: provider_activity.context_tokens,
        provider_context_window: provider_activity.context_window,

1249	The `Commands` enum in `crates/deadreckon/src/main.rs` defines the CLI surface. Handlers and roles:
1250	
1251	| Verb | Handler | Role |
1252	|---|---|---|
1253	| `init` | `cli.rs:440` | Interactive setup of `~/.deadreckon/config.toml` |
1254	| `config get/set` | `cli.rs:465` | Non-interactive TOML edits |
1255	| `run` | `cli.rs:537` | Create + enter turn loop |
1256	| `doctor` | `cli.rs:910` | 8-point actionable preflight |
1257	| `status` / `next` | `cli.rs:1308` | Current project's latest run, locations, and next action |
1258	| `list` | `cli.rs:964` | Project-scoped run inventory by default; `--all` for global history, `--full` for exact values |
1259	| `apply` | `cli.rs:1062` | Apply a completed worktree run (or merged plan result) to the user's current branch |
1260	| `finish` | `cli.rs:992` | Choose the right completion action (apply for git worktrees, export for non-git) for a run or merged plan |
1261	| `abandon` / `discard` | `cli.rs:1103` | Remove a run's worktree branch/path or mark no-op modes abandoned |
1262	| `materialize` / `export` | `cli.rs:1041` | Copy a completed fresh/copy artifact (or merged plan result) to a normal directory |
1263	| `cleanup` / `prune` | `cli.rs:1121` | Clean abandoned, stale, or selected completed worktree runs |
1264	| `attach` | `cli.rs:1216` | TUI on a live or completed run, chain, or plan |
1265	| `kill` | `cli.rs:1230` | Lock release + child PID termination (run, chain, or plan) |
1266	| `resume` | `cli.rs:1248` | Re-enter the loop on a non-Completed run |
1267	| `extend` | `cli.rs:1149` | Re-open a completed run with a follow-up goal that inherits history |
1268	| `undo` | `cli.rs:1265` | Restore snapshot to a target turn |
1269	| `show` | `cli.rs:1281` | Pretty-print full state + provenance + traces; `--why-failed` for runs and plans |
1270	| `import` | `cli.rs:1329` | Read-only descriptor-backed transcript import from CLI providers plus Cursor SQLite |
1271	| `chain` | `cli.rs:798` | Create, plan, run, attach, pause/resume/kill, undo, extend, and redo serial autonomous chains |
1272	| `orchestrate` | `cli.rs:630` | One-command wrappers for `review` and `full-plan` multi-agent runs |
1273	| `plan` | `cli.rs:679` | Write an orchestration plan (worker specs + `plan.json`) without starting child runs |
1274	| `fork` | `cli.rs:720` | Spawn ready child runs for a plan and supervise them through completion |
1275	| `merge` | `cli.rs:756` | Compose completed child library artifacts into a new promoted run (with semantic merge repair) |
1276	| `def-done` | `cli.rs:502` | Write, add, show, or check the project's English done criteria |
1277	| `acceptance` | `cli.rs:492` | Hidden compatibility surface for creating, explaining, or checking done criteria |
1278	| `doc` | `cli.rs:1182` | Print run narrative, as-built, implementation decision ledger, or delta; with optional polish pass |
1279	| `history` | `cli.rs:1298` | Search durable run traces and provenance (regex/scope/plan filters) |
1280	| `library` | `cli.rs:983` | Query promoted run artifacts by goal/date/scope |
1281	| `detect` | `cli.rs:919` | Probe registered providers and return availability and credential status |
1282	| `providers` | `cli.rs:932` | List provider routes, models, kind tokens, and the active selection |
1283	| `update` | `cli.rs:941` | Check for or route self-updates via npm, Homebrew, shell, Cargo, or source channel |
1284	| `completion` / `completions` | `cli.rs:482` | Generate or install shell tab-completion scripts (bash, zsh, fish, elvish, powershell) |
1285	
1286	The CLI defaults are honest: `--sandbox` defaults to `auto`, `--max-spend` defaults to `$10` (with a confirmation gate above `$50`), `--provider` defaults to the highest-credentialed entry per the fallback chain, `--skill` defaults to `default-coding`.
1287	
1288	`run` now starts codebase-aware by default. In a git repo it previews and then creates a `git worktree` on a `dr/...` branch; `--fresh` preserves the old empty-working-dir behavior, `--from <path>` uses copy mode, and `--in-place --i-know-its-a-lot` edits the source tree directly. Completed worktree runs hint `apply` / `discard`; copy and fresh runs hint `export` / `extend`. Run-id arguments accept unique prefixes and `latest` / `last` resolves to the latest run in the current project scope.

673	### 9.3 Loop body (paraphrased; see `crates/deadreckon-runtime/src/turn_loop.rs`)
674	
675	```text
676	load_or_reconstruct_history()      # lines 69, 550-631
677	set Phase(40)=Executing            # line 70
678	save_state(); save_history()       # line 71
679	
680	for turn in (state.turn+1)..=max_turns:
681	    if cancelled or status=Killed:
682	        return Killed
683	    emit TurnStarted event
684	    snapshot_working(turn-1)        # capture pre-turn state
685	    prompt = build_prompt(state, history) [or build_cli_subagent_prompt]
686	    request = ProviderRequest{
687	        prompt, max_output_tokens=2048, cwd, output_path, sandbox_backend,
688	        pid_file=run_root/child-pids/provider-turn-N.pid,
689	        cancellation_token=turn_token,
690	    }
691	    response = router.complete(&request).await
692	    append_trace(llm.complete, latency, response.trace)
693	    state.total_spend_usd += response.spend.cost_usd
694	    state.total_wall_seconds += response.spend.wall_time_seconds
695	    append_spend(...)
696	    if max_spend exceeded: return PausedAtCap
697	    if subscription and max_wall_seconds exceeded: return PausedAtCap
698	
699	    if response is cli_subagent:
700	        changed = changed_files_since_snapshot(turn-1)
701	        if changed.is_empty: return Failed
702	        snapshot_working(turn)
703	        append_trace(tool.cli_subagent, files=changed)
704	        append_provenance_for_files(turn, tool_call_id, model, changed)
705	        run_acceptance_gate(state)        # dr-gate
706	        validate_acceptance_marker(state) # signed?
707	        promote_if_ready(state)           # working → library
708	        set Phase(60)=Completed
709	        return Done
710	
711	    parse Action from response.content (serde tag="action"):
712	        Bash { tool_call_id, command } =>
713	            run_sandbox(SandboxSpec{
714	                program=sh, args=[-lc, command], cwd=working_dir,
715	                pid_file, cancellation_token=turn_token.child_token(),
716	                read_allowlist=[working_dir],
717	                allow_network=false,
718	            }).await
719	            append_trace(tool.bash, stdout, stderr, status)
720	            snapshot_working(turn); append_provenance(turn, changed_files)
721	            history.push("tool {id} result: status={...}")
722	        WriteFile { tool_call_id, path, content } =>
723	            safe_working_path(path); write_file
724	            append_trace(tool.write_file); snapshot_working(turn)
725	            append_provenance(turn, [path])
726	            history.push("tool {id} result: wrote file")
727	        Done { summary } =>
728	            run_acceptance_gate; validate_marker; promote_if_ready
729	            set Phase(60)=Completed
730	            return Done
731	
732	    state.turn = turn; save_history(); save_state()
733	
734	# loop exited via max_turns
735	state.failure_reason = Some("max turn budget exhausted")
736	set Phase(40)=Failed; save_state()

1359	Each attach surface runs a budgeted tick loop. The render path is pure: it must not call providers, recurse through provider roots, append narrative snapshots, or reread unbounded JSONL files. Slow or potentially blocking work is either moved into an attach-owned cache/tailer or into a background refresh job whose completion is polled between frames.
1360	
1361	Run attach uses `TuiEventFeed` for run events and `AttachJsonlTail` for `spend.jsonl`, `traces.jsonl`, and `flight-events.jsonl`, so redraws parse only appended complete rows after the first load and ignore partial trailing JSONL until it is complete. Live-file collection uses an attach-specific inventory walker that prunes heavy cache/profile directories before descent and caps displayed rows without losing total counts. Provider activity prefers current flight rows; descriptor-backed provider-log fallback scans are throttled by freshness, matched path, root mtime, and file mtime so a live attach does not recursively scan provider homes every frame.
1362	
1363	`collect_provider_activity` resolves provider ingest through descriptor `[ingest]` metadata: candidate roots, env overrides, cwd matching, storage kind, file glob, freshness window, and schema key. `deadreckon import` reuses the same descriptor metadata for provider transcript discovery and adds import-only session selection, manifest writing, and normalized trace/provenance event creation. `cli:codex` reads `~/.codex/sessions/**.jsonl` and matches `session_meta.payload.cwd`; `cli:claude-code` reads `~/.claude/projects/<cwd-slug>/*.jsonl` using Claude Code's path-to-project mapping and matches top-level `cwd`; `cli:gemini` reads Gemini JSON/JSONL file logs; `cli:opencode` reads OpenCode file-mode `storage/session`, `storage/message`, and `storage/part` JSON; `cli:copilot` reads `~/.copilot/session-state/*.jsonl` plus nested `events.jsonl` and matches `data.context.cwd`; `cli:pi` reads `~/.pi/agent/sessions/<encoded-cwd>/*.jsonl`, validates the first nonblank row is a Pi `session`, and matches the header `cwd`. Schema-specific adapters only decode rows into common activity lines (`agent`, `thinking`, `tool`, `result`, `todo`, `tokens`) and normalize tool labels through `deadreckon_providers::taxonomy`.
1364	
1365	Same-process run attaches can use the `RunEventBus` broadcast channel directly; cross-process run attaches still use durable event replay/tailing. Plan attach consumes `PlanEventBus` / `PlanEventFeed`, which owns `plan-events.jsonl` replay/tailing, emits plan snapshots, tolerates malformed or partial plan-event rows, and multiplexes discovered child and repair run `events.jsonl` streams into the plan activity pane. Chain attach keeps its own `AttachJsonlTail<ChainEvent>` for `chain-events.jsonl`, preserves the existing drill/redo/extend/pause/kill controls, ignores partial last lines until complete, and shows an activity-read hint when chain event catch-up falls behind the tick budget. The production feeds remain durable-file backed for cross-process attach, with broadcast-capable APIs available for same-process streams.

341	## Command Surface
342	
343	Core lifecycle:
344

346	init          create local config
347	config        inspect or edit config keys
348	run           start an unattended coding run
349	attach        open the live dashboard
350	status        latest run and next action for this project
351	list          list runs (current project; --all for every scope)
352	show          inspect state, lineage, spend, files
353	doc           print or export run documentation
354	apply         apply a completed worktree run to your branch
355	abandon       remove a worktree run and temporary branch
356	export        copy a completed artifact to a normal directory
357	extend        continue from a completed run
358	resume        continue an interrupted run
359	kill          stop a live run and child processes
360	undo          restore a previous turn snapshot
361	cleanup       clean abandoned, stale, or completed worktrees
362	finish        choose apply or export from completed run
363	import        normalize histories from other coding tools
364	doctor        check config, providers, sandboxes, disk, runtime
365	```

367	Aliases: `keep` → `apply`, `materialize` → `export`, `discard` → `abandon`, `prune` → `cleanup`, `follow-up` → `extend`, `continue` → `resume`, `stop` → `kill`, `next` → `status`.

- **audit-providers** — providers, sandbox, turn loop, gate
- **audit-cli** — CLI surface, config, telemetry, resume, import
- **audit-tui** — attach TUI, narrative, coherence, plan observability
- **audit-features** — codebase modes, docs, chains, plans, distribution, flight recorder, self-improvement
